c2233802.titulo: Cuts the workweek to 40 hours and guarantees 2 days off per week
c2233802.oQueMuda: The maximum workweek would drop from 44 to 40 hours, up to 8 hours a day, with 2 paid days off (one preferably on Sunday), with no pay cut. The change would be gradual: 2 months after enactment, a maximum of 42 hours, already with 2 days off; 14 months after enactment, 40 hours. Collective agreements could offset hours, and a complementary law could create transition rules for micro-entrepreneurs, micro and small businesses.
c2233802.quemAfeta: Workers with formal employment contracts and their employers. For university graduates earning 2.5 times the social security (INSS) ceiling or more (about R$21,200 a month in 2026), the hours limit and time-clock control would no longer apply, unless the employer decides to keep them or a collective agreement provides for them; the 2 days off would remain guaranteed. This exception does not apply to public-sector employees.
c2233802.porQueImporta: People who work more than 40 hours a week today would work less for the same pay, which the text guarantees. For a worker who now does 44 hours, each hour worked would cost the employer about 10% more (44 ÷ 40); for someone doing 42 hours, about 5%. For those already working 40 hours or less, working hours do not change.
c2233802.nota: Studies disagree on the effect on jobs. Ipea estimates the average cost of formal labor would rise 7.84%, less than 1% of total costs in industry and retail, and says the calculation tends to overstate the impact. A study by Naercio Menezes Filho of the cut from 48 to 44 hours in 1988 found no rise in unemployment. FGV Ibre simulations project job losses in the most pessimistic scenario.

c1228863.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal and civil adulthood to 16 and makes voting mandatory at 16
c1228863.oQueMuda: 16- and 17-year-olds would be tried as adults, gain full civil capacity, be required to vote and be able to run for office earlier.
c1228863.quemAfeta: 16- and 17-year-olds, the justice system and elections.
c1228863.porQueImporta: Today, 16- and 17-year-olds are subject to the Child and Adolescent Statute, with at most 3 years of detention, and voting is optional. Under the PEC, they would be tried and imprisoned as adults and voting would become mandatory.
c1228863.nota: A review of studies done for the CDC, the US government health agency, found that young people transferred to the adult criminal system go on to commit more violence than those kept in the juvenile system, and found no evidence that it reduces violence among other youths. Supporters of lowering the age say it would reduce reoffending, but present no studies showing that effect.

c2140446.titulo: Ends special court privileges for common crimes, except for five officials
c2140446.oQueMuda:
End of special courts for common crimes: deputies, senators, ministers, governors, mayors, judges, prosecutors and other officials would be tried by first-instance judges, like anyone else.
Who keeps it: the President and Vice President of the Republic and the presidents of the Chamber, the Senate and the Supreme Court would still be tried by the Supreme Court.
Impeachable offenses: trials stay in the courts and the Senate, as today.
State constitutions: barred from creating special courts.
One judge: the first criminal case against an official fixes the judge for later cases on the same facts.
c2140446.quemAfeta: Politicians, judges, prosecutors and other officials who today have special court privileges.
c2140446.porQueImporta: Today tens of thousands of officials have special court privileges and are tried by higher courts. Since 2018, under the Supreme Court's interpretation, the privilege for deputies and senators applies only to crimes committed in office and related to it. The text was approved by the Senate in 2017 and by a Chamber special committee in 2018, unchanged, and awaits a floor vote in the Chamber.
c2140446.apelido: End of Special Court Privilege PEC

s8992908.titulo: Creates a national minimum salary for doctors and dentists
s8992908.oQueMuda: Doctors and dentists would be entitled to a national minimum salary, in public bodies and private companies.
s8992908.quemAfeta: Doctors, dentists and those who hire them, such as hospitals, clinics and city governments.
s8992908.porQueImporta: Today there is no national minimum salary for doctors and dentists in the Constitution. Under the PEC, hospitals, clinics, city governments and health plans would have to pay at least the amount set by law.

s7391043.titulo: Lets former workers of Amapá, Roraima and Rondônia join the federal payroll
s7391043.oQueMuda: Unifies criteria for transferring civil servants of the former territories and these states to the federal government.
s7391043.quemAfeta: Current and former civil servants of these states.
s7391043.porQueImporta: Today some of these civil servants are paid by the states. Under the PEC, they would move to a federal roster, and the federal government would take over their salaries and pensions.

c347421.titulo: 2024 spending cuts: wage bonus, pay cap, DRU and Fundeb (enacted)
c347421.oQueMuda:
## For people
Wage bonus (PIS/Pasep): workers earning up to 2 minimum wages were eligible. Now that limit rises only with inflation, no longer with the minimum wage, until it reaches 1.5 minimum wages.
Pay above the cap: allowances and other payments may exceed the public pay cap only if a national law allows it. Until that law exists, the old rules apply.
## For the government and schools
Fundeb: in 2025, up to 10% of the federal money in the fund may go to full-time school places. From 2026, at least 4% of Fundeb must go to this.
DRU: the government may freely use 30% of some revenues reserved for specific areas until 2032, except what goes to states and municipalities.
Subsidies and tax incentives: the government may cut subsidies to meet fiscal targets, and a complementary law is to set limits for granting tax incentives.
c347421.quemAfeta: People who receive the wage bonus; people paid above the public pay cap; public schools; the federal budget.
c347421.nota: As of June 2026, the law on the pay cap had not been passed. So the Supreme Court (STF) set temporary rules for judges and prosecutors: extra payments are limited to 35% of the monthly salary, with exceptions.

c2500080.titulo: Reorganizes public security: national system, funds, municipal police and tougher penalties
c2500080.oQueMuda:
## Organization
Susp in the Constitution: the Unified Public Security System, which integrates the police forces and today exists only in law, is written into the Constitution.
Funds: the national security and prison funds enter the Constitution, and the federal government must transfer 50% of each to the states, with no agreement required.
Municipal police: municipalities with enough own revenue may create municipal police forces for patrol and community policing, overseen by prosecutors.
Federal Police: the Constitution gives it the fight against gangs and militias operating in more than one state or abroad.
## Penalties and rights
Gangs and violent crimes: the law must provide for maximum-security prisons, limits on sentence progression, pretrial release and temporary leave, and confiscation of assets without compensation.
Pretrial detainees: people held without a conviction would have their political rights suspended, including the right to vote, while detained.
## Powers
CNJ and CNMP: Congress could overturn acts of the national councils of justice and of prosecutors on security and criminal law.
c2500080.quemAfeta: Governments at all levels, police forces, municipal guards, prisoners and crime victims.
c2500080.porQueImporta: Today public security is mainly a state responsibility, the system that integrates the police exists only in law, and pretrial detainees can vote.

s9104654.titulo: Changes how Supreme Court justices are chosen
s9104654.oQueMuda: Creates new requirements for appointing Supreme Court justices and bars them from running for office for five years after leaving.
s9104654.quemAfeta: Current and future Supreme Court justices.
s9104654.porQueImporta: Today the president nominates Supreme Court justices aged 35 to 70 with notable legal knowledge and spotless reputation, and they can run for office after leaving. Under the PEC, there would be new requirements and a five-year ban on running for office.

c2551011.titulo: Requires full sentences in closed prison for heinous crimes
c2551011.oQueMuda: People convicted of torture, drug trafficking, terrorism and heinous crimes would serve their whole sentence in closed prison.
c2551011.quemAfeta: People convicted of these crimes and the prison system.
c2551011.porQueImporta: Today people convicted of heinous crimes can move to a semi-open regime after serving 40% to 70% of the sentence, depending on the case. Under the PEC, they would serve the whole sentence in closed prison.

c621521.titulo: Allows a single unified police force in each state
c621521.oQueMuda: Federal and state governments could merge police forces into one that handles everything from patrols to investigation.
c621521.quemAfeta: Military police, civil police, firefighters and the people they serve.
c621521.porQueImporta: Today each state has a Military Police, which patrols, and a Civil Police, which investigates. Under the PEC, governments could merge them into a single police force.

c2166443.titulo: Creates the National Public Safety Development Fund
c2166443.oQueMuda: Adds to the Constitution a fund with money set aside for public safety.
c2166443.quemAfeta: State governments, police forces and the public.
c2166443.porQueImporta: Today the National Public Security Fund exists by law, and its money can change every year. Under the PEC, the fund and its funding source would be in the Constitution.

c2644800.titulo: Confirms rural property titles in border areas
c2644800.oQueMuda: Validates rural land titles near the borders that states granted before 1988.
c2644800.porQueImporta: Today land titles in the border strip granted by states without federal approval before 1988 can be annulled. Under the PEC, these records would be confirmed, and holders would become definitive owners.

c354302.titulo: Grants autonomy to government attorney offices
c354302.oQueMuda:
Autonomy: the Attorney General's Office and state, Federal District and municipal attorneys' offices would have administrative, budgetary and technical autonomy, and would propose their own budgets.
Guaranteed funding: their budgets would be transferred in monthly installments by the 20th, as already happens with the Judiciary, the Legislature, prosecutors and public defenders.
Independence: government lawyers would be inviolable in the exercise of their duties and act independently.
c354302.quemAfeta: Government lawyers and attorneys, and the governments they represent.
c354302.porQueImporta: Today the Attorney General's Office and attorneys' offices are part of the Executive, their heads are chosen by the government and their budgets are set by it. The text has been ready for a Chamber floor vote since 2014.

c2432987.titulo: Gives budget autonomy to the AGU and state attorneys' offices
c2432987.oQueMuda: The Federal Attorney General's Office and state attorneys' offices would control their own budgets.
c2432987.quemAfeta: Government lawyers and the federal and state governments.
c2432987.porQueImporta: Today the budget of the AGU and attorney offices is set by the government. Under the PEC, they would propose their own budget, within the limits of the budget guidelines law, like the judiciary and prosecutors.

c2442880.titulo: Changes retirement rules for police and security officers
c2442880.oQueMuda: Changes special retirement criteria from the 2019 pension reform and creates specific rules for public safety.
c2442880.quemAfeta: Police officers and other public safety workers.
c2442880.porQueImporta: Since the 2019 reform, federal police and other officers retire at 55 with a minimum time in service. Under the PEC, the rules would be changed in favor of these workers, increasing pension spending.

c483905.titulo: Allows judges and prosecutors to be dismissed as punishment
c483905.oQueMuda: Ends forced retirement as a penalty and allows loss of office in serious cases.
c483905.porQueImporta: Today the maximum administrative penalty for judges and prosecutors is compulsory retirement, with pay proportional to time served. Under the PEC, they could lose their post and pay.

c372537.titulo: Sets aside budget money for sports
c372537.oQueMuda: Creates a mandatory allocation of funds for sports in the Constitution.
c372537.porQueImporta: Today there is no mandatory minimum for sport in the budget. Under the PEC, a fixed share of revenue would have to go to it.

c586407.titulo: Changes disciplinary rules for judges and prosecutors
c586407.oQueMuda: Regulates the disciplinary system for the judiciary and prosecutors.
c586407.porQueImporta: Today punishments for judges and prosecutors follow the 1979 Judiciary Organic Law and prosecutors' laws. Under the PEC, the Constitution would define the disciplinary regime for these careers.

c520886.titulo: Bans retirement as a punishment for judges
c520886.oQueMuda: Judges punished for misconduct could no longer be forced into retirement with proportional pay.
c520886.porQueImporta: Today judges punished for serious misconduct can be compulsorily retired, receiving pay proportional to time served. Under the PEC, this form of punishment would no longer exist.

c2158594.titulo: Allows the National Council of Justice to dismiss judges
c2158594.oQueMuda: The National Council of Justice (CNJ) could order a judge's removal from office.
c2158594.porQueImporta: Today a judge only loses office through a final court ruling. Under the PEC, the CNJ, an administrative body, could also order removal from office.

c328385.titulo: Phases out retired civil servants' pension contribution from age 61
c328385.oQueMuda: The text ready for a vote, approved by the special committee in 2010, cuts the pension contribution of retired civil servants and survivors by 20% each year from age 61, reaching zero at 65. People with permanent disability stop paying.
c328385.quemAfeta: Retired civil servants and survivors, and federal, state and municipal pension systems.
c328385.porQueImporta: Since 2004, retired civil servants and survivors pay a pension contribution on the amount above the INSS ceiling; since the 2019 reform, when there is a deficit, it can also be charged on amounts above one minimum wage. Under the PEC, people 65 and over would stop paying.
c328385.nota: A technical note estimated that ending the whole contribution of retirees and survivors would cost up to R$ 25 billion a year to the federal, state and municipal governments (2023 values). The committee text, which only reaches zero at 65, would cost much less. The 2019 pension reform changed the article the PEC amends, so the text would need to be adapted.

c2419252.titulo: Changes contribution and retirement rules for civil servants
c2419252.oQueMuda: Changes parts of the 2019 pension reform on extra contributions and rules for civil servants.
c2419252.porQueImporta: The 2019 reform allowed extra contributions from civil servants when public pension systems run a deficit. Under the PEC, these rules would change, altering how much civil servants pay.

c2623400.titulo: Allows lowering the age of criminal responsibility for heinous crimes
c2623400.oQueMuda: In exceptional cases, such as heinous or extremely cruel crimes, teenagers could be tried as adults.
c2623400.porQueImporta: Today people under 18 are subject to the Child and Adolescent Statute, with at most 3 years of detention. Under the PEC, teenagers who commit heinous or extremely cruel crimes could be tried and imprisoned as adults.

c2623604.titulo: Lowers the minimum age of criminal responsibility
c2623604.oQueMuda: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility under the conditions in the proposal.
c2623604.porQueImporta: Today people under 18 are subject to the Child and Adolescent Statute, with at most 3 years of detention. Under the PEC, teenagers below that age could be tried and imprisoned as adults.

s8325260.titulo: Allows municipal police and adds traffic agents to public security
s8325260.oQueMuda: Municipalities could have municipal guards or police doing visible local patrols, and traffic agents would become part of public security.
s8325260.quemAfeta: Municipal guards, traffic agents and city governments.
s8325260.porQueImporta: Today municipal guards protect city property, services and facilities, and patrolling belongs to the Military Police. Under the PEC, city governments could have municipal police doing patrols, paid with city money.

s7753208.titulo: Creates forensic police forces in the states
s7753208.oQueMuda: Criminal forensics would become its own public safety body, reporting to the governor.
s7753208.quemAfeta: Forensic experts and state police forces.
s7753208.porQueImporta: Today, in most states, forensic services are part of the Civil Police. Under the PEC, they would be a separate body reporting directly to the governor.

c2504516.titulo: Removes the time limit to prosecute sexual crimes against children
c2504516.oQueMuda: Sexual crimes against children under 12 could be punished at any time, with no statute of limitations.
c2504516.quemAfeta: Victims of child sexual abuse and those accused of these crimes.
c2504516.porQueImporta: Today the time limit for punishing sexual crimes against children starts when the victim turns 18 and can reach 20 years after that. Under the PEC, there would be no time limit.

c2576168.titulo: Administrative reform: performance bonuses, longer careers and an end to seniority-based benefits
c2576168.oQueMuda:
## Pay and careers
Performance bonus: civil servants could receive a bonus of up to 2 monthly salaries a year, and up to 4 for managers, tied to targets; this bonus would sit outside the public pay cap.
Careers: starting pay could not exceed 50% of the career's top pay (except careers paying up to 4 minimum wages), with at least 20 levels and at least 1 year between each.
End of seniority perks: allowances and promotions based only on length of service and premium leave end; pay rises with retroactive effect are banned.
Vacation: up to 30 days a year (except teachers and some health workers), with a bonus of up to 1/3.
## Evaluation and judiciary
Probation: objective evaluation with targets; a servant deemed unfit is dismissed.
Judges: compulsory retirement is no longer a penalty; for serious misconduct, the penalty becomes loss of office.
c2576168.quemAfeta: Civil servants at all levels, judges and users of public services.
c2576168.porQueImporta: Today many careers have automatic allowances and promotions based on length of service, and judges punished for serious misconduct can be compulsorily retired with pay proportional to their years of service.
c2576168.nota: Civil servant groups say the PEC weakens job stability. The text keeps stability after probation but requires an objective evaluation to confirm it. The bonus outside the pay cap is a new exception to the public salary limit.

c2604173.titulo: Caps the vehicle tax (IPVA) and limits ad and legislative spending
c2604173.oQueMuda: Sets a ceiling for the IPVA rate and limits spending on government advertising and the legislature.
c2604173.porQueImporta: Today each state sets the IPVA rate, and half the amount goes to city governments. Under the PEC, there would be a national cap on the rate and limits on spending on official advertising and on the legislature.

c2631190.titulo: Allows culture and sports incentive programs under the new tax
c2631190.oQueMuda: The IBS Management Committee could allow states and municipalities to create, by their own law, programs in which donations and sponsorships for cultural and sports projects generate IBS credits, with uniform national rules and limits for each government. The value of the credits would be deducted from the revenue of the state or municipality that created the program.
c2631190.quemAfeta: Sponsoring companies, artists, sports organizations, states and municipalities.
c2631190.porQueImporta: With the tax reform, ICMS and ISS will be replaced by IBS by 2033, ending local culture and sports incentive programs based on those taxes. Under the PEC, states and municipalities could create similar programs using IBS credits.

c2633488.titulo: Exempts nonprofit sports organizations from taxes
c2633488.oQueMuda: Nonprofit clubs and sports organizations would stop paying certain taxes.
c2633488.porQueImporta: Today non-profit sports organizations pay taxes on assets and income, except for legal exemptions. Under the PEC, they would have constitutional immunity, as parties, unions and social assistance bodies already do.

c2136725.titulo: Makes rape a crime without bail or time limit
c2136725.oQueMuda: Rape would no longer allow bail and could be punished at any time.
c2136725.quemAfeta: Rape victims and those accused of the crime.
c2136725.porQueImporta: Today rape is already non-bailable, as a heinous crime, but the time limit for prosecution is up to 20 years, depending on the sentence. Under the PEC, there would be no time limit.

c2234666.titulo: Changes how the Municipal Participation Fund is shared
c2234666.oQueMuda: Changes the rules for federal transfers to cities through the FPM.
c2234666.quemAfeta: City governments, especially those that depend on these transfers.
c2234666.porQueImporta: Today FPM is split among city governments based on population and income per person. Under the PEC, the criteria would change, altering how much each town receives.

c2091473.titulo: Lets associations of municipalities challenge laws at the Supreme Court
c2091473.oQueMuda: National associations of cities could file Supreme Court cases to challenge or defend laws.
c2091473.quemAfeta: City governments and their national associations.
c2091473.porQueImporta: Today only officials and bodies listed in the Constitution, such as the president, governors, parties and union confederations, can ask the Supreme Court to strike down a law. Under the PEC, national associations of municipalities could too.

c2284555.titulo: Guarantees special retirement for community health workers
c2284555.oQueMuda:
Special retirement: community health agents and disease-control agents could retire at 57 (women) and 60 (men), with 25 years of contributions and work; transition rules allow lower ages for those already in the job.
Full pay: in some cases, the pension would equal the last salary and get the same raises as active workers.
Employment: agents get a direct link to the municipality or state; temporary or outsourced hiring is banned except in public health emergencies.
Who pays: the federal government would help states and municipalities cover the extra cost and pay an extra benefit to those retiring under INSS.
Indigenous agents: the rules also apply to Indigenous health and sanitation agents.
c2284555.quemAfeta: Community health and disease-control agents, municipalities, municipal pension systems and the federal government.
c2284555.porQueImporta: Today these agents follow the general retirement rules. The PEC was approved by the Chamber in October 2025 and by the Senate in July 2026, 73 votes to 1, and awaits enactment.
c2284555.nota: The Social Security Ministry estimates the cost at about R$ 29 billion over ten years. The National Confederation of Municipalities estimates R$ 69.9 billion for municipal pension systems and says the PEC interferes with municipal autonomy.

c412505.titulo: Creates the National Technical Education Fund
c412505.oQueMuda: Sets aside tax money to fund technical education.
c412505.porQueImporta: Today technical education is paid from general education funds. Under the PEC, there would be a fund with a share of taxes reserved for it.

c527081.titulo: Directs tax money to the Uruguay River region
c527081.oQueMuda: Sets aside part of income tax and IPI for a development fund for the Uruguay River basin.
c527081.quemAfeta: Cities and residents of the Uruguay River basin, in the South.
c527081.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, part of income tax and IPI would have to go to a fund for the Uruguay River basin in the South; that share would no longer stay with the federal government.

c1701023.titulo: Creates a fund for the Uruguay River region
c1701023.oQueMuda: Creates the Uruguay River Basin Development Fund with federal money.
c1701023.quemAfeta: Cities and residents of the Uruguay River basin.
c1701023.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, part of federal taxes would have to go to a fund for the Uruguay River basin in the South; that share would no longer stay with the federal government.

s7864739.oQueMuda: The federal government would legislate on cyber defense, and all governments would protect the digital security of public services.
s7864739.quemAfeta: Governments and users of digital public services.
s7864739.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution does not mention cybersecurity. Under the PEC, only the federal government would make cyber-defense laws, and all governments would have to protect their systems.

c796797.titulo: Creates a fund for technical high school education
c796797.oQueMuda: Creates Fundetec, a fund to finance technical education at the high school level.
c796797.porQueImporta: Today secondary technical education is paid from general education funds. Under the PEC, it would have its own fund.

c1672354.titulo: Creates the Racial Equality Promotion Fund
c1672354.oQueMuda: Creates a federally funded fund for racial equality policies.
c1672354.quemAfeta: Black Brazilians and public anti-racism policies.
c1672354.porQueImporta: Today racial equality policies depend on each year's budget. Under the PEC, they would have a fund with reserved federal money.

c1713489.titulo: Creates a national fund for racial equality and reparations
c1713489.oQueMuda: Creates a fund to promote racial equality, fight racism and repair harm.
c1713489.quemAfeta: Black Brazilians and public anti-racism policies.
c1713489.porQueImporta: Today racial equality policies depend on each year's budget. Under the PEC, they would have their own fund, including for reparation.

c2557024.titulo: Changes how recycling is taxed under the tax reform
c2557024.oQueMuda: Creates specific tax treatment for the recycling sector in the new tax system.
c2557024.quemAfeta: Waste pickers, cooperatives and recycling companies.
c2557024.porQueImporta: In the tax reform approved in 2023, recycling has no special regime. Under the PEC, recycled materials would get special treatment under IBS and CBS, paying less tax.

c2458742.titulo: Makes early childhood a priority in the Constitution
c2458742.oQueMuda: Young children would have rights and guarantees explicitly named in the Constitution.
c2458742.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution protects children in general, and early childhood is covered by a 2016 law. Under the PEC, early childhood (up to age 6) would have rights listed in the Constitution.

s8986903.titulo: Changes employers' social security contributions from 2027
s8986903.oQueMuda: Changes how employers' social security contributions apply to payroll and revenue, with a maximum rate.
s8986903.quemAfeta: Companies, workers and the social security system.
s8986903.porQueImporta: Today companies generally pay 20% of payroll to social security, and some sectors pay on revenue instead. Under the PEC, the way it is charged would change from 2027, with a defined maximum rate.

s8639911.titulo: Allows leasing of Indigenous lands and free sale of their production
s8639911.oQueMuda:
Activities: Indigenous people and communities could carry out any forestry and farming activities and sell their production.
Contracts and leasing: they could sign contracts, including leases and partnerships with third parties, and would decide on their own how to split the proceeds.
Support: the federal government would have to provide technical support and incentives for Indigenous commercial activities.
s8639911.quemAfeta: Indigenous peoples, farmers interested in leasing land and the federal government.
s8639911.porQueImporta: Today Indigenous lands belong to the federal government, with permanent possession and exclusive use by Indigenous peoples, and leasing to third parties is banned by law. Under the PEC, these lands could be leased for third-party production.
s8639911.nota: At the Senate Justice Committee public hearing in December 2025, the idea of allowing leasing was rejected by all participants, including Indigenous representatives and Cimi, who say it contradicts the constitutional right to exclusive use of the lands. Views were split on the part allowing sale of production and contracts.

s8828166.titulo: Creates a national policy to support truck drivers
s8828166.oQueMuda: It sets up a national policy for professional drivers, including rest stops at regular intervals along highways.
s8828166.porQueImporta: Today the truck drivers' law requires breaks, but highways lack rest stops. Under the PEC, governments would be required to provide rest areas at regular intervals on highways.

s9065675.titulo: Keeps local culture and sports incentives under the new tax
s9065675.oQueMuda: Preserves, under the IBS, state and city programs that give tax breaks to supporters of culture and sports.
s9065675.quemAfeta: Artists, sports organizations, sponsors and local governments.
s9065675.porQueImporta: With the tax reform, ICMS and ISS will be replaced by IBS by 2033, which would end local tax-discount programs for supporters of culture and sport. Under the PEC, these programs would be kept under IBS.

c2341717.titulo: Makes Audit Courts permanent and bans creating or abolishing them
c2341717.oQueMuda: Audit courts become permanent institutions essential to external oversight. Abolishing, creating or setting up state and municipal audit courts is prohibited.
c2341717.quemAfeta: Audit courts, their members and staff, and the governments and councils they oversee.
c2341717.porQueImporta: In force since May 2026 (Amendment 139). Before, states could abolish audit courts by amending their state constitutions, as Ceará did with its municipal audit court in 2017; that is no longer possible, and no new ones can be created.

c2436224.titulo: Promotes federal nursing assistants to nursing technicians
c2436224.oQueMuda: Federal employees working as nursing assistants would move to the nursing technician career.
c2436224.quemAfeta: Nursing assistants in the federal civil service.
c2436224.porQueImporta: Today nursing assistants and technicians are different posts with different salaries, and changing posts requires a public exam. Under the PEC, federal assistants would become technicians without a new exam.

c2485767.titulo: Sets guidelines for careers and minimum pay of public health workers
c2485767.oQueMuda: Defines general rules for career plans and national minimum salaries for health workers in the public system (SUS).
c2485767.quemAfeta: Public health workers and the governments that hire them.
c2485767.porQueImporta: Today each government sets the career and salary of the public health workers it hires, except existing floors such as nursing. Under the PEC, there would be national rules and pay floors for more public health professions.

s8593552.titulo: Gives the Central Bank financial autonomy and changes its legal status
s8593552.oQueMuda:
Nature: the Central Bank becomes a special public entity, with technical, administrative, budgetary and financial autonomy, not tied to any ministry.
Own budget: the Central Bank would approve its own budget, paid from its revenues, outside the federal budget; payroll and running costs would go through the National Monetary Council and a Senate committee.
Staff: the Central Bank would set its staff's salaries and careers; payroll could grow up to inflation plus 2.5% a year, unless the Senate authorizes more.
Public accounts: result transfers between the Central Bank and the Treasury would be outside fiscal targets.
s8593552.quemAfeta: The Central Bank, its staff, the Treasury and the financial system.
s8593552.porQueImporta: Since 2021 the Central Bank has had autonomy to set interest rates, but it is a federal agency and its budget is part of the federal budget approved by Congress. Under the PEC, its budget would leave the federal budget.
s8593552.nota: The Attorney General's Office considers the PEC unconstitutional because changes to the Executive's structure would require the president's initiative. The Central Bank staff association supports it and says it keeps the bank under public law.

c2351506.titulo: Churches and temples would stop paying taxes on purchases
c2351506.oQueMuda: Today the Constitution bars taxes on temples of any faith. The PEC says this ban covers purchases of goods and services needed to set up, maintain and run religious entities and temples, as well as daycare centers, therapeutic communities, monasteries, seminaries, convents, shelter services, social-assistance activities and other non-profit activities. Everything must relate to the entity's essential purposes, and a complementary law will set the conditions.
c2351506.quemAfeta: Churches and temples of any faith and the non-profit activities linked to them, such as daycare centers, therapeutic communities and seminaries.
c2351506.porQueImporta: Today temples pay no taxes on property, income and services tied to their purposes, but they pay the taxes built into the price of what they buy. Under the PEC, they would also stop paying them on purchases needed to operate.
c2351506.nota: The expansion falls within the temples' tax immunity. Press coverage describes the daycare centers and other entities as those linked to churches and religious denominations, not all of them in the country.

s9038492.titulo: Creates a special tax regime for soccer clubs and sports
s9038492.oQueMuda: Clubs, football associations and non-profit sports organizations would join the same specific IBS regime as hotels, bars, restaurants, parks and travel agencies, which allows rates, tax bases and credits different from the general rule.
s9038492.quemAfeta: Clubs and sports organizations, and other taxpayers, since each specific regime can affect the general rate.
s9038492.porQueImporta: In the tax reform, football corporations (SAFs) got this regime, but clubs organized as non-profit associations were left out. Under the PEC, they could also get specific taxation.

s9055580.titulo: Lets workers choose a flexible hourly schedule
s9055580.oQueMuda: Employees could choose between the standard CLT work schedule and a flexible arrangement paid by the hour.
s9055580.porQueImporta: Today the labor code limits the workweek to 44 hours with a monthly salary. Under the PEC, workers could choose a regime paid only for hours worked, without fixed hours.

c2485341.titulo: Cuts the workweek to 36 hours over 4 days
c2485341.oQueMuda: The maximum workweek would be 36 hours, up to 8 hours a day, over 4 days a week; the rule would take effect 360 days after approval.
c2485341.quemAfeta: Workers with formal employment contracts and employers.
c2485341.porQueImporta: People who work more than 36 hours or more than four days a week today would work less for the same pay. For those going from 44 to 36 hours, the employer's wage cost per hour worked rises about 22%.
c2485341.apelido: End of the 6x1 schedule amendment (4-day week)

s8548483.titulo: Sets a time limit ('marco temporal') for recognizing Indigenous lands
s8548483.oQueMuda:
Time frame: only lands occupied by Indigenous peoples on October 5, 1988 would count as Indigenous lands, and already demarcated lands could not be expanded.
Non-Indigenous occupants: where there was no Indigenous occupation in 1988 and no proven ongoing land conflict since then, private titles and good-faith possession are valid.
Compensation: if the federal government expropriates the area, it pays the owner the market value of the land and improvements, when it cannot give the Indigenous community another equivalent area.
Demarcation: owners, occupants and governments take part in the process from the moment demarcation is requested.
s8548483.quemAfeta: Indigenous peoples, farmers and residents of disputed areas, and the federal government, which would pay compensation.
s8548483.porQueImporta: In 2023 the Supreme Court ruled that the 1988 date cannot be used to deny demarcations; that same year a law restored the rule, and the issue returned to the Court. Under the PEC, the time frame would be in the Constitution.
s8548483.nota: The Supreme Court ruled the time-frame thesis unconstitutional in 2023 and reaffirmed it in December 2025, one day after the Senate approved this PEC. Supporters say it gives legal certainty to good-faith occupants; critics point out that many peoples were expelled from their lands before 1988.

s8938455.titulo: Makes productive efficiency a permanent goal of the State
s8938455.oQueMuda: States that the State must foster productivity and long-term growth, through competition, economic openness and investment in education, science and innovation. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8938455.quemAfeta: Governments, companies and those who make economic laws.
s8938455.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution lists economic principles such as free competition and consumer protection, but no productivity goal. Under the PEC, fostering productive efficiency would become a permanent goal of the State.

s9050555.titulo: Creates a code of conduct for public officials
s9050555.oQueMuda: Adds to the Constitution rules of conduct, duties and prohibitions for public officials, focused on avoiding conflicts of interest.
s9050555.quemAfeta: Civil servants, politicians and other public officials.
s9050555.porQueImporta: Today conduct rules for public officials are in laws and each body's ethics code. Under the PEC, duties and prohibitions would be in the Constitution, applying to all levels of government.

c2361500.titulo: Recognizes court bailiffs as a state career
c2361500.oQueMuda: Court bailiffs would get their own section in the Constitution and different retirement rules.
c2361500.porQueImporta: Today court bailiffs are judiciary staff under general retirement rules. Under the PEC, they would have their own section in the Constitution and special retirement rules.

c2340881.titulo: Adds notary representatives to the National Council of Justice (CNJ)
c2340881.oQueMuda: The National Council of Justice would gain two members: a notary and a registrar.
c2340881.quemAfeta: Notary offices and the National Council of Justice.
c2340881.porQueImporta: Today the CNJ has 15 members, including judges, prosecutors, lawyers and citizens, and oversees notary offices. Under the PEC, it would gain two members from the notary offices themselves.

c257418.titulo: Allows Congress to summon heads of state-owned companies
c257418.oQueMuda: The Chamber, the Senate and committees could require heads of companies with federal stakes to give information in person.
c257418.quemAfeta: Presidents and directors of state-owned companies, such as Petrobras and public banks.
c257418.porQueImporta: Today Congress can summon ministers but not heads of state companies. Under the PEC, heads of companies such as Petrobras and public banks could be required to appear.

s9047816.titulo: Creates a national minimum salary for military police and firefighters
s9047816.oQueMuda: Military police officers and military firefighters would have a national minimum salary set by federal law.
s9047816.quemAfeta: Military police, firefighters and the state governments that pay them.
s9047816.porQueImporta: Today each state sets the pay of its military police and firefighters. Under the PEC, there would be a national floor set by federal law, paid by the states.

s7733780.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility to 16, and 14 for serious crimes
s7733780.oQueMuda: Young people from 16 would be tried as adults; for heinous crimes, drug trafficking and terrorism, from 14.
s7733780.quemAfeta: Teenagers and the justice and prison systems.
s7733780.porQueImporta: Today people under 18 are subject to the Child and Adolescent Statute, with at most 3 years of detention. Under the PEC, those aged 16, or 14 for serious crimes, would be tried and imprisoned as adults.

s8318028.titulo: Adds municipal guards to public safety
s8318028.oQueMuda: Municipal guards would officially become part of the public safety bodies.
s8318028.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution allows municipal guards to protect city property and services, outside the list of public security bodies. Under the PEC, they would be added to that list.

c2362526.titulo: Creates a Unified Mobility System and free fares on urban public transport
c2362526.oQueMuda:
Free fares: urban public transport would become free for users; a law would set the deadlines.
Unified system: transport becomes a right organized in a unified mobility system, with an integrated network and public participation, like SUS in health.
Who pays: federal, state and municipal governments would allocate part of their taxes to the system, and two contributions could be created: one paid by vehicle owners, charged by municipalities, and another paid by employers, charged by the federal government in cities with free fares.
Deadline: Congress would have 2 years to pass the laws on the system and the contributions.
c2362526.quemAfeta: Bus and subway riders, vehicle owners, employers and municipalities.
c2362526.porQueImporta: Since 2015 transport has been a social right in the Constitution, but public transport is largely paid for by fares, and the transport voucher is funded by workers and companies. Under the PEC, users would stop paying, and the cost would shift to taxes and the new contributions.
c2362526.nota: A 2019 Inesc study estimated that free, universal public transport would cost about R$ 70.8 billion a year, close to 1% of GDP. Supporters say the new contribution would cost employers less than the current transport voucher.

c14666.titulo: Expands who Congress can summon to testify
c14666.oQueMuda: Ministers, heads of agencies, regulators and state-owned companies could be summoned by Congress.
c14666.porQueImporta: Today Congress can summon ministers and officials linked to the Presidency. Under the PEC, it could also summon heads of regulatory agencies, public bodies and state companies.

c2162116.titulo: Guarantees minimum funding for social assistance (SUAS)
c2162116.oQueMuda:
Floor for social assistance: the federal government would have to spend at least 1% of its net current revenue on social assistance every year. States, the Federal District and municipalities, another 1% of their own revenue, on top of what they receive from the federal government.
Transition: 0.3% in the 1st year after enactment, 0.5% in the 2nd and 0.75% in the 3rd. The 1% applies from the 4th year.
What counts: only social-protection services defined in the social assistance law. BPC, Bolsa Família, other cash-transfer programs and one-off benefits do not count.
c2162116.quemAfeta: People served by social assistance services; federal, state, Federal District and municipal governments.
c2162116.porQueImporta: Today health and education have mandatory minimum spending in the Constitution, and social assistance does not. Under the PEC, it would: 1% of each government's revenue, reached in four years.

s9017996.titulo: Requires suspects and witnesses to appear before inquiry committees
s9017996.oQueMuda: People under investigation and witnesses summoned by parliamentary inquiry committees would have to appear, under penalty of being brought in by force and fined. They would keep the right to remain silent on self-incriminating questions, but silence would not excuse them from appearing.
s9017996.quemAfeta: People summoned by parliamentary inquiry committees.
s9017996.porQueImporta: Today Supreme Court rulings on the issue diverge: some let people under investigation skip inquiry hearings, others require attendance with the right to silence. Under the PEC, attendance would always be mandatory.

c2121543.oQueMuda: The Constitution's social rights (education, health, food, work, housing, transport, leisure, security, social security, protection of motherhood and childhood, and assistance to the destitute) would become entrenched clauses, and no amendment could tend to abolish them.
c2121543.porQueImporta: Today entrenched clauses, which cannot be abolished by amendment, include individual rights, the vote and separation of powers. Under the PEC, social rights such as health, education and work would be added.

c546158.titulo: Lets police officers also work as teachers or health workers
c546158.oQueMuda: Police officers could hold a second public job as a teacher or health worker; police and guard posts would count as technical jobs.
c546158.porQueImporta: Today civil servants can only hold two public posts in listed cases, such as two teaching posts or one teaching and one technical. Under the PEC, police officers could hold a second post as teacher or health worker.

c463451.titulo: Creates a national minimum for military police and firefighters equal to the Federal District's
c463451.oQueMuda:
Minimum pay: military police and firefighters in every state could not earn less than those in the Federal District, a rule that would also apply to retirees and survivors.
Amounts: the initial minimum would be based on R$ 4,500 for the lowest rank and R$ 9,000 for the lowest officer rank, in December 2009 values, to be updated.
Who pays: the federal government would help states through a dedicated fund, set by law.
Deadline: measures would have to be adopted within 180 days.
c463451.quemAfeta: Military police and firefighters (active, retired and survivors) and state and federal governments.
c463451.porQueImporta: Today each state sets its military police and firefighters' pay, and those in the Federal District, paid by the federal government, are among the highest. The text, known as PEC 300, was approved by a special committee in 2009 and has been ready for a vote since.

c414367.titulo: Matches state military police pay to the Federal District's
c414367.oQueMuda: State military police and firefighters, including retirees, could not earn less than those in the Federal District.
c414367.quemAfeta: Military police, firefighters and state governments.
c414367.porQueImporta: Today each state sets the pay of its military police and firefighters, and those in the Federal District, paid by the federal government, are among the highest. Under the PEC, no state could pay less than the Federal District, including to retirees.

c2323056.titulo: Adds the solidarity economy to the principles of the economy
c2323056.oQueMuda: Adds 'solidarity economy' (cooperatives and collective work groups) to the list of principles guiding the country's economy. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2323056.quemAfeta: Cooperatives, associations and those who make economic laws and policies.
c2323056.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution tells the law to support cooperatives but does not mention the solidarity economy. Under the PEC, it would be added to the principles of the economic order.

s8082738.titulo: Makes Brazilian Sign Language (Libras) an official language
s8082738.oQueMuda: Brazilian Sign Language would become an official language alongside Portuguese.
s8082738.porQueImporta: Since 2002 Libras has been recognized by law as a means of communication, but the Constitution's only official language is Portuguese. Under the PEC, Libras would also be an official language.

s8440723.titulo: Sets minimum values for the nursing minimum wage
s8440723.oQueMuda: Sets minimum amounts for the national minimum salaries of nurses, technicians, nursing assistants and midwives.
s8440723.quemAfeta: Nursing professionals and those who hire them.
s8440723.porQueImporta: Since 2022 there has been a national nursing minimum wage set by law. In April 2026, the Senate Justice Committee recommended rejecting this PEC and approved instead PEC 19/2024, which ties the minimum wage to a 36-hour week.

s8600341.titulo: Shields media outlets from liability for what interviewees say
s8600341.oQueMuda: Newspapers, broadcasters and news sites would not be liable in civil court when an interviewee accuses someone of a crime; only the interviewee could be sued for damages.
s8600341.quemAfeta: Newspapers, broadcasters, journalists and people accused in interviews.
s8600341.porQueImporta: Today, under the thesis set by the Supreme Court in November 2023, an outlet is liable for an interviewee's statement only if there were concrete signs the accusation was false and it failed to check and to report those signs. Under the PEC, the outlet would never be liable.

s8622662.titulo: Bans retirement as a punishment for public officials
s8622662.oQueMuda: Judges, prosecutors and military personnel punished for misconduct could no longer be retired as a sanction.
s8622662.porQueImporta: Today judges, prosecutors and military officers punished for serious misconduct can be retired with proportional pay. Under the PEC, this form of punishment would no longer exist.

s8640436.titulo: Requires 24-hour Public Defender service for health and domestic violence
s8640436.oQueMuda: Public Defender's Offices would offer uninterrupted service, prioritizing health matters and domestic violence.
s8640436.quemAfeta: People who need the courts to obtain treatment and domestic violence victims.
s8640436.porQueImporta: Today each Public Defender's Office sets its own hours. Under the PEC, all would have 24-hour service, prioritizing health and domestic violence.

s8664568.titulo: Ties the nursing minimum wage to a 36-hour week and guarantees inflation adjustments
s8664568.oQueMuda:
Hours: the nursing minimum wage would apply to a maximum 36-hour week, in public and private hospitals (the original proposal said 30 hours; the Senate Justice Committee changed it to 36, with the agreement of the profession's organizations).
Adjustment: the minimum wage would have to be raised every year, at least by the previous 12 months' inflation.
s8664568.quemAfeta: Nurses, nursing technicians and assistants, midwives, and public and private hospitals.
s8664568.porQueImporta: Today the nursing minimum wage applies to a week of up to 44 hours. Under the PEC, the same amount would be paid for at most 36 hours, raising the hourly value by about 22% for those working 44 hours (44 ÷ 36).

c2231327.titulo: Extends the pension reform to states and cities
c2231327.oQueMuda: States and cities could adopt federal pension rules; it also creates a benefit for children in poverty.
c2231327.quemAfeta: State and city civil servants, and poor children.
c2231327.porQueImporta: The 2019 pension reform applied only to federal civil servants and INSS. Under the PEC, states and municipalities could adopt the same rules for their staff, and a benefit for poor children would be created.

c439075.titulo: Unifies elections, ends reelection and changes term lengths
c439075.oQueMuda: All elections would happen together, terms would be 5 years (10 for senators) and executives could not be reelected.
c439075.porQueImporta: Today there are elections every two years, 4-year terms (8 for senators) and one re-election allowed. Under the PEC, all elections would be held in the same year every 5 years, without re-election for president, governor and mayor.

c608998.titulo: Adds lawyers to small claims courts
c608998.oQueMuda: Lawyers would sit on small claims courts and their appeal panels.
c608998.quemAfeta: Lawyers and people who use small claims courts.
c608998.porQueImporta: Today small claims courts are staffed by career judges. Under the PEC, lawyers would also sit on them.

c2214856.titulo: Expands who can move human rights cases to federal courts
c2214856.oQueMuda: More authorities could ask the Superior Court of Justice to send serious human rights violations to federal courts.
c2214856.quemAfeta: Victims of serious human rights violations.
c2214856.porQueImporta: Today only the Prosecutor General can ask the Superior Court of Justice to move a serious human rights case to federal courts. Under the PEC, other officials and bodies could ask too.

c2229382.titulo: Lets temporary acting executives run for office
c2229382.oQueMuda: Speakers of city councils and state assemblies who briefly replace a mayor or governor would not become ineligible.
c2229382.porQueImporta: Today anyone who takes over as mayor or governor in the six months before an election is barred from running for certain posts. Under the PEC, heads of councils and legislatures who briefly take over would not be barred.

c590035.oQueMuda: Removes from the Constitution the mandatory collection of union dues.
c590035.porQueImporta: Since 2017 the union contribution has only been charged to those who authorize it, by law. Under the PEC, the mandatory contribution would be removed from the Constitution, and a law could no longer make it mandatory.

c2126901.titulo: Requires the income tax table to be updated
c2126901.oQueMuda: The personal income tax brackets and deductions would have mandatory periodic adjustments.
c2126901.porQueImporta: Today the income tax table is only adjusted when the government decides, and it has gone years without adjustment. Under the PEC, adjustment would be mandatory and periodic.

c2402861.titulo: Turns municipal guards into municipal police
c2402861.oQueMuda: Creates municipal police forces and changes retirement rules for guards and prison police.
c2402861.quemAfeta: Municipal guards, prison police and city governments.
c2402861.porQueImporta: Today municipal guards protect city property and services and do not patrol. Under the PEC, they would become municipal police, with their own retirement rules for guards and prison officers.

s8937612.oQueMuda: Creates rules and funding to expand full-day public education.
s8937612.quemAfeta: Students, families and public school systems.
s8937612.porQueImporta: Today the National Education Plan sets targets for full-time schooling, without money guaranteed in the Constitution. Under the PEC, there would be rules and funds to expand full-time places.

s8950015.titulo: Puts women's right to a life free of violence into the Constitution
s8950015.oQueMuda: Adds one sentence to the list of fundamental rights: women have the right to a life free of violence, at home and outside it. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8950015.quemAfeta: Women, judges and lawmakers, who would have this right written into the Constitution.
s8950015.porQueImporta: Today protection comes mainly from laws such as the Maria da Penha Law, and the Constitution only mentions violence within the family. As a fundamental right, it could not be removed even by another amendment.

s8951742.titulo: Protects people close to retirement from sudden rule changes
s8951742.oQueMuda: Adds the principle of legitimate expectations on pension rules to the Constitution.
s8951742.quemAfeta: People insured by the pension system.
s8951742.porQueImporta: Today pension rules can be changed by amendment, as in 2019. Under the PEC, changes would have to respect the expectations of current contributors, and governments could not change rules to the detriment of those already insured.

c2332037.titulo: Creates higher minimum pay for health agents with technical training
c2332037.oQueMuda: Community health and disease-control agents with technical training would have a separate minimum salary.
c2332037.quemAfeta: Community health agents and city governments.
c2332037.porQueImporta: Since 2022 community health and disease control workers have a pay floor of two minimum wages. Under the PEC, those with technical training would have a higher floor.

c2447265.titulo: Creates an economic reparations fund for Black Brazilians
c2447265.oQueMuda: Adds a racial equality chapter to the Constitution and a fund to create opportunities for Black and brown Brazilians.
c2447265.porQueImporta: Today policies for Black Brazilians are in the 2010 Racial Equality Statute and depend on each year's budget. Under the PEC, there would be a chapter in the Constitution and a fund with reserved resources.

s7732421.titulo: Allows public university students to give something back
s7732421.oQueMuda: Public education stays free, but university students could provide community services in return.
s7732421.porQueImporta: Today public education is free, with nothing required in return. Under the PEC, it would remain free, but public university students could be required to provide social services.

s7825125.titulo: Takes the education payroll contribution out of the spending cap
s7825125.oQueMuda: Spending paid with the education payroll contribution (salário-educação) would no longer count toward the federal spending limit.
s7825125.porQueImporta: Today spending funded by the salário-educação, a contribution paid by companies, counts toward the federal spending limit. Under the PEC, it would be outside that limit.

s8639162.titulo: Gives states the power to make prison laws
s8639162.oQueMuda: States alone would set the rules for serving sentences and running prisons.
s8639162.quemAfeta: Prisoners, prison staff and state governments.
s8639162.porQueImporta: Today sentencing rules are in the Penal Execution Law, which applies nationwide. Under the PEC, each state would make its own rules.

s8834143.titulo: Gives the legislature power to create reserves and Indigenous lands
s8834143.oQueMuda: Environmental protection areas and Indigenous lands would require approval from Congress.
s8834143.quemAfeta: Indigenous peoples, farmers and environmental agencies.
s8834143.porQueImporta: Today conservation areas and Indigenous lands are created by the executive branch, by decree. Under the PEC, they would depend on approval by Congress.

c560156.titulo: Lets administrative civil servants also work as teachers
c560156.oQueMuda: Civil servants in administrative careers could hold a second job as a teacher.
c560156.porQueImporta: Today only technical or scientific posts can be combined with a teaching post. Under the PEC, administrative staff could also hold a second teaching post.

c1504922.titulo: Allows combining a teaching-support job with teaching
c1504922.oQueMuda: Professionals in teaching-support posts could hold another teaching job.
c1504922.porQueImporta: Today only technical or scientific posts can be combined with a teaching post. Under the PEC, those in technical-pedagogical posts could hold a second teaching post.

c276180.titulo: Requires a public exam to hire justices of the peace
c276180.oQueMuda: Justices of the peace would be chosen through a public exam; current ones stay until their seat opens.
c276180.quemAfeta: Justices of the peace and people getting married in civil ceremonies.
c276180.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution provides that justices of the peace, who perform weddings, are elected by the public. Under the PEC, they would be chosen by public exam.

s8999790.oQueMuda: The President could not run for the next term.
s8999790.porQueImporta: Since 1997, the president can be re-elected once. Under the PEC, each president would have a single 4-year term.

c2225224.titulo: Lets teachers hold another public job
c2225224.oQueMuda: A public school teacher may hold another public post in any field, as long as the schedules are compatible.
c2225224.quemAfeta: Public school teachers and the bodies that hire them.
c2225224.porQueImporta: In force since December 2025 (Amendment 138). Before, teachers could only combine their post with another teaching post or a technical or scientific post.

c2578996.titulo: Lets workers choose a flexible hourly schedule
c2578996.oQueMuda: Employees could choose between the standard CLT work schedule and a flexible arrangement paid by the hour.
c2578996.porQueImporta: Today the labor code limits the workweek to 44 hours with a monthly salary. Under the PEC, workers could choose a regime paid only for hours worked, without fixed hours.

c542454.titulo: Allows judges to be removed for misconduct
c542454.oQueMuda: Bans retirement as a punishment and provides for judges to lose office for breach of decorum.
c542454.porQueImporta: Today the maximum administrative penalty for judges is compulsory retirement with proportional pay. Under the PEC, it would end, and judges could lose their post for breach of decorum.

s8831744.oQueMuda: Changes articles on the use of education funds, such as the education payroll contribution and transfers to non-state schools.
s8831744.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, the rules on using the salário-educação and on passing public money to community, religious and charitable schools would change.

s8900982.titulo: Has city council members tried by state courts
s8900982.oQueMuda: Municipal charters could provide that city council members be tried by the state courts of justice.
s8900982.porQueImporta: Today city councilors are tried by first-instance judges, like any citizen. Under the PEC, each city could provide that they are tried by the state Court of Justice.

c500183.oQueMuda: Teenagers from age 14 could work part-time.
c500183.porQueImporta: Today people under 16 can only work as apprentices, from age 14. Under the PEC, they could have part-time jobs from 14.

c2118618.titulo: Splits legislative seats equally between men and women
c2118618.oQueMuda: Seats in the Chamber, the Senate, state assemblies and city councils would be divided half and half.
c2118618.porQueImporta: Today about 18% of seats in the Chamber of Deputies are held by women. Under the PEC, half of the seats in all legislatures would be reserved for women.

c2224818.titulo: Gives the Federal Police investigative autonomy
c2224818.oQueMuda: Guarantees the Federal Police investigative and technical-scientific autonomy.
c2224818.quemAfeta: The Federal Police and the federal government.
c2224818.porQueImporta: Today the Federal Police reports to the Ministry of Justice, and its director is chosen by the president. Under the PEC, the Federal Police would have investigative autonomy guaranteed in the Constitution.

c1299731.titulo: Sets pay rules for the Federal Highway Police
c1299731.oQueMuda: Sets constitutional parameters for the pay of federal highway police officers.
c1299731.porQueImporta: Today federal highway police pay is set by law. Under the PEC, the Constitution would set parameters for this pay, funded by the federal government.

c2188961.titulo: Changes how FPM transfers to cities are calculated
c2188961.oQueMuda: The Municipal Participation Fund amount would be based on the average of the previous 48 months.
c2188961.porQueImporta: Today the monthly FPM transfer follows income tax and IPI revenue in that period. Under the PEC, the amount would be based on the average of the previous 48 months.

c2377463.titulo: Bans decriminalizing drugs, including possession for personal use
c2377463.oQueMuda:
National goal: eradicating trafficking, production, possession, carrying and use of illegal drugs would become one of the Republic's fundamental goals.
Ban: decriminalizing possession and carrying of drugs, even for personal use, and legalizing recreational use of any drug beyond those already allowed would be prohibited.
Treatment: the state would promote prevention and treatment with the help of families, therapeutic communities, private organizations and religious institutions.
Research: scientific research on new substances with medicinal use is guaranteed.
c2377463.quemAfeta: Drug users, the justice system and treatment organizations, including religious ones.
c2377463.porQueImporta: Today the Drug Law punishes possession for personal use with a warning, community service or a course, and in 2024 the Supreme Court stopped treating possession of up to 40 grams of marijuana as a crime. Under the PEC, the Constitution would ban decriminalizing possession of any drug, in any amount.

c2380340.titulo: Changes pensions for city civil servants
c2380340.oQueMuda: Changes the rules of city pension systems to balance their accounts.
c2380340.quemAfeta: City civil servants and city governments.
c2380340.porQueImporta: Many city governments run their own pension systems for staff, and several are in deficit. Under the PEC, contribution and benefit rules for these systems would change.

c579931.titulo: Creates a Constitutional Court and changes the STJ and CNJ
c579931.oQueMuda: Creates a court only for constitutional matters and changes the makeup and appointments of the Superior Court of Justice and the National Council of Justice.
c579931.quemAfeta: Higher courts and people who appeal to them.
c579931.porQueImporta: Today the Supreme Court rules both on constitutional questions and on appeals and cases against officials. Under the PEC, a new Constitutional Court would handle only constitutional questions, and the way members of the STJ and CNJ are chosen would change.

c514540.titulo: Allows seizing land where illegal hunting occurs
c514540.oQueMuda: Rural properties with illegal hunting could be expropriated and used for land reform.
c514540.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution allows land to be seized without compensation only where drugs are grown or slave labor is found. Under the PEC, land where illegal hunting occurs could also be seized and used for land reform.

c384232.oQueMuda: People not affiliated with a party could run, as long as they have support from a minimum number of voters.
c384232.quemAfeta: Voters, parties and possible independent candidates.
c384232.porQueImporta: Today one can only run for office as a member of a party. Under the PEC, people with support from a minimum number of voters could run without a party.

c2086220.titulo: Creates recall: voters could remove officials
c2086220.oQueMuda: Citizens could vote to remove a president, governor or mayor, with prior approval from the legislature.
c2086220.quemAfeta: Voters and heads of the executive branch.
c2086220.porQueImporta: Today a president, governor or mayor only leaves office early through impeachment, removal or resignation. Under the PEC, voters could vote to end the term, with prior approval from the legislature.

c2088445.titulo: Adopts a parliamentary system in Brazil
c2088445.oQueMuda: The government would be led by a prime minister chosen with the support of Congress, who could be removed by a vote of no confidence.
c2088445.porQueImporta: Today the elected president is both head of state and head of government; in 1993 voters chose this system in a referendum. Under the PEC, a prime minister backed by Congress would govern and could be removed by a vote of lawmakers.

c113412.titulo: Limits spending on ads for government projects
c113412.oQueMuda: Sets limits on what governments and state-owned companies can spend advertising public works and campaigns.
c113412.porQueImporta: Today there is no constitutional limit on government and state company advertising spending, only rules in election years. Under the PEC, there would be a cap on this spending.

c145695.titulo: Sets rules for raising politicians' and officials' salaries
c145695.oQueMuda: Defines criteria for reviewing the salaries of top officials, legislators, ministers and secretaries.
c145695.porQueImporta: Today salaries of lawmakers, ministers and judges are raised by law or decree, with no fixed index. Under the PEC, there would be criteria set in the Constitution for these raises.

c320708.titulo: Lets municipal guards patrol the streets
c320708.oQueMuda: Municipal guards could do street patrols through an agreement with the state.
c320708.quemAfeta: Municipal guards, military police and city governments.
c320708.porQueImporta: Today municipal guards protect city property and services, and patrolling belongs to the military police. Under the PEC, guards could patrol streets through an agreement with the state.

c453251.titulo: Gives autonomy to the Federal Police
c453251.oQueMuda: A complementary law would give the Federal Police operational and administrative autonomy and the power to propose its own budget.
c453251.quemAfeta: The Federal Police and the federal government.
c453251.porQueImporta: Today the Federal Police is part of the Ministry of Justice, which sets its budget, and its director is chosen by the president. Under the PEC, the Federal Police would have functional and administrative autonomy and propose its own budget.

c589892.titulo: Ends the benefit for prisoners' families and creates one for crime victims
c589892.oQueMuda: The benefit paid to prisoners' dependents would end and a new benefit would be created for victims and their dependents.
c589892.porQueImporta: Today the prisoner's family benefit is paid to dependents of low-income prisoners who contributed to INSS. Under the PEC, this benefit would end and a benefit for crime victims and their dependents would be created.

c2081963.titulo: Extends a benefit to orphans who grew up in shelters until age 21
c2081963.oQueMuda: Young orphans who lived in institutional care would receive one minimum wage a month from 18 to 21.
c2081963.quemAfeta: Young people who grew up in shelters.
c2081963.porQueImporta: Today young people raised in shelters leave care at 18 with no guaranteed benefit. Under the PEC, orphans in this situation would receive one minimum wage per month until 21.

c2174497.titulo: Lets cities charge a fee to revitalize urban areas
c2174497.oQueMuda: Cities and the Federal District could create a contribution to pay for revitalization works in specific areas.
c2174497.quemAfeta: Residents and businesses in those areas, and city governments.
c2174497.porQueImporta: Today cities cannot create a levy for works in specific areas. Under the PEC, they could charge residents and businesses in those areas to pay for revitalization.

s8611954.titulo: Exempts cars 20 years or older from vehicle tax (IPVA)
s8611954.oQueMuda: Passenger cars, pickups and mixed-use vehicles 20 or more years old stop paying the vehicle tax (IPVA) nationwide. Buses, minibuses, trailers and semi-trailers still pay.
s8611954.quemAfeta: Owners of old vehicles and the states, which collect IPVA and pass half to municipalities.
s8611954.porQueImporta: In force since December 2025. Before, each state set the age at which vehicles stopped paying IPVA, and the rules ranged from 10 to 30 years or more.

c2598301.titulo: Adds civil servants to the CNJ and CNMP
c2598301.oQueMuda: Changes the councils that oversee the judiciary and prosecutors to include civil servants.
c2598301.quemAfeta: Staff of the judiciary and prosecutors' offices.
c2598301.porQueImporta: Today the CNJ and CNMP are made up of judges, prosecutors, lawyers and citizens appointed by Congress. Under the PEC, judiciary and prosecution staff would also have seats.

c1307014.titulo: Creates the Rio Branco Free Trade Zone, in Acre
c1307014.oQueMuda: Creates an area with tax benefits for companies in Rio Branco.
c1307014.porQueImporta: Today the only free trade zone with tax benefits in the Constitution is Manaus. Under the PEC, Rio Branco would also have an area where companies pay less tax.

c434376.titulo: Requires full sentences in closed prison for heinous crimes
c434376.oQueMuda: People who commit heinous crimes would serve the entire sentence in closed prison.
c434376.quemAfeta: People convicted of heinous crimes and the prison system.
c434376.porQueImporta: Today people convicted of heinous crimes can move to a semi-open regime after serving 40% to 70% of the sentence; in 2006 the Supreme Court struck down a rule banning this. Under the PEC, they would serve the whole sentence in closed prison.

s1396298.titulo: Cuts the workweek to 36 hours over up to 5 days
s1396298.oQueMuda: Under the version approved by the Senate committee, the maximum workweek would be 36 hours over up to 5 days, with 2 days off (preferably Saturday and Sunday).
s1396298.quemAfeta: Workers with formal employment contracts and employers.
s1396298.porQueImporta: People who work more than 36 hours or six days a week today would work less for the same pay, which the text guarantees. For those going from 44 to 36 hours, the employer's wage cost per hour worked rises about 22%.

c2596372.titulo: Allows restrictions on lottery and betting ads
c2596372.oQueMuda: The law could limit or ban advertising for lotteries and sports betting.
c2596372.quemAfeta: Betting companies, media outlets and bettors.
c2596372.porQueImporta: Today gambling advertising is regulated by law and government rules, with restrictions on time and audience. Under the PEC, the law could limit or ban this advertising, based on the Constitution.

c2595818.titulo: Lets education professionals hold two public jobs
c2595818.oQueMuda: Other education professionals, besides teachers, could hold two public jobs.
c2595818.porQueImporta: Today only teachers, health professionals and technical posts can hold two public posts. Under the PEC, other education professionals could too.

c2140426.titulo: Creates a popular veto on laws
c2140426.oQueMuda: Voters could strike down approved laws, following set criteria.
c2140426.porQueImporta: Today voters can propose laws by collecting signatures but cannot overturn laws already passed. Under the PEC, they could repeal laws through a popular veto.

s8815148.titulo: Adds the juvenile detention system to public safety
s8815148.oQueMuda: Bodies that apply measures to juvenile offenders would become part of public safety, with jobs filled by public exam.
s8815148.quemAfeta: Juvenile detention staff and detained teenagers.
s8815148.porQueImporta: Today staff at juvenile detention units are not part of the public security bodies. Under the PEC, they would be, with posts filled by public exam.

s8060173.titulo: Bans individual judges' rulings that suspend laws
s8060173.oQueMuda:
Individual rulings: in every court, a single judge could not suspend a law or acts of the presidents of the Republic, the Chamber, the Senate or Congress; that would require a majority of the court.
Recess: during judicial holidays, the court's president could decide alone in cases of serious urgency, and the court would have 30 days after returning to confirm it or the ruling loses effect.
Deadline: when the Supreme Court suspends a law in a constitutional challenge, it has 6 months to decide the case; after that, the case jumps the queue or the suspension loses effect.
Other cases: rulings that halt bills in Congress, affect public policies or create expenses would also require a majority of the court.
s8060173.quemAfeta: Courts, especially the Supreme Court, and Congress.
s8060173.porQueImporta: Today a single Supreme Court justice can suspend a law with a provisional ruling, which is later taken to the full court. Under the PEC, a majority would be needed from the start. The original version also set a deadline for requests for review, but that part was removed in the Senate.

c2391567.titulo: Lets Congress overturn Supreme Court rulings
c2391567.oQueMuda: Congress could overturn final Supreme Court rulings it considers beyond the Constitution's limits. One third of deputies and senators would have to propose it, and it would need three fifths of the votes in each house, in two rounds. The overturn would take effect immediately.
c2391567.porQueImporta: Today final Supreme Court rulings cannot be overturned by Congress, only superseded by a new constitutional amendment or a new law. Under the PEC, Congress itself would decide which rulings went too far.
c2391567.apelido: PEC letting Congress overturn Supreme Court rulings
c2391567.nota: Separation of powers is an entrenched clause: the Constitution bars amendments tending to abolish it (art. 60, § 4). For that reason, legal scholars consider the PEC likely to be ruled unconstitutional. Its author says it removes no powers from the Supreme Court and only balances the branches.

s8968311.titulo: Lets any citizen file charges against Supreme Court justices
s8968311.oQueMuda: Restores citizens' right to file impeachable-offense charges against Supreme Court justices.
s8968311.quemAfeta: Citizens, the Senate and Supreme Court justices.
s8968311.porQueImporta: Today, under a Supreme Court ruling, only the Prosecutor General can request the impeachment of Supreme Court justices. Under the PEC, any citizen could again petition the Senate.

c2591196.titulo: Counts school meals as education spending
c2591196.oQueMuda: Spending on school meals would count toward the minimum governments must invest in education.
c2591196.porQueImporta: Today governments must spend a minimum share of tax revenue on education (18% federal, 25% states and municipalities), and school meals do not count. Under the PEC, school meal spending would count toward that minimum.

s8966726.titulo: Changes how Supreme Court justices are chosen
s8966726.oQueMuda: Changes the appointment process, with participation of the National Council of Justice and a list of candidates.
s8966726.quemAfeta: The President, the Senate and the Supreme Court.
s8966726.porQueImporta: Today the president freely nominates Supreme Court justices, who must be approved by the Senate. Under the PEC, the choice would come from a list of candidates with CNJ participation.

s8789546.titulo: Gives Congress power over public safety rules
s8789546.oQueMuda: Congress alone would set general rules on public safety, social defense and prisons.
s8789546.quemAfeta: Federal and state governments and the police.
s8789546.porQueImporta: Today the federal government and states share the power to make public security and prison laws. Under the PEC, only Congress would make the general rules.

s8961392.titulo: States in the Constitution that honor and image remain protected after death
s8961392.oQueMuda: Adds 'even after death' to the right to privacy, honor and image, with the right to compensation. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8961392.quemAfeta: Families of deceased people, journalists and the media.
s8961392.porQueImporta: The Civil Code already lets relatives defend the image of someone who has died; the change puts this protection in the Constitution.

c2543145.titulo: Creates anti-privilege rules for public officials
c2543145.oQueMuda: Bans certain perks and salary equivalences between politicians and civil servants.
c2543145.porQueImporta: Today some careers and political posts have linked salaries, so a raise for one lifts others. Under the PEC, these links and certain perks would be banned.

s7757038.titulo: Lets the federal government hand ports, railways and energy to states
s7757038.oQueMuda: States could run ports, railways and energy, and keep increases in federal revenue collected in their territory.
s7757038.quemAfeta: State governments and the federal government.
s7757038.porQueImporta: Today ports, railways and energy are federal responsibilities. Under the PEC, states could operate these services and keep the increase in federal revenue generated in their territory.

s7737114.titulo: Sends oil royalties to education and health
s7737114.oQueMuda: Oil money from new fields would go 75% to education and 25% to health, outside the spending cap.
s7737114.porQueImporta: Today part of oil royalties already goes to education and health under a 2013 law. Under the PEC, money from new fields would go 75% to education and 25% to health, outside the spending limit.

c2479738.titulo: Creates special working conditions for professional drivers
