c2479738.oQueMuda: Sets specific rules for drivers employed in freight and passenger transport.
c2479738.quemAfeta: Truck and bus drivers and companies.
c2479738.porQueImporta: Today professional drivers have working-hour and rest rules in the 2015 Drivers Law. Under the PEC, these conditions would have a basis in the Constitution.

c2225743.titulo: Creates the Teresina Free Trade Zone, in Piauí
c2225743.oQueMuda: Creates an area with tax benefits for companies in Teresina.
c2225743.porQueImporta: Today the only free trade zone with tax benefits in the Constitution is Manaus. Under the PEC, Teresina would also have an area where companies pay less tax.

c334449.titulo: Extends special retirement to other education professionals
c334449.oQueMuda: Principals, coordinators and counselors would have the same special retirement as teachers.
c334449.porQueImporta: Today classroom teachers retire five years earlier than other civil servants. Under the PEC, principals, coordinators and counselors would have the same right.

s8951883.titulo: Requires Congress to vote on citizen-initiated bills
s8951883.oQueMuda: Citizen-initiated bills or requests from a majority of legislators would have to be considered.
s8951883.porQueImporta: Today the heads of the Chamber and Senate decide which bills go to a vote, and citizen-initiated bills can stall. Under the PEC, these bills would have to be considered.

c2471383.titulo: Sets aside part of legislators' budget amendments for sports
c2471383.oQueMuda: Part of deputies' and senators' individual budget amendments would have to go to sports programs.
c2471383.porQueImporta: Today half of individual budget amendments must already go to health. Under the PEC, a share would also have to go to sports programs.

c2336011.titulo: Raises the March FPM transfer by 1.5%
c2336011.oQueMuda: The federal government would hand an extra 1.5% of its revenue to the Municipal Participation Fund every March.
c2336011.porQueImporta: Today the federal government transfers 22.5% of income tax and IPI to FPM, plus extra 1% shares in July, September and December. Under the PEC, there would be another 1.5% in March.

c2363434.titulo: Changes the FPM and creates funds for the South and Southeast
c2363434.oQueMuda: Changes how the FPM is shared and creates constitutional financing funds for the South and Southeast regions.
c2363434.quemAfeta: City governments and companies in these regions.
c2363434.porQueImporta: Today there are constitutional credit funds only for the North, Northeast and Center-West. Under the PEC, the South and Southeast would also have them, and FPM would be split differently.

c2122682.titulo: Makes Audit Courts permanent and bans creating or abolishing them
c2122682.oQueMuda: Audit Courts would become permanent bodies essential to overseeing public spending, and abolishing, creating or setting up new ones would be prohibited.
c2122682.quemAfeta: Audit Courts and the governments they oversee.
c2122682.porQueImporta: Today there are 33 Audit Courts in the country, and states could create or abolish those that oversee municipalities. Under the PEC, existing ones could not be abolished, and creating new ones would be banned.

s8941223.titulo: Creates fixed terms and new requirements for Supreme Court justices
s8941223.oQueMuda: Changes age and requirements and creates fixed terms for Supreme Court justices.
s8941223.quemAfeta: Current and future Supreme Court justices.
s8941223.porQueImporta: Today Supreme Court justices serve until age 75. Under the PEC, they would have fixed terms, and the age and requirements for nomination would change.

c2467670.titulo: Gives the Chamber power to oversee regulatory agencies
c2467670.oQueMuda: The Chamber of Deputies would have its own power to oversee regulatory agencies.
c2467670.quemAfeta: Agencies such as Anatel, Aneel and ANS.
c2467670.porQueImporta: Today regulatory agencies are overseen by Congress and the Federal Audit Court in general terms. Under the PEC, the Chamber of Deputies would have its own specific power to oversee them.

c555267.titulo: Bans government advertising except for public service messages
c555267.oQueMuda: Public bodies could only run public service advertising.
c555267.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution allows official advertising that is educational, informative or socially oriented. Under the PEC, public bodies could only run public-service advertising.

c1212600.titulo: Bans government slogans and branding in official ads
c1212600.oQueMuda: Official advertising could not use slogans, logos or colors that identify those in power.
c1212600.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution bans names, symbols and images promoting officials in official advertising, but governments use their own slogans and logos. Under the PEC, government slogans, logos and colors would also be banned.

c1584971.titulo: Bans identifying officeholders in official ads
c1584971.oQueMuda: Official advertising could not include anything that identifies the officeholder.
c1584971.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution bans names, symbols and images promoting officials in official advertising, but governments use their own brands. Under the PEC, any element identifying the leader would be banned.

s8810165.titulo: Allows bonus points for local applicants to federal universities
s8810165.oQueMuda: Federal universities could give extra points to applicants born or living in the region.
s8810165.porQueImporta: Today admission to federal universities is through the Enem exam, with social and racial quotas, and no advantage based on place of origin. Under the PEC, universities could give extra points to local candidates.

c2293703.titulo: Reserves 30% of campaign funds for women candidates and pardons parties that missed quotas
c2293703.oQueMuda:
Funds for women: parties must give women candidates at least 30% of the campaign fund, of the party-fund share used in campaigns and of radio and TV time, in proportion to the number of women candidates; how it is split among them follows each party's criteria.
Political participation: at least 5% of the party fund must go to programs encouraging women's political participation.
Pardon: parties that failed to meet gender and race quotas in past elections cannot be punished with fines, repayment or suspension of the party fund; money not spent on programs for women may be used in later elections.
c2293703.quemAfeta: Parties, women candidates and Black candidates.
c2293703.porQueImporta: In force since April 2022. Before, the 30% reserve for women came from Supreme Court and Electoral Court rulings, and parties that ignored it could be punished; the amendment put the rule in the Constitution and pardoned penalties for past elections.

c355205.titulo: Creates a single salary cap for the whole public sector
c355205.oQueMuda: The maximum salary would be the same in federal, state and city governments.
c355205.porQueImporta: Today the salary cap is a Supreme Court justice's pay at federal level, with lower sub-caps in states and municipalities. Under the PEC, the same limit would apply to all.

c2270800.titulo: Requires Congress's permission to prosecute members of Congress
c2270800.oQueMuda:
Permission to prosecute: the Supreme Court could only open criminal cases against deputies and senators with authorization from the Chamber or Senate, by secret ballot and absolute majority, within 90 days.
Arrest: members of Congress could only be arrested in the act of a non-bailable crime, and their house would decide by secret ballot whether to keep them detained.
Special court for party leaders: national presidents of parties represented in Congress would be tried by the Supreme Court.
Precautionary measures: searches, asset freezes and other measures against members of Congress could only be ordered by the Supreme Court.
c2270800.quemAfeta: Federal deputies, senators, party presidents and the Supreme Court.
c2270800.porQueImporta: Since 2001, the Supreme Court can prosecute members of Congress without asking Congress; before that, almost no requests were approved. The Chamber approved the PEC in September 2025; a week later, the Senate Justice Committee unanimously rejected it and it was shelved.

c2563273.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for a digital currency or ending paper money
c2563273.oQueMuda: Creating a Central Bank digital currency or ending paper money would need approval from Congress.
c2563273.porQueImporta: Today the Central Bank decides alone on digital currency and paper money. Under the PEC, creating a digital real or ending notes and coins would depend on Congress.

c2145273.titulo: Adds long-term care to social security
c2145273.oQueMuda: People who depend on long-term care would have this support as a social security right, with its own fund.
c2145273.quemAfeta: Dependent older people and people with disabilities, and their families.
c2145273.porQueImporta: Today long-term care for older and dependent people is generally paid by families, except for specific programs. Under the PEC, it would become a social security right, with its own fund.

s8796560.titulo: Allows regional quotas at public universities
s8796560.oQueMuda: Public universities could adopt affirmative action based on geography in admissions.
s8796560.porQueImporta: Today quotas at public universities are based on income, public schooling, race and disability. Under the PEC, they could also consider the candidate's region of origin.

s8823143.titulo: Guarantees maternity leave to women legislators
s8823143.oQueMuda: Women legislators would have the right to leave for pregnancy or adoption.
s8823143.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution does not provide maternity leave for those holding legislative office, and each house has its own rules. Under the PEC, women councilors, deputies and senators would have this right, with the alternate taking their place.

s8594291.titulo: Caps court-ordered debt payments, ends the deadline to clear them and reopens debt installment plans
s8594291.oQueMuda:
## States and municipalities
Annual cap: states and municipalities pay court-ordered debts (precatórios) up to 1% to 5% of revenue, depending on the size of the debt; the cap rises 0.5 point every 10 years, from 2036, if debt remains.
No final deadline: the deadline the Constitution set to pay off the whole overdue debt ends.
Old debts: the cap also applies to court-ordered debts issued before the amendment.
Adjustment: amounts are adjusted by inflation (IPCA) plus 2% a year, as long as this does not exceed the Selic rate.
Settlement: creditors may accept a discount to be paid earlier, in a lump sum.
Pensions: municipalities may pay pension-system debts in up to 300 monthly installments.
## Federal government
Federal spending: from 2026, federal court-ordered debts leave the government's spending cap and are gradually counted in the fiscal target, 10% more each year, from 2027.
s8594291.quemAfeta: People and companies owed court-ordered payments, municipal and state governments, and the federal government.
s8594291.porQueImporta: In force since September 2025. Before, states and municipalities had a constitutional deadline to pay off all overdue court-ordered debt; that deadline no longer exists.
s8594291.apelido: Court-ordered debts and city debts amendment
s8594291.nota: The Independent Fiscal Institution, the Senate's technical body, says this regime, like previous ones, creates a growing stock of unpaid court-ordered debts. The Brazilian Bar Association challenged the amendment at the Supreme Court, calling it an "official default". Supporters say it makes public finances more predictable.

c519258.oQueMuda: Creates a body for maritime, airport and border policing.
c519258.quemAfeta: The Federal Police and residents of border regions.
c519258.porQueImporta: Today border, port and airport policing is done by the Federal Police. Under the PEC, a dedicated body, the Border Guard, would be created.

c522713.titulo: Hands public safety in the Amazon to the federal government
c522713.oQueMuda: Public safety in the Legal Amazon would be the federal government's responsibility.
c522713.quemAfeta: Residents of the Legal Amazon, state police and the Federal Police.
c522713.porQueImporta: Today public security in the Legal Amazon states is the responsibility of state governments. Under the PEC, it would move to the federal government.

c505266.oQueMuda: Teenagers could be hired as regular employees from age 14.
c505266.porQueImporta: Today people under 16 can only work as apprentices, from age 14. Under the PEC, they could have regular formal jobs from 14.

c579916.oQueMuda: Lowers the minimum age to work.
c579916.porQueImporta: Today people under 16 can only work as apprentices, from age 14. Under the PEC, the minimum working age would be lowered.

c1527035.oQueMuda: Teenagers over 15 would have the right to work.
c1527035.porQueImporta: Today people under 16 can only work as apprentices, from age 14. Under the PEC, 15-year-olds could have regular jobs.

c1598550.oQueMuda: Young people over 16 could be formally hired without being apprentices.
c1598550.porQueImporta: Today 16- and 17-year-olds can already have formal jobs, with night, dangerous or unhealthy work banned. Under the PEC, this would be made more explicit in the Constitution, separate from apprenticeship contracts.

c1618127.porQueImporta: Today people under 16 can only work as apprentices, from age 14. Under the PEC, they could have regular jobs from 14.

c2236844.oQueMuda: The ban on any work would apply only to children under 13 (today it is 16, except apprentices from 14); night, dangerous or unhealthy work would remain banned before 18.
c2236844.quemAfeta: Teenagers aged 13 to 15, their families and employers.
c2236844.porQueImporta: Today people under 16 can only work as apprentices, from age 14. Under the PEC, children from 13 could have regular jobs; Brazil has signed the ILO convention setting a minimum working age.

c2231221.titulo: Allows public universities to charge tuition
c2231221.oQueMuda: Public universities could charge students tuition.
c2231221.quemAfeta: Public university students and their families.
c2231221.porQueImporta: Today public university education is free for everyone. Under the PEC, they could charge students tuition.

c2341862.titulo: Frees R$ 145 billion outside the cap in 2023, raises congressional amendments and orders the spending cap replaced
c2341862.oQueMuda:
Extra spending in 2023: the 2023 spending cap rose by R$ 145 billion, used for programs such as the R$ 600 Bolsa Família, without counting toward the fiscal target.
End of the cap: the government had to send a new fiscal rule by August 2023 to replace the spending cap; it became the fiscal framework.
Congressional amendments: individual budget amendments by deputies and senators rose from 1.2% to 2% of net current revenue (1.55% for deputies and 0.45% for senators), half for health.
c2341862.quemAfeta: The federal government, social program beneficiaries and members of Congress.
c2341862.porQueImporta: In force since December 2022. The spending cap, which had limited spending growth to inflation since 2016, was replaced by the fiscal framework, and each member of Congress now has more budget money to allocate.

c2075880.titulo: Requires estimating the impact of new obligations on businesses
c2075880.oQueMuda: Laws creating or expanding obligations for economic sectors would need an estimate of the financial impact.
c2075880.porQueImporta: Today laws creating obligations for companies do not need to come with a cost estimate. Under the PEC, this estimate would be mandatory.

s8786193.titulo: Adjusts the Federal District fund by federal revenue
s8786193.oQueMuda: The Federal District's Constitutional Fund would be adjusted every year by the change in federal net revenue.
s8786193.quemAfeta: The government and residents of the Federal District.
s8786193.porQueImporta: Today the fund the federal government pays the Federal District for security, health and education is adjusted by federal net current revenue, by law. Under the PEC, this rule would be in the Constitution.

s8839624.titulo: Ends special court privileges when the term ends
s8839624.oQueMuda: Courts' power to try officials would end along with their term or office.
s8839624.quemAfeta: Politicians and officials with special court privileges.
s8839624.porQueImporta: In 2025 the Supreme Court ruled that special jurisdiction continues after an official leaves office, for crimes committed in the role. Under the PEC, the case would return to the first instance as soon as the term or post ended.

c2086981.titulo: Changes how the vehicle tax (IPVA) is calculated
c2086981.oQueMuda: Creates a new tax base for the vehicle tax.
c2086981.porQueImporta: Today IPVA is calculated on the vehicle's market value. Under the PEC, the calculation base would change.

c2142844.titulo: Gives the armed forces border, port and airport policing
c2142844.oQueMuda: The armed forces would take on this policing role.
c2142844.quemAfeta: The armed forces and the Federal Police.
c2142844.porQueImporta: Today border, port and airport policing belongs to the Federal Police, and the armed forces only act in specific operations. Under the PEC, it would be a permanent duty of the armed forces.

s8856883.titulo: Adds the environment to foreign policy goals
s8856883.oQueMuda: Brazil's international relations would aim to promote environmental balance and sustainable development.
s8856883.porQueImporta: Today the foreign policy principles in the Constitution include human rights and peace, but not the environment. Under the PEC, environmental balance would become a goal of the country's international relations.

c2544926.titulo: Lowers the retirement age for women police and officers
c2544926.oQueMuda: Women police officers, prison officers and juvenile detention officers could retire earlier.
c2544926.porQueImporta: Today retirement for these careers follows the 2019 reform at federal level and each state's laws. Under the PEC, women police officers and prison and juvenile detention officers would retire earlier than today.

s8255099.titulo: Ends reelection, creates 5-year terms and unifies elections in 2034
s8255099.oQueMuda:
End of reelection: the president, governors and mayors could not run for the same office in the next term.
5-year terms: for every office, including deputies, councillors and senators (senators now serve 8 years).
Single election: from 2034, every office, from councillor to president, would be elected on the same day, every 5 years.
Transition: mayors elected in 2024 and the president and governors elected in 2026 could still seek reelection; mayors and councillors elected in 2028 would serve 6 years; senators elected in 2030 would serve 9 years.
s8255099.quemAfeta: Voters and everyone holding elected office.
s8255099.porQueImporta: Since 1997, the president, governors and mayors can be reelected once, with 4-year terms, and municipal elections take place two years after general elections. The text was approved by the Senate Justice Committee in May 2025 and awaits a floor vote.

c351184.oQueMuda: Creates a police force for ports, which could absorb port guards.
c351184.porQueImporta: Today port security is handled by the Federal Police and by port guards hired by port authorities. Under the PEC, a Federal Port Police would be created.

s7804756.titulo: Defines education as the engine of the country's progress
s7804756.oQueMuda: Adds to the Constitution that education drives Brazil's progress.
s7804756.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution already says education is a right of all and a duty of the State. Under the PEC, it would also say education drives the country's progress; on its own, the change creates no funding or rules.

c486477.titulo: Grants job security to long-serving workers hired under the CLT
c486477.oQueMuda: Civil servants hired under the CLT who were working when the unified legal regime was created would gain tenure.
c486477.quemAfeta: This group of long-serving civil servants.
c486477.porQueImporta: In 1988, civil servants with five years of service gained job stability, but some hired under labor law were left out. Under the PEC, this group would gain stability too.

c2262083.titulo: 2020 administrative reform: dismissal for poor performance, temporary contracts of up to 10 years and reduced hours
c2262083.oQueMuda:
Job stability: tenured civil servants stay tenured after 3 years, but could lose their job for unsatisfactory performance reviews, with the right to a defense.
Abolished posts: a tenured servant would lose the post if a law declares it unnecessary or obsolete, with compensation; if an equivalent post is created within 5 years, they return.
Temporary staff: fixed-term contracts could last up to 10 years, with a simplified selection process.
Reduced hours: in a fiscal crisis, civil servants' hours and pay could be cut by up to 25%.
Partnerships: governments could sign cooperation agreements with private entities to provide public services, including using their staff.
c2262083.quemAfeta: Current and future civil servants and users of public services.
c2262083.porQueImporta: Today tenured civil servants gain job stability after three years and only lose their post through a final court ruling, a disciplinary process or spending cuts. The special committee text has been ready for a Chamber floor vote since 2021; the government's original proposal limited stability to core state careers, but that was removed.

s8574119.titulo: Guarantees a minimum budget for Defense
s8574119.oQueMuda: The Ministry of Defense would have a guaranteed minimum budget and protected strategic projects.
s8574119.quemAfeta: The armed forces and the federal budget.
s8574119.porQueImporta: Today the defense budget is set each year and can be frozen. Under the PEC, it would have a guaranteed minimum and strategic projects protected from cuts.

c2326575.titulo: Adds digital inclusion to the fundamental rights
c2326575.oQueMuda: States that everyone has the right to digital inclusion and that the government must have policies to expand internet access, as set by law. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2326575.quemAfeta: People without internet access and governments.
c2326575.porQueImporta: The Brazilian Internet Bill of Rights already treats access as essential; the change brings this right into the Constitution and calls for public policies.

c464909.titulo: Creates a single national career for public doctors
c464909.oQueMuda: Sets guidelines for a national career for doctors in public service.
c464909.quemAfeta: Doctors and patients of the public health system (SUS).
c464909.porQueImporta: Today public health system doctors are hired mostly by city and state governments, each with their own rules. Under the PEC, there would be a national public-service medical career.

s8582100.oQueMuda: Increases the length of maternity, paternity and adoption leave.
s8582100.porQueImporta: Today maternity leave is 120 days (180 at companies in the Empresa Cidadã program) and paternity leave is 5 days (20 at those companies). Under the PEC, these leaves would be longer.

c356309.titulo: Changes rules for creating or merging municipalities
c356309.oQueMuda: Creating, merging or splitting municipalities would have to preserve historical and cultural unity and happen up to 12 months before elections.
c356309.quemAfeta: Residents of areas seeking to become a municipality.
c356309.porQueImporta: Today creating or splitting municipalities depends on a federal law that has never been passed. Under the PEC, the process would have to preserve historical and cultural unity and occur up to 12 months before elections.

c2209776.titulo: Gives health insurance to former Sucam workers exposed to DDT
c2209776.oQueMuda: Former employees who handled the pesticide DDT would be entitled to health insurance.
c2209776.quemAfeta: Former employees of the old Sucam agency.
c2209776.porQueImporta: Former staff of the old Sucam agency handled the insecticide DDT to fight diseases such as malaria. Under the PEC, they would be entitled to a health plan paid by the federal government.

s8563075.titulo: Adds inclusive education to the principles of education
s8563075.oQueMuda: Adds to the principles of education a guarantee of inclusive teaching at all levels, considering each student's needs. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8563075.quemAfeta: Students with disabilities or specific needs, schools and school systems.
s8563075.porQueImporta: The Constitution already provides specialized support for students with disabilities, preferably in regular schools; the change extends the principle to all levels.

c1618422.titulo: Restores income tax exemption for retirees over 65
c1618422.oQueMuda: It brings back an old rule that exempted from income tax, within legal limits, pensions of people over 65 who live only on that income.
c1618422.porQueImporta: Until 1998, the Constitution exempted part of the pensions of people over 65 from income tax; today there is only a partial exemption by law. Under the PEC, the old rule would return.

c2140425.oQueMuda: Public consultations would take place on election day.
c2140425.porQueImporta: Today referendums can be held on any date. Under the PEC, they would be held on election day.

c2084889.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for heads of state-owned companies
c2084889.oQueMuda: Presidents and directors of federal companies would have to be approved by Congress.
c2084889.quemAfeta: State-owned companies such as Petrobras and public banks.
c2084889.porQueImporta: Today heads and directors of state companies are chosen by the government without congressional approval. Under the PEC, they would need approval by lawmakers.

c460138.titulo: Creates a fund to maintain the public safety system
c460138.oQueMuda: Creates a fund for maintaining and developing public safety.
c460138.porQueImporta: Today the National Public Security Fund exists by law, and its money can change every year. Under the PEC, there would be a fund in the Constitution to maintain public security.

c540302.titulo: Creates a national system and minimum spending on public safety
c540302.oQueMuda: Federal and state governments would have to spend minimum percentages on public safety.
c540302.porQueImporta: Today health and education have mandatory minimum spending, but public security does not. Under the PEC, the federal government and states would have to spend minimum shares of revenue on it.

c568527.titulo: Requires recorded votes on provisional measures
c568527.oQueMuda: Each legislator would have to record their vote on provisional measures (executive decrees).
c568527.porQueImporta: Today many provisional measures are approved by symbolic vote, without recording each lawmaker's vote. Under the PEC, recorded votes would be mandatory.

s1399166.titulo: Lets states make laws protecting older people
s1399166.oQueMuda: Federal and state governments would share the power to make laws protecting older people.
s1399166.porQueImporta: Today protection of older people is covered mainly by federal laws, such as the Statute of Older Persons. Under the PEC, states and the Federal District could also legislate on it.

s8834618.oQueMuda: The word 'agrotóxicos' would be replaced by 'pesticidas' in the constitutional text.
s8834618.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution uses the word 'agrotóxicos' (agro-toxins); a 2023 law switched to 'pesticides'. Under the PEC, the Constitution would also use 'pesticides', without changing the rules on using these products.

s8834813.titulo: Bans freezing science and technology fund money
s8834813.oQueMuda: Spending from the National Science and Technology Development Fund (FNDCT) could not be frozen by the government.
s8834813.porQueImporta: Since 2021 a law has banned freezing FNDCT money, the main federal science fund. Under the PEC, this ban would be in the Constitution.

s8794275.titulo: Cuts social security contributions for inland cities
s8794275.oQueMuda: Inland city governments would pay lower contributions on their payroll.
s8794275.quemAfeta: Inland city governments and social security.
s8794275.porQueImporta: Today city governments pay INSS a contribution on the payroll of staff without their own pension system. Under the PEC, inland cities would pay a lower rate, and INSS would not receive the difference.

c489897.titulo: Gives union confederations part of union dues
c489897.oQueMuda: National union confederations would receive part of union dues.
c489897.porQueImporta: Since 2017 the union contribution has only been charged to those who authorize it. Under the PEC, part of what is collected would go to union federations.

s1395667.titulo: Adds basic sanitation to the social rights
s1395667.oQueMuda: Adds basic sanitation to the Constitution's list of social rights (article 6). On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s1395667.quemAfeta: People without clean water or sewage, and governments.
s1395667.porQueImporta: Today sanitation appears in the Constitution only as a government task, not as a right. Under the PEC, it would join the list of social rights, alongside health, education and housing.

s8309893.titulo: Creates a minimum salary for physical and occupational therapists
s8309893.oQueMuda: Establishes a national minimum salary for these professions.
s8309893.quemAfeta: Physical therapists, occupational therapists and employers.
s8309893.porQueImporta: Today physiotherapists and occupational therapists have no national minimum salary. Under the PEC, clinics, hospitals and governments would have to pay at least the floor set by law.

s7849279.titulo: Creates a fund to repair environmental damage from mining and oil
s7849279.oQueMuda: 1% of federal revenue from oil, gas and minerals would go to preventing and repairing environmental damage.
s7849279.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, 1% of what the federal government receives from oil, gas and minerals would go to a fund for preventing and repairing environmental disasters, like those in Mariana and Brumadinho.

c2499794.titulo: Creates a minimum salary for police and firefighters
c2499794.oQueMuda: Civil police, military police and firefighters would have a national minimum salary.
c2499794.quemAfeta: Police officers, firefighters and state governments.
c2499794.porQueImporta: Today each state sets the pay of its police and firefighters. Under the PEC, there would be a national floor for civil and military police and firefighters, paid by the states.

c2435133.titulo: Creates a special regime to rebuild Rio Grande do Sul
c2435133.oQueMuda:
Emergency regime: while the calamity lasts, the federal government could hire temporary staff and contract works and purchases in a simplified way, and calamity spending would be exempt from Fiscal Responsibility Law and fiscal framework limits.
State debt: Rio Grande do Sul's debt payments to the federal government would be suspended during the calamity.
Deduction: state spending on reconstruction and support for families could be deducted from its federal debt, after validation by the Finance Ministry.
c2435133.quemAfeta: Residents and the government of Rio Grande do Sul, and the federal government.
c2435133.porQueImporta: In 2024, floods hit most municipalities in Rio Grande do Sul. That same year, a complementary law suspended the state's debt payments to the federal government for 3 years; the PEC would go further, allowing reconstruction spending to be deducted from the debt.

c2231888.titulo: Guarantees income for families in poverty
c2231888.oQueMuda: Adds to the Constitution an anti-poverty policy with cash transfers to poor families.
c2231888.quemAfeta: Families in poverty and extreme poverty.
c2231888.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution provides a family basic income for vulnerable people, and Bolsa Família exists by law. Under the PEC, a cash-transfer policy for poor families would be detailed in the Constitution.

s8796486.titulo: Allows a regional bonus for admission to public higher education
s8796486.oQueMuda: Public institutions could give a bonus to applicants from poorer regions.
s8796486.porQueImporta: Today admission to public universities has social and racial quotas, with no regional bonus. Under the PEC, they could give bonuses to candidates from poorer regions.

c1738895.titulo: Sets rules and deadlines for creating municipalities
c1738895.oQueMuda: Sets procedures and timing for creating, merging or splitting municipalities.
c1738895.quemAfeta: Residents of districts and state governments.
c1738895.porQueImporta: Today creating or splitting municipalities depends on a federal law that has never been passed. Under the PEC, there would be defined rules and deadlines for it.

c598858.titulo: Adds maritime policing to military police duties
c598858.oQueMuda: Military police would also patrol coastal waters.
c598858.porQueImporta: Today maritime policing is done by the Navy and the Federal Police. Under the PEC, state military police would also police the sea.

c263327.oQueMuda: Changes rules on union registration, collective bargaining and worker representation.
c263327.porQueImporta: Today there can only be one union per profession in each city, registered with the Ministry of Labor. Under the PEC, the rules on registration, collective bargaining and representation would change.

c277153.titulo: Ends the single-union rule and creates a bargaining fee
c277153.oQueMuda: Allows more than one union per category, creates a collective bargaining fee and workplace representation.
c277153.porQueImporta: Today there can only be one union per profession in each city. Under the PEC, there could be more than one, a contribution tied to collective bargaining would be created, and there would be workplace representatives.

c292210.titulo: Renames collective labor disputes as 'normative actions'
c292210.oQueMuda: Collective cases in the Labor Courts would be called normative actions, filed by unions.
c292210.porQueImporta: Today collective labor disputes reach the courts through a 'dissídio coletivo', which since 2004 requires agreement between the parties. Under the PEC, it would become a 'normative action' filed by unions.

c489621.titulo: Gives states back the power to create municipalities
c489621.oQueMuda: States could again make laws on creating, merging and splitting municipalities.
c489621.quemAfeta: Residents of districts seeking independence and state governments.
c489621.porQueImporta: Today creating or splitting municipalities depends on a federal law that has never been passed, and almost no towns have been created since 1996. Under the PEC, states could again do this by state law.

c502631.titulo: Changes rules for creating or merging municipalities
c502631.oQueMuda: Creating, merging or splitting municipalities would have to preserve historical and cultural unity and happen up to 12 months before elections.
c502631.quemAfeta: Residents of areas seeking to become a municipality.
c502631.porQueImporta: Today creating or splitting municipalities depends on a federal law that has never been passed. Under the PEC, the process would have to preserve historical and cultural unity and occur up to 12 months before elections.

c2162097.titulo: Bars judges from cases tied to whoever appointed them
c2162097.oQueMuda: Judges could not take part in cases involving the president or governor who appointed them.
c2162097.quemAfeta: Judges and justices appointed by the executive.
c2162097.porQueImporta: Today justices and appellate judges appointed by the president or governors can rule on cases involving those officials. Under the PEC, they would be barred from those cases.

c2233327.titulo: Makes it easier to change municipal borders
c2233327.oQueMuda: Sets rules to split, merge or redraw municipal borders without creating new cities.
c2233327.quemAfeta: Residents of border areas and city governments.
c2233327.porQueImporta: Today changing boundaries between municipalities follows the same rule as creating towns, which depends on a federal law never passed. Under the PEC, there would be specific rules for changing borders without creating new towns.

s8809676.titulo: Sends part of the education payroll contribution to public daycare
s8809676.oQueMuda: States and cities would have to use a share of the education payroll contribution to open and run daycare centers.
s8809676.quemAfeta: Young children, families and city governments.
s8809676.porQueImporta: Today the salário-educação, a contribution paid by companies, funds basic education with no mandatory share for daycare. Under the PEC, states and municipalities would have to spend part of it on daycare.

c508965.titulo: Transfers federal seaside land to states, cities and occupants
c508965.oQueMuda:
End of 'navy lands': the Constitution no longer says this coastal strip belongs to the federal government.
Stays federal: areas used by federal services, federal environmental units and unoccupied areas. Unoccupied areas requested for urban expansion may pass to the municipality.
Goes to states and municipalities, free of charge: areas where their services operate.
Goes to occupants: those registered with the federal government become owners; unregistered occupants too, if they have occupied the area for at least 5 years and prove good faith. Free for social housing and paid in other cases. The text does not define which areas count as social housing.
Fees: the annual fee, occupation fee and transfer fee (laudêmio) end. Registered occupants get what they paid in fees over the last 5 years deducted. The federal government has up to 2 years to carry out the transfers.
c508965.quemAfeta: Residents and businesses on navy lands, states, municipalities and the federal government.
c508965.porQueImporta: Today 'navy lands', a 33-meter strip measured from the average high-tide line of 1831, belong to the federal government, and occupants pay it fees. The PEC does not change the article of the Constitution that defines beaches as federal property.
c508965.nota: The PEC does not change the 1988 law that guarantees free access to beaches. The debate is about access to them, because the land right behind the sand would have private owners.

s8540294.titulo: Changes rules for active-duty military running for office
s8540294.oQueMuda: Members of the armed forces who want to run would have to move to the reserve when registering as candidates.
s8540294.porQueImporta: Today active-duty military with more than 10 years of service only move to the reserve if elected. Under the PEC, they would have to move to the reserve when registering as candidates.

c2487390.titulo: Expands audit court oversight of multinational companies with federal stakes
c2487390.oQueMuda: Congress and the federal audit court (TCU) could audit supranational companies in which the federal government has a stake.
c2487390.porQueImporta: Today binational companies such as Itaipu are not audited by the Federal Audit Court, since they are governed by treaty. Under the PEC, Congress and the court could audit their accounts.

s8808203.titulo: Requires anyone summoned to appear before inquiry committees
s8808203.oQueMuda: Citizens and officials summoned by parliamentary inquiry committees would have to appear.
s8808203.quemAfeta: People summoned by parliamentary inquiry committees.
s8808203.porQueImporta: Today the Supreme Court allows suspects to skip inquiry hearings or remain silent. Under the PEC, anyone summoned would be required to appear.

c348335.titulo: Ties pension increases to the minimum wage
c348335.oQueMuda: Social security benefits would get the same increase as the minimum wage, and the cap would rise to ten minimum wages.
c348335.quemAfeta: Retirees and pensioners of the national social security system (INSS).
c348335.porQueImporta: Today the minimum wage gets real increases, while INSS benefits above the minimum are only adjusted for inflation; the INSS ceiling is just over 5 minimum wages. Under the PEC, all would get the minimum wage raise and the ceiling would rise to 10 minimum wages.

c1738778.titulo: Exempts police hazard bonuses from taxes
c1738778.oQueMuda: Hazard and life-risk bonuses paid to police would not be taxed.
c1738778.porQueImporta: Today police hazard bonuses and allowances pay income tax like the rest of the salary. Under the PEC, these amounts would be tax-exempt.

c2018276.titulo: Sets priority and urgency criteria in health care
c2018276.oQueMuda: Keeps the universal right to health but sets criteria to define priorities and emergencies.
c2018276.quemAfeta: Patients of the public health system (SUS).
c2018276.porQueImporta: Today the public health system must serve everyone, and the order of care follows each service's rules. Under the PEC, the Constitution would set priority and urgency criteria.

c2189436.titulo: Lists academic freedom among the fundamental rights
c2189436.oQueMuda: Adds 'teaching' (academic freedom) to the right to free intellectual, artistic and scientific expression. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2189436.porQueImporta: The Constitution already guarantees freedom to teach and research among the principles of education; the change repeats this guarantee in the list of fundamental rights.

c2307037.titulo: Adds basic income to the social rights
c2307037.oQueMuda: States that every Brazilian with insufficient income has the right to a basic income, with amount and rules set by law. On its own, it does not create the benefit: a law is needed.
c2307037.quemAfeta: Low-income people and the federal government.
c2307037.porQueImporta: A similar rule, on family basic income, was already added to the Constitution in 2021 (Amendment 114); this proposal was filed before that.

c1738617.titulo: Ends the stay-on bonus for civil servants
c1738617.oQueMuda: Civil servants who can already retire but keep working would stop receiving this bonus.
c1738617.porQueImporta: Today civil servants who can already retire but keep working receive a bonus equal to their pension contribution. Under the PEC, this bonus would end.

c2057623.titulo: Changes the share of funds sent to the BNDES
c2057623.oQueMuda: Changes the share of PIS/PASEP money passed to the national development bank (BNDES) for loans.
c2057623.quemAfeta: The BNDES and companies that borrow from it.
c2057623.porQueImporta: Today at least 28% of PIS/Pasep money goes to BNDES to finance development, and the rest helps pay unemployment insurance and the wage bonus. Under the PEC, this share would change.

c2233640.titulo: Allows city fire brigades with volunteers
c2233640.oQueMuda: Cities could create fire brigades through agreements with volunteer firefighters.
c2233640.porQueImporta: Today firefighting is a state service, and many towns have no fire station. Under the PEC, municipalities could create fire brigades with volunteers through agreements.

c2344523.titulo: Cuts property tax (IPTU) on land with native vegetation
c2344523.oQueMuda: The urban property tax would have environmental criteria, and areas with native vegetation would be tax-free.
c2344523.quemAfeta: Owners of urban property with preserved woodland and city governments.
c2344523.porQueImporta: Today urban property tax is charged on the whole lot, including wooded areas. Under the PEC, native-vegetation areas would be exempt, and city governments would not collect tax on them.

c2220682.titulo: Bans extra perks on top public salaries
c2220682.oQueMuda: Officials earning more than a quarter of a Supreme Court justice's salary could not receive add-ons without express provision.
c2220682.quemAfeta: Civil servants and officials with high salaries.
c2220682.porQueImporta: Today allowances and bonuses let some civil servants receive more than the salary cap. Under the PEC, those earning more than a quarter of the cap could not receive extras without express legal provision.

c458500.titulo: Merges civil and military police and demilitarizes firefighters
c458500.oQueMuda: Creates a single state police force replacing civil and military police and makes firefighters civilian.
c458500.quemAfeta: Police officers, firefighters and municipal guards.
c458500.porQueImporta: Today each state has a Military Police, a Civil Police and a Military Fire Brigade. Under the PEC, the police would merge into a single civilian force, and firefighters would no longer be military.

c2165018.titulo: Bans recent party membership for electoral court members
c2165018.oQueMuda: People serving in the electoral courts could not have been party members in the previous two years.
c2165018.quemAfeta: Judges and lawyers who sit on electoral courts.
c2165018.porQueImporta: Today lawyers appointed to electoral courts need not have been without party membership for a minimum period. Under the PEC, those affiliated in the previous two years could not serve.

c2221671.oQueMuda: Postal services could be run by private companies under authorization or concession.
c2221671.quemAfeta: The postal service (Correios), its employees and users.
c2221671.porQueImporta: Today letter delivery is a federal monopoly, run by Correios. Under the PEC, private companies could provide this service through authorization or concession.

c2139404.titulo: Caps interest payments on the public debt
c2139404.oQueMuda: Sets a limit on what the federal government spends on interest and debt charges.
c2139404.quemAfeta: The federal government and the country's creditors.
c2139404.porQueImporta: Today there is no limit on federal spending on debt interest, one of the largest budget items. Under the PEC, there would be a cap on this spending.

c2181063.titulo: Reduces the number of senators and deputies
c2181063.oQueMuda: Reduces the number of senators, federal deputies and state deputies.
c2181063.porQueImporta: Today there are 81 senators (3 per state) and 513 federal deputies. Under the PEC, these numbers would fall, as would the number of state deputies.

c110958.titulo: Establishes full freedom of association for unions
c110958.oQueMuda: Changes union organization rules, allowing more freedom to create organizations.
c110958.porQueImporta: Today there can only be one union per profession in each city. Under the PEC, workers would be free to create more than one organization.

c423901.titulo: Gives the Labor Courts power to try labor crimes
c423901.oQueMuda: Crimes such as slave labor and crimes against labor organization would be tried by the Labor Courts.
c423901.quemAfeta: Workers, employers and the federal courts.
c423901.porQueImporta: Today crimes such as slave labor are tried by federal courts. Under the PEC, they would move to the Labor Courts.

c2487818.titulo: Allows summoning the Central Bank president
c2487818.oQueMuda: The Central Bank president could be summoned by the Chamber, the Senate or their committees.
c2487818.porQueImporta: Today the Central Bank president can be invited by Congress, but not summoned. Under the PEC, he or she would be required to appear when summoned.

c2487249.titulo: Guarantees lawyers the right to argue in person or online
c2487249.oQueMuda: Strengthens the lawyer's role and guarantees the right to speak at hearings, in person or online.
c2487249.porQueImporta: Today a lawyer's right to speak at a hearing depends on the type of case and each court's rules, and virtual hearings do not always allow live speech. Under the PEC, this right would be guaranteed in the Constitution, in person or online.

s8664217.titulo: Makes the Mato Grosso do Sul Pantanal national heritage
s8664217.oQueMuda: The Pantanal of Mato Grosso do Sul would be added to the national heritage areas.
s8664217.quemAfeta: Residents and producers in the Pantanal.
s8664217.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution lists as national heritage the Amazon, Atlantic Forest, Serra do Mar, Mato Grosso Pantanal and the coastal zone. Under the PEC, the Mato Grosso do Sul Pantanal would be added, with its use conditioned on preservation.

s8771508.titulo: Lowers the new tax on water and sewage
s8771508.oQueMuda: Changes the tax reform to reduce IBS and CBS rates on water and sewage services.
s8771508.porQueImporta: Under the tax reform, sanitation pays the full IBS and CBS rate, while today it pays PIS, Cofins and, in some cases, ISS. Under the PEC, the rate on water and sewage would be reduced.

s7817905.oQueMuda: Children would be a social security priority, with a monthly benefit for those living in poverty.
s7817905.porQueImporta: Today poor families with children receive Bolsa Família, set by law. Under the PEC, there would be a monthly benefit for poor children guaranteed in the Constitution, within social security.

s8403373.titulo: Exempts rare disease medicines from taxes
s8403373.oQueMuda: Medicines to treat rare diseases would be tax-free.
s8403373.quemAfeta: Patients with rare diseases and their families.
s8403373.porQueImporta: Today medicines for rare diseases pay taxes, except for specific exemptions. Under the PEC, they would be free of taxes and contributions, as set by a complementary law.

s8477226.titulo: Requires a National Food Security Plan
s8477226.oQueMuda: The Constitution would require a national plan against hunger and for good nutrition.
s8477226.porQueImporta: Today food is a social right, and fighting hunger is organized through laws and government programs. Under the PEC, the Constitution would require a National Food and Nutrition Security Plan.

s8656750.titulo: Creates the National Climate Emergency Fund
s8656750.oQueMuda: Creates a fund to guarantee money for floods, droughts and other climate disasters.
s8656750.porQueImporta: Today disaster money comes from each year's budget or emergency credits. Under the PEC, there would be a national fund with money reserved for climate emergencies.

s8542259.titulo: Makes possession of any amount of drugs a crime
s8542259.oQueMuda: The Constitution would require the law to treat possession and carrying of drugs without authorization as a crime, in any amount. The text sets no amount to tell users from dealers: the distinction would be made case by case, based on the circumstances. Users would get alternatives to prison and addiction treatment.
s8542259.quemAfeta: Drug users and the justice system.
s8542259.porQueImporta: In 2024 the Supreme Court stopped treating possession of up to 40 grams of marijuana for personal use as a crime and set that amount as a reference to presume someone is a user. Under the PEC, possession of any amount would be a crime again, with no reference amount in the Constitution.
s8542259.nota: The current drug law also separates users from dealers case by case. Ipea studies of that law show that Black defendants are prosecuted for trafficking with smaller amounts than white defendants. Supporters of the PEC say it protects public health and strengthens the fight against trafficking.

c2075449.titulo: Extends maternity leave for premature births
c2075449.oQueMuda: Time the premature baby spends in hospital would not be deducted from maternity leave.
c2075449.quemAfeta: Mothers of premature babies and employers.
c2075449.porQueImporta: Today maternity leave is 120 days and, under a 2020 Supreme Court ruling, only starts after the mother or hospitalized baby is discharged. Under the PEC, this rule would be in the Constitution.

s8792757.titulo: Cuts the workweek to 40 hours and 5 days
s8792757.oQueMuda: The maximum would drop from 44 to 40 hours, over up to 5 days and 8 hours a day, with days off preferably on weekends.
s8792757.porQueImporta: People who work more than 40 hours or six days a week today would work less for the same pay, which the text guarantees. For those going from 44 to 40 hours, the employer's wage cost per hour worked rises about 10%.

c2483164.oQueMuda:
Prime minister: the president would still be directly elected, as head of state, but the government would be led by a prime minister appointed by the president after consulting the majority parties in the Chamber.
Chamber confidence: the Chamber could bring down the government with a censure motion, passed by absolute majority, starting six months after the prime minister takes office.
Dissolution: in a serious political crisis, the president could dissolve the Chamber and call new elections within 60 days.
Mixed-member voting: some federal deputies would be elected by districts and some by party lists.
c2483164.quemAfeta: The whole population and the political system.
c2483164.porQueImporta: Today the elected president is both head of state and head of government, and deputies are elected by proportional vote across the state. In 1993, voters chose presidentialism in a plebiscite.

c2229938.titulo: Makes second-instance rulings final in all cases
c2229938.oQueMuda: Appeals to the Supreme Court and the Superior Court of Justice would no longer exist. Second-instance rulings would become final in every type of case, not just criminal ones, and could only be reviewed through a new action in those courts, called a review action, after the case is closed.
c2229938.quemAfeta: Defendants, all parties to court cases (including civil and tax cases) and the higher courts.
c2229938.porQueImporta: Today, under a 2019 Supreme Court ruling, a sentence only starts once all appeals are exhausted. Under the PEC, it would start after the second-instance ruling, and the same would apply to the end of civil, tax and labor cases.

s1395980.titulo: Allows Congress to summon heads of state companies and agencies
s1395980.oQueMuda: The Chamber, the Senate and committees could summon heads of federal indirect administration bodies.
s1395980.quemAfeta: Heads of state-owned companies, agencies and authorities.
s1395980.porQueImporta: Today Congress can summon ministers, but not heads of state companies and agencies. Under the PEC, it could summon the heads of all federal indirect administration.

c14493.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility to 16
c14493.oQueMuda: Young people from 16 would be tried as adults.
c14493.quemAfeta: Teenagers aged 16 and 17 and the justice system.
c14493.porQueImporta: Today people under 18 are subject to the Child and Adolescent Statute, with at most 3 years of detention. Under the PEC, approved by the Chamber in 2015 and stalled in the Senate, 16- and 17-year-olds would be tried and imprisoned as adults for serious crimes.

c516111.titulo: Changes the process for provisional measures
c516111.oQueMuda: Changes deadlines and review steps for provisional measures (executive decrees) and bans reissuing them.
c516111.porQueImporta: Today a provisional measure is valid for up to 120 days and blocks Congress's agenda after 45. Under the PEC, review deadlines and steps would change, and reissuing provisional measures would be banned.

c786713.titulo: Unifies disability retirement rules for civil servants
c786713.oQueMuda: Sets the same rule for disability retirement and a transition for those who joined the civil service by 2003.
c786713.porQueImporta: Today civil servants who joined by 2003 and retire for disability may have different rules depending on date and cause. Under the PEC, there would be a single rule for this group.

c946494.oQueMuda: The government would have to carry out deputies' and senators' individual budget amendments.
c946494.quemAfeta: Legislators, cities and the federal government.
c946494.porQueImporta: In force since 2015: the government must pay individual budget amendments from deputies and senators.

c1526944.titulo: Creates a special regime to pay overdue court debts
c1526944.oQueMuda: Sets rules for paying governments' court-ordered debts and a special regime for overdue cases.
c1526944.quemAfeta: People and companies that won lawsuits against governments.
c1526944.porQueImporta: Governments accumulate court-ordered debts they do not pay on time. Under the PEC, there would be payment rules and a special regime to clear arrears.

c2209349.titulo: Makes state caucus budget amendments mandatory
c2209349.oQueMuda: The government would have to carry out the collective budget amendments of state caucuses.
c2209349.quemAfeta: Legislators, states and the federal government.
c2209349.porQueImporta: Since 2019, the government must also pay state caucus budget amendments, a rule added to the Constitution through another PEC.

c606656.titulo: Adds human rights to the principles of the economy
c606656.oQueMuda: Adds 'respect for human rights' to the principles of the economy and describes the system as 'humanist capitalism'. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c606656.quemAfeta: Companies, governments and those who make economic laws.
c606656.porQueImporta: Today the principles of the economic order include sovereignty, free competition, consumer and environmental protection, but not human rights. Under the PEC, respect for human rights would be added.

s8735431.titulo: Changes rules for inquiries opened by courts
s8735431.oQueMuda: Sets when courts can open inquiries into crimes at their premises or against their members.
s8735431.quemAfeta: Courts, especially the Supreme Court, and people under investigation.
s8735431.porQueImporta: Since 2019, the Supreme Court has run investigations it opened itself, such as the fake news inquiry, based on its internal rules. Under the PEC, the Constitution would limit when courts can open such investigations.

s8735562.titulo: Creates disciplinary complaints against Supreme Court justices
s8735562.oQueMuda: Supreme Court justices could face disciplinary complaints for conduct outside impeachable offenses.
s8735562.porQueImporta: Today Supreme Court justices are not overseen by the CNJ and can only be removed by impeachment in the Senate. Under the PEC, they could face disciplinary complaints.

s8739428.titulo: Changes the makeup of the Electoral Court and removes Supreme Court justices from it
s8739428.oQueMuda: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) would have 7 members with 2-year terms: 2 justices of the Superior Court of Justice (STJ), 1 lawyer nominated by the Bar Association and appointed by the president, 2 chosen by the Chamber and 2 by the Senate.
s8739428.quemAfeta: The Electoral Court, the Supreme Court, Congress and voters.
s8739428.porQueImporta: Today the Electoral Court has 7 members: 3 Supreme Court justices, 2 STJ justices and 2 lawyers appointed by the president. Under the PEC, the Supreme Court justices would leave, and the Chamber and Senate would choose 4 of the 7 members.

s8749240.titulo: Changes rules for approving and paying budget amendments
s8749240.oQueMuda: Creates criteria for approving and paying legislators' amendments to budget laws.
s8749240.porQueImporta: Today budget amendments total tens of billions of reais a year, and some, such as direct transfers, have little transparency. Under the PEC, there would be criteria for approving and paying these amendments.

s8772231.titulo: Creates technical criteria for choosing federal audit court ministers
s8772231.oQueMuda: Requires technical criteria and bans appointing recent politicians and relatives to the Federal Court of Accounts (TCU).
s8772231.porQueImporta: Today of the 9 Federal Audit Court ministers, 6 are chosen by Congress and 3 by the president, and many were politicians. Under the PEC, there would be technical criteria, and recent politicians and relatives of officials would be barred.

s8776422.titulo: Creates gender parity in judges' promotions
s8776422.oQueMuda: Guarantees quotas for women in promoting judges to appeals courts.
s8776422.porQueImporta: Since 2023 a CNJ resolution requires alternating lists of men and women in merit-based promotions. Under the PEC, gender parity in judicial promotion would be in the Constitution.

s8780865.titulo: Removes from jury trial killings attributed to gangs, militias and criminal groups
s8780865.oQueMuda: Intentional crimes against life, such as homicide, committed by members of a criminal association, militia or criminal organization would be decided by a single judge rather than a jury of citizens.
s8780865.quemAfeta: Defendants accused of these crimes, victims and their families, jurors and criminal judges.
s8780865.porQueImporta: Today homicides and other intentional crimes against life are tried by a citizen jury, a constitutional guarantee. Under the PEC, when the defendant belongs to a criminal association (by law, a group of three or more people), militia or criminal organization, the trial would be decided by a judge.

c2428346.titulo: Adds care to the social rights
c2428346.oQueMuda: Adds 'care' (for older people, children, people with disabilities and other dependents) to the list of social rights. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2428346.quemAfeta: People who need care, their caregivers and governments.
c2428346.porQueImporta: Since 2024 there has been a National Care Policy, created by law. Under the PEC, care would join the Constitution's list of social rights.

c348719.titulo: Tax reform with a financial transactions tax
c348719.oQueMuda: Creates selective taxes, a financial transactions tax of up to 0.76%, and ends the CSLL and the large fortunes tax.
c348719.quemAfeta: All taxpayers, states and the federal government.
c348719.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, there would be a financial transactions tax of up to 0.76%, similar to the old CPMF, and the CSLL and the wealth tax, which was never created, would be abolished.

c355705.titulo: Increases the share of vehicle tax (IPVA) kept by cities
c355705.oQueMuda: Cities would get a bigger share of the IPVA from vehicles registered in their territory.
c355705.porQueImporta: Today IPVA is split half and half between the state and the city where the vehicle is registered. Under the PEC, cities' share would rise and states' would fall.

c357691.oQueMuda: No taxes could be created on producing and selling essential foods.
c357691.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, no government could tax the production and sale of basic foods. The 2023 tax reform already zeroed taxes on a national basic food basket.

c360826.titulo: Cuts the IPI tax on products made from recycled material
c360826.oQueMuda: Manufactured goods using recycled material would pay less IPI.
c360826.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, products made with recycled materials would pay less IPI; IPI is shared with states and municipalities, which would receive less.

c370136.titulo: Exempts people with disabilities from income and property taxes
c370136.oQueMuda: People with disabilities would not pay taxes on their income or on buying and selling goods for their own use.
c370136.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, people with disabilities would pay no income tax nor taxes on buying and selling goods for their own use, whatever their income.

c370580.titulo: Rewards states and cities with conservation areas
c370580.oQueMuda: Up to 0.5% of participation fund transfers would go to states and cities with environmental conservation areas.
c370580.quemAfeta: States and cities with protected areas.
c370580.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, up to 0.5% of the participation funds would go to states and municipalities with conservation areas; the others would receive that much less.

c370778.titulo: Creates a rural support fund from federal transfers
c370778.oQueMuda: 3% of federal revenue sent to cities would go to a special fund supporting agriculture.
c370778.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, 3% of federal revenue transferred to municipalities would go to a fund supporting the rural sector, and city governments could not use that money elsewhere.

c383286.titulo: Defines where money from new federal taxes goes
c383286.oQueMuda: Sets where the revenue from any new or increased federal tax would go.
c383286.porQueImporta: Today revenue from new federal taxes goes into the general federal treasury. Under the PEC, the Constitution would set where money from any new or increased tax goes.

c384058.titulo: Changes compensation to states for exports
c384058.oQueMuda: Changes the compensation the federal government pays states for losses from tax exemptions on exports.
c384058.porQueImporta: Since 1996, exports pay no ICMS, and the federal government compensates part of states' losses. Under the PEC, the compensation rules would change.

c384059.titulo: Bans social contributions on government revenue
c384059.oQueMuda: The federal government, states, the Federal District, municipalities and public agencies would no longer pay social contributions on revenue, such as PIS/Pasep.
c384059.quemAfeta: All levels of government and the social security system, which receives these contributions.
c384059.porQueImporta: Today governments and public bodies pay PIS/Pasep on their revenue. Under the PEC, they would be exempt from these contributions, which fund social security.

c384060.titulo: Splits sales tax on online purchases between states
c384060.oQueMuda: In online sales between states, part of the ICMS would go to the buyer's state.
c384060.porQueImporta: Since 2015, an amendment splits ICMS on online sales between the seller's state and the buyer's state. This 2008 PEC proposed a similar rule.

c384544.titulo: Cuts taxes on machinery and equipment
c384544.oQueMuda: Capital goods, such as industrial machines, would be exempt from IPI and ICMS.
c384544.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, industrial and farm machinery would pay no IPI or ICMS; the federal, state and municipal governments would not collect these amounts.

c384954.titulo: Creates a federal VAT by merging contributions
c384954.oQueMuda: Combines Cofins, PIS and Cide into a value-added tax and folds the CSLL into corporate income tax.
c384954.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, Cofins, PIS and Cide would become a single federal value-added tax, and CSLL would be merged into corporate income tax. The 2023 reform created the CBS, which replaces PIS and Cofins.

c389981.oQueMuda: Creates a minimum tax on financial transactions and transfers.
c389981.quemAfeta: Everyone who moves money through banks.
c389981.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, a tax on financial transactions would be created, like the CPMF in force from 1997 to 2007, with an exemption band set by law.

c391353.oQueMuda: Employers would stop paying social contributions on salaries.
c391353.porQueImporta: Today companies generally pay 20% of payroll to social security. Under the PEC, this contribution would end, and social security would lose this source.

c440021.titulo: Creates a single tax on goods and services
c440021.oQueMuda: Creates a non-cumulative tax on transactions with goods or services, including imports.
c440021.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, a non-cumulative tax on goods and services, including imports, would be created. The 2023 reform adopted a similar model with IBS and CBS.

c604132.titulo: Creates a welfare benefit for crime victims
c604132.oQueMuda: Crime victims would be entitled to a social assistance benefit.
c604132.porQueImporta: Today there is no social assistance benefit specifically for crime victims. Under the PEC, they would be entitled to one.

c1229857.titulo: Ends the benefit for prisoners' families
c1229857.oQueMuda: The benefit paid to prisoners' dependents would be removed from social security.
c1229857.porQueImporta: Today the prisoner's family benefit is paid to dependents of low-income prisoners who contributed to INSS. Under the PEC, this benefit would cease to exist.

c1712462.titulo: Gives a monthly benefit to dependents of homicide victims
c1712462.oQueMuda: Dependents of people who were murdered would receive one minimum wage a month.
c1712462.porQueImporta: Today the one-minimum-wage assistance benefit (BPC) is paid to low-income older people and people with disabilities. Under the PEC, dependents of homicide victims would also be entitled.

c2113815.titulo: Swaps the prisoners' family benefit for one for victims' families
c2113815.oQueMuda: Ends the benefit for prisoners' families and gives one minimum wage a month to dependents of homicide victims.
c2113815.quemAfeta: Families of prisoners and of homicide victims.
c2113815.porQueImporta: Today the prisoner's family benefit is paid to dependents of low-income prisoners. Under the PEC, it would end, and dependents of homicide victims would receive one minimum wage per month.

c2140762.titulo: Ties the prisoners' family benefit to the prisoner working
c2140762.oQueMuda: The benefit for dependents would only be paid if the convicted prisoner works.
c2140762.porQueImporta: Today the prisoner's family benefit is paid to dependents of low-income prisoners whether or not they work. Under the PEC, it would only be paid if the prisoner works.

c2474283.oQueMuda: Changes rules on super-salaries, the BPC disability and elderly benefit, the Fundeb education fund and the wage bonus, and extends the DRU to 2032.
c2474283.quemAfeta: Civil servants, BPC and wage bonus recipients, and basic education.
c2474283.porQueImporta: This text was voted together with PEC 31/2007 and became a constitutional amendment in December 2024: it changed rules on very high salaries, BPC, Fundeb and the wage bonus, and extended the DRU until 2032.

c14638.titulo: Cuts the workweek from 44 to 30 hours
c14638.oQueMuda: The workweek would drop one hour a year down to 30 hours, with agreements allowing up to 40.
c14638.porQueImporta: People who work more than 30 hours would work less for the same pay. For those going from 44 to 30 hours, the employer's wage cost per hour worked rises about 47%.

c378195.titulo: Ties pension increases to the minimum wage
c378195.oQueMuda: The minimum wage would be the benchmark for adjusting social security benefits and their real value.
c378195.quemAfeta: Retirees and pensioners of the national social security system (INSS).
c378195.porQueImporta: Today the minimum wage gets real increases, while INSS benefits above the minimum are only adjusted for inflation. Under the PEC, the minimum wage would be the reference for adjusting all benefits.

c539564.titulo: Guarantees pensions the same increase as the minimum wage
c539564.oQueMuda: No social security benefit could rise less than the minimum wage, and current ones would be updated.
c539564.quemAfeta: Retirees and pensioners of the national social security system.
c539564.porQueImporta: Today the minimum wage gets real increases, while INSS benefits above the minimum are only adjusted for inflation. Under the PEC, no benefit would get a smaller raise than the minimum wage, and current ones would be recalculated.

c543447.titulo: Protects the real value of pensions
c543447.oQueMuda: Pensions and social security benefits would be guaranteed to keep their purchasing power.
c543447.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution already guarantees that INSS benefits keep their real value, adjusted for inflation. Under the PEC, this guarantee would be reinforced.

c1228532.titulo: Bans moving to lighter prison regimes for heinous crimes and trafficking
c1228532.oQueMuda: People convicted of torture, drug trafficking, terrorism and heinous crimes would serve the whole sentence in the same regime.
c1228532.quemAfeta: People convicted of these crimes and the prison system.
c1228532.porQueImporta: Today people convicted of heinous crimes and trafficking can move to lighter regimes after serving 40% to 70% of the sentence; in 2006 the Supreme Court struck down a rule banning this. Under the PEC, they would serve the whole sentence in the same regime.

c2155899.titulo: Toughens sentences for heinous crimes against military and police
c2155899.oQueMuda: Heinous crimes against military personnel, police and their families would have harsher sentencing rules.
c2155899.quemAfeta: Security agents, their families and convicts.
c2155899.porQueImporta: Since 2015 the law has treated the killing of police and military officers on duty, or of their relatives because of their role, as a heinous crime. Under the PEC, these crimes would have even stricter sentencing rules.

s8635009.oQueMuda: Changes the bodies and powers of federal and state military courts.
s8635009.quemAfeta: Military personnel and the military courts.
s8635009.porQueImporta: Today military courts try military crimes; since 2017, crimes by military personnel against civilians in certain missions also go to them. Under the PEC, the bodies and powers of these courts would change, federally and in the states.

c336945.titulo: Allows municipal guards in state capitals to protect people
c336945.oQueMuda: State capitals could have guards to protect people and private property, alongside the military police.
c336945.quemAfeta: Municipal guards and residents of capitals.
c336945.porQueImporta: Today municipal guards protect city property, services and facilities. Under the PEC, in state capitals, they could also protect people and private property, alongside the military police.

c528631.titulo: Limits politicians' raises to the minimum wage increase
c528631.oQueMuda: Salaries of legislators, executives and listed officials could not rise more than the minimum wage.
c528631.porQueImporta: Today politicians' salaries are raised by law or decree, without a fixed index. Under the PEC, they could not rise faster than the minimum wage.

c578465.oQueMuda: Creates a civil police in cities and redefines the military police's duties.
c578465.porQueImporta: Today criminal investigation belongs to the state Civil Police. Under the PEC, municipalities would have their own civil police, and military police duties would be redefined.

c2086167.oQueMuda: Cities could have police for patrolling and public order, using municipal guards.
c2086167.porQueImporta: Today municipal guards protect city property and services and do not patrol. Under the PEC, municipalities could have police forces to patrol, using existing guards.

c2120463.titulo: Freezes elected officials' salaries for 5 years
c2120463.oQueMuda: Salaries of people holding elected office could not rise for five years.
c2120463.porQueImporta: Today elected politicians' salaries can be raised by law each legislature. Under the PEC, they would be frozen for five years.

c2166332.titulo: Adds municipal police to public safety
c2166332.oQueMuda: Municipal police forces would become part of the public safety bodies.
c2166332.porQueImporta: Today the list of public security bodies in the Constitution does not include municipal police. Under the PEC, they would be added.

c2174544.titulo: Adds municipal guards to public safety
c2174544.oQueMuda: Municipal guards would officially become part of the public safety bodies.
c2174544.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution allows municipal guards to protect city property and services, outside the list of public security bodies. Under the PEC, they would be added to that list.

c2227277.titulo: Requires cities over 20,000 people to have a municipal guard
c2227277.oQueMuda: Every city with 20,000 or more residents would have to create a municipal guard.
c2227277.porQueImporta: Today each municipality decides whether to create a municipal guard. Under the PEC, all with 20,000 or more residents would have to create and maintain one.

c2314519.titulo: Requires reinvesting concession money in transport
c2314519.oQueMuda: At least 70% of what is paid for transport concessions would have to be reinvested in the sector.
c2314519.quemAfeta: Users of highways, ports and railways, and the government.
c2314519.porQueImporta: Today money paid by companies that win concessions for highways, ports and railways goes into the general federal treasury. Under the PEC, at least 70% would have to be reinvested in transport.

c2350490.titulo: Adds culture to the social rights
c2350490.oQueMuda: Adds culture to the Constitution's list of social rights (article 6). On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2350490.quemAfeta: The whole population, artists and governments.
c2350490.porQueImporta: The Constitution already tells the State to guarantee cultural rights; the change also puts culture on the list of social rights.

c597232.titulo: Changes the makeup and oversight of audit courts
c597232.oQueMuda: Changes how audit court members are chosen and places them under the CNJ and CNMP councils.
c597232.porQueImporta: Today Audit Court members are mostly chosen by state legislatures and governors and are not overseen by the CNJ. Under the PEC, the selection would change and they would be overseen by the CNJ and CNMP.

c2478427.titulo: Expands legislators' immunity for what they say
c2478427.oQueMuda: Deputies and senators could not be punished for opinions anywhere, and a Supreme Court justice who disregards this would lose office.
c2478427.porQueImporta: Today lawmakers cannot be punished for opinions, words and votes linked to their mandate, and the Supreme Court has convicted deputies for statements outside that role. Under the PEC, protection would cover statements anywhere, and a justice who disregarded it would lose office.

c2190000.titulo: Increases federal transfers to the FPM
c2190000.oQueMuda: An extra share of federal revenue, including CSLL and Cofins, would go to the Municipal Participation Fund.
c2190000.porQueImporta: Today FPM receives part of income tax and IPI, but nothing from CSLL and Cofins, which fund social security. Under the PEC, part of these contributions would also go to city governments.

c2228314.titulo: Increases the share of federal taxes sent to states and cities
c2228314.oQueMuda: Raises the shares of income tax and IPI revenue passed to states, the Federal District and cities.
c2228314.quemAfeta: States, cities and the federal government.
c2228314.porQueImporta: Today the federal government transfers about half of income tax and IPI revenue to states and municipalities. Under the PEC, this share would increase.

s8759356.titulo: Adds protection of victims to the fundamental rights
s8759356.oQueMuda: States that victims of crimes and public disasters have the right to special protection, as set by law, and bans insufficient protection by the State. On its own, it does not create services or funding: a law is needed.
s8759356.quemAfeta: Victims of crimes and disasters, and the government.
s8759356.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution has no specific article on the rights of victims of crimes and disasters. Under the PEC, this right would be expressly stated, banning insufficient State protection.

s8759452.titulo: Applies the salary cap to allowances too
s8759452.oQueMuda: The public sector salary cap would also apply to allowances and compensation payments.
s8759452.quemAfeta: Civil servants and officials with high salaries.
s8759452.porQueImporta: Today compensation allowances do not count toward the salary cap, allowing payments above it. Under the PEC, they would count.

c125854.titulo: Expands freedom of association for unions
c125854.oQueMuda: Changes rules on union organization and union contributions.
c125854.porQueImporta: Today there can only be one union per profession in each city. Under the PEC, union organization and contribution rules would change.

c2350568.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for public bank loans abroad
c2350568.oQueMuda: Loans by the BNDES and other federal banks for projects abroad would depend on Congress.
c2350568.quemAfeta: Public banks and the federal government.
c2350568.porQueImporta: Today BNDES and other public banks can finance works abroad without congressional approval. Under the PEC, these loans would depend on lawmakers' approval.

c2362646.titulo: Allows direct transfers of caucus amendments to states and cities
c2362646.oQueMuda: Individual and caucus budget amendments could be transferred directly, without formal agreements.
