c2362646.porQueImporta: Since 2019 direct transfers of budget amendments to states and municipalities, without agreements, have existed (the so-called 'Pix amendments'). This PEC sought to expand that model; in 2024 the Supreme Court began requiring more transparency on these transfers.

c2291133.titulo: Bans active-duty military from civilian government posts
c2291133.oQueMuda: Active-duty military could not hold civilian posts in public administration.
c2291133.porQueImporta: Today active-duty military personnel can hold civilian posts in public administration, such as ministries and departments. Under the PEC, this would be banned.

c2238418.titulo: Requires collective Supreme Court decisions on injunctions
c2238418.oQueMuda: Injunctions in constitutional challenges would have to be decided by more than one justice.
c2238418.porQueImporta: Today a single Supreme Court justice can suspend a law with a provisional ruling. Under the PEC, these rulings would require more than one justice.

c2336481.titulo: Allows direct election of the leadership of the largest state courts
c2336481.oQueMuda: In state Courts of Justice with more than 170 appellate judges, all of them would vote by secret ballot to choose the leadership, for 2-year terms with only one re-election.
c2336481.quemAfeta: Appellate judges in the largest state courts, such as São Paulo's.
c2336481.porQueImporta: Already in force: in state Courts of Justice with more than 170 appellate judges, such as São Paulo's, all of them vote to choose the leadership, for 2-year terms with one re-election.

c543252.titulo: Guarantees the right to life from conception
c543252.oQueMuda: The Constitution would state that the right to life is inviolable from conception.
c543252.porQueImporta: Today abortion is allowed in Brazil in cases of rape, risk to the mother's life and fetal anencephaly, rules set by the Penal Code and a Supreme Court ruling. Under the PEC, the Constitution, which ranks above those rules, would say the right to life is inviolable from conception.

c567421.titulo: Requires a referendum to sell control of state-owned companies
c567421.oQueMuda: Selling control of state-owned companies would require approval by voters in a referendum.
c567421.porQueImporta: Today selling control of a state company depends on a law passed by Congress. Under the PEC, it would also depend on approval by the public in a referendum.

c1672707.titulo: Bans provisional measures that reduce labor rights
c1672707.oQueMuda: The President could not issue a provisional measure (executive decree) to reduce workers' rights.
c1672707.porQueImporta: Today the president can issue provisional measures on labor rights, as happened during the pandemic. Under the PEC, measures reducing these rights would be banned.

c2211748.titulo: Adds social workers, psychologists and nutritionists to schools
c2211748.oQueMuda: Public and private schools would have these professionals.
c2211748.porQueImporta: Since 2019 a law has required psychologists and social workers in public school systems. Under the PEC, public and private schools would also need nutritionists, based on the Constitution.

c2186256.titulo: Bans provisional measures on labor and pensions
c2186256.oQueMuda: The President could not issue a provisional measure (executive decree) on labor or pension law.
c2186256.porQueImporta: Today the president can issue provisional measures on labor and pension law. Under the PEC, changes in these areas could only be made by laws passed by Congress.

s7833783.titulo: Abolishes public funds not confirmed by law
s7833783.oQueMuda: Public funds would require a complementary law, and existing ones would be abolished if not ratified.
s7833783.quemAfeta: The government and areas financed by funds.
s7833783.porQueImporta: Today there are hundreds of public funds created by law, with money reserved for specific purposes. Under the PEC, each fund would need confirmation by complementary law or be abolished, and idle money could go to other spending.

s8136536.titulo: Makes IBGE, Inep and evaluation bodies permanent institutions
s8136536.oQueMuda: Statistics and education evaluation bodies would be permanent, with rules for choosing their heads.
s8136536.porQueImporta: Today IBGE and Inep are bodies created by law, and their heads are freely chosen by the government. Under the PEC, they would be permanent institutions, with rules for choosing their heads.

s8743101.titulo: Allows summoning regulatory agencies to Congress
s8743101.oQueMuda: Heads of regulatory agencies and other federal bodies could be summoned to explain themselves.
s8743101.quemAfeta: Agencies such as Anatel, Aneel and ANS.
s8743101.porQueImporta: Today Congress can summon ministers but not heads of regulatory agencies. Under the PEC, they would also have to appear when summoned.

c591185.titulo: Simplifies pension contributions for waste pickers
c591185.oQueMuda: Waste pickers who work as a family would contribute to social security as special insured workers.
c591185.porQueImporta: Today waste pickers contribute to INSS as self-employed workers or micro-entrepreneurs. Under the PEC, those who work as a family would contribute as 'special insured persons', like family farmers, paying on what they sell.

s7740538.oQueMuda: Sets conditions and personal requirements for holding appointed posts and positions of trust.
s7740538.quemAfeta: Holders of appointed posts and governments.
s7740538.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution requires that some positions of trust be held by career civil servants, without other personal requirements. Under the PEC, there would be requirements for holding appointed posts and positions of trust.

c1732943.titulo: Sets a deadline for Congress to rule on the President's accounts
c1732943.oQueMuda: Congress would have a deadline to rule on the presidential accounts, or the head of Congress would commit an impeachable offense.
c1732943.porQueImporta: Today there is no deadline for Congress to rule on the president's accounts, and several went years without a ruling. Under the PEC, there would be a deadline, and the head of Congress who missed it would commit an impeachable offense.

s7730684.titulo: Creates 8-year terms for Supreme Court justices
s7730684.oQueMuda: Supreme Court justices would serve eight-year terms, with deadlines for nomination and approval.
s7730684.quemAfeta: Current and future Supreme Court justices.
s7730684.porQueImporta: Today Supreme Court justices serve until age 75. Under the PEC, they would have eight-year terms, with deadlines for nomination and approval.

c2448732.titulo: Lets Congress suspend Supreme Court rulings
c2448732.oQueMuda: Injunctions would have to be confirmed by the full court, and Congress could halt certain Supreme Court rulings.
c2448732.porQueImporta: Today Supreme Court rulings can only be superseded by a new law or amendment. Under the PEC, injunctions would have to be confirmed by the full court, and Congress could suspend certain rulings.

c2278136.titulo: Exempts vaccines from taxes in health emergencies
c2278136.oQueMuda: Vaccines and supplies against diseases under a national emergency would be tax-free for three years.
c2278136.quemAfeta: Vaccine makers and the public health system (SUS).
c2278136.porQueImporta: Today vaccines pay taxes, except for specific exemptions. Under the PEC, vaccines and supplies against diseases in a national emergency would be tax-free for three years.

s8730454.titulo: Creates a long-term plan to guide the budget
s8730454.oQueMuda: A plan covering several four-year periods would guide federal spending and investment.
s8730454.porQueImporta: Today federal budget planning uses a four-year plan matching each government. Under the PEC, there would also be a long-term plan spanning several governments.

s8735524.titulo: Lets Congress halt acts of other branches
s8735524.oQueMuda: The legislature could annul executive and judicial rules that exceed their powers.
s8735524.quemAfeta: Congress, the government and the courts.
s8735524.porQueImporta: Today Congress can suspend executive acts that exceed its regulatory power, but not judicial acts. Under the PEC, it could also annul normative acts by courts.

c459294.titulo: Merges civil and military police and demilitarizes firefighters
c459294.oQueMuda: Creates a single state police force replacing civil and military police and makes firefighters civilian.
c459294.quemAfeta: Police officers, firefighters and municipal guards.
c459294.porQueImporta: Today each state has a Military Police, a Civil Police and a Military Fire Brigade. Under the PEC, the police would merge into a single civilian force, and firefighters would no longer be military.

c595169.oQueMuda: Adds new state and city police forces to the public safety bodies.
c595169.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution's list of public security bodies includes federal police, state military and civil police, and prison police. Under the PEC, new state and municipal police forces would be added.

c2212168.titulo: Limits spending on public debt payments
c2212168.oQueMuda: Adds a limit on public debt spending to the spending cap.
c2212168.porQueImporta: Today interest and public debt payments have no constitutional limit. Under the PEC, there would be an annual cap on this expense.

s8705604.titulo: Guarantees lawyers the right to speak at any hearing
s8705604.oQueMuda: Lawyers would have the right to oral argument at any hearing in any court.
s8705604.porQueImporta: Today a lawyer's right to speak at a hearing depends on the type of appeal and each court's rules. Under the PEC, there would be a right to oral argument at any hearing.

s8719180.titulo: Guarantees compensation to police injured on duty
s8719180.oQueMuda: Police and state military personnel would be compensated for accidents or assaults suffered at work.
s8719180.quemAfeta: Police and military personnel of the states and the federal government.
s8719180.porQueImporta: Today police officers injured on duty have rights set by each state's laws. Under the PEC, state police and military personnel would have a guaranteed right to compensation for accidents or assaults at work.

s8720944.titulo: Creates a financing fund for the South region
s8720944.oQueMuda: Creates a constitutional fund for the South, focused on Rio Grande do Sul's recovery after the floods.
s8720944.quemAfeta: Companies and residents of the South.
s8720944.porQueImporta: Today there are constitutional credit funds only for the North, Northeast and Center-West. Under the PEC, the South would also have one, focused on Rio Grande do Sul's recovery.

c2352476.titulo: Pardons and refinances party debts and reserves 30% of funds for Black candidates
c2352476.oQueMuda:
Racial quota: parties must spend 30% of the campaign fund and of the party-fund share used in campaigns on Black and brown candidates, wherever they choose.
Racial quota pardon: what parties spent on Black candidates in past elections counts as compliance, provided they spend the shortfall over the next 4 elections, from 2026.
Fines cancelled: charges, fines and repayments more than 5 years old are cancelled, including those already decided in court, except social security debts.
Refinancing: parties may pay debts in installments with no interest or fines, over up to 15 years (5 years for social security debts).
Public money for fines: parties may use the party fund to pay fines and return irregular funds, including those of unidentified origin.
Pix: donations by Pix no longer require an electoral receipt.
c2352476.quemAfeta: Political parties, Black candidates and taxpayers who fund parties.
c2352476.porQueImporta: In force since August 2024. Before, parties that missed quotas or had irregular accounts could be fined and made to repay money; with the amendment, part of those charges was cancelled, and the party fund, which is public money, can pay the rest.

c1548995.titulo: Shares social contributions with states and cities
c1548995.oQueMuda: Part of CSLL and Cofins revenue would be passed on to states, the Federal District and cities.
c1548995.quemAfeta: States, cities and the federal government.
c1548995.porQueImporta: Today CSLL and Cofins stay with the federal government and fund social security. Under the PEC, part would be passed on to states, the Federal District and municipalities.

c2455515.titulo: Creates a national climate authority, council and fund
c2455515.oQueMuda: Creates the National Climate Change Council, the National Climate Authority and a federally funded fund.
c2455515.porQueImporta: Today climate policy is coordinated by ministries and the Climate Fund, created by law. Under the PEC, the Constitution would provide for a council, a national climate authority and a fund with federal resources.

s8572569.titulo: Removes the time limit to prosecute child trafficking
s8572569.oQueMuda: Trafficking of children and teenagers could be punished at any time.
s8572569.quemAfeta: Victims and those accused of this crime.
s8572569.porQueImporta: Today child trafficking has a time limit for prosecution, depending on the sentence. Under the PEC, there would be no time limit.

s8466340.titulo: Adds city attorneys to the public legal service
s8466340.oQueMuda: City attorneys would become part of the public legal service provided for in the Constitution.
s8466340.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution provides for career attorneys hired by exam for the federal government and states, but not for municipalities. Under the PEC, city governments would need career attorneys.

c2388029.titulo: Sets aside part of lawmakers' budget amendments for natural disasters
c2388029.oQueMuda: 5% of individual budget amendments from deputies and senators would go to disaster prevention and response, such as floods and droughts.
c2388029.quemAfeta: Municipalities hit by floods, droughts and landslides.
c2388029.porQueImporta: Today half of individual budget amendments must go to health, and the rest is free. Under the PEC, 5% would have to go to disaster prevention and response.

c2448752.titulo: Defines life as beginning at conception
c2448752.oQueMuda: The Constitution would state that the right to life is inviolable from fertilization.
c2448752.porQueImporta: Today abortion is allowed in Brazil in cases of rape, risk to the mother's life and fetal anencephaly, rules set by the Penal Code and a Supreme Court ruling. Under the PEC, the Constitution, which ranks above those rules, would say the right to life is inviolable from fertilization.

s8693939.oQueMuda: The government would have to carry out budget amendments made by congressional committees.
s8693939.porQueImporta: Today the government must pay individual and state caucus amendments, but not committee amendments. Under the PEC, committee amendments would also be mandatory.

s8693978.titulo: Creates the Rio Grande do Sul Free Trade Zone
s8693978.oQueMuda: Creates, for a set period, an area with tax benefits in Rio Grande do Sul.
s8693978.quemAfeta: Companies and residents of Rio Grande do Sul.
s8693978.porQueImporta: Today the only free trade zone with tax benefits in the Constitution is Manaus. Under the PEC, there would be an area with lower taxes in Rio Grande do Sul, for a fixed period.

c2189078.titulo: Changes how the State Participation Fund is shared
c2189078.oQueMuda: Changes the rules for splitting the FPE among states and the Federal District.
c2189078.porQueImporta: Today FPE, which transfers 21.5% of income tax and IPI to states, is split by population and income criteria set by law. Under the PEC, the criteria would change, altering how much each state receives.

c2209439.titulo: Allows regional funds to pay for public works
c2209439.oQueMuda: Money from the North, Northeast and Center-West funds could finance public works.
c2209439.quemAfeta: States and cities in these regions.
c2209439.porQueImporta: Today the constitutional funds of the North, Northeast and Center-West lend money to companies and producers. Under the PEC, they could also finance state and municipal public works.

c2277279.titulo: Makes access to drinking water a fundamental right
c2277279.oQueMuda: Access to drinking water would be included among fundamental rights.
c2277279.quemAfeta: People without clean water and the government.
c2277279.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution does not expressly mention access to drinking water as a right. Under the PEC, it would be added to the list of fundamental rights; on its own, the change creates no funding or works.

c2147461.titulo: Removes the time limit to prosecute rape
c2147461.oQueMuda: Rape could be punished at any time.
c2147461.quemAfeta: Victims and those accused of rape.
c2147461.porQueImporta: Today the time limit for prosecuting rape is up to 20 years, depending on the sentence. Under the PEC, there would be no time limit.

s7755772.titulo: Limits expropriations and requires market-price compensation
s7755772.oQueMuda: Expropriating urban and rural property would need approval from the legislature or a court, with payment at market value.
s7755772.quemAfeta: Owners, governments and housing and land movements.
s7755772.porQueImporta: Today governments can expropriate property by decree, and land that does not fulfill its social function is paid for with agrarian debt bonds. Under the PEC, expropriation would require approval by the legislature or courts, with payment at market value.

c2229539.titulo: Removes the time limit to prosecute rape and femicide
c2229539.oQueMuda: Rape and femicide would allow no bail and could be punished at any time.
c2229539.quemAfeta: Victims, their families and the accused.
c2229539.porQueImporta: Today rape and femicide are already non-bailable, as heinous crimes, but the time limit for prosecution is up to 20 years. Under the PEC, there would be no time limit.

c451074.oQueMuda: People not affiliated with a party could run for office.
c451074.porQueImporta: Today one can only run for office as a member of a party. Under the PEC, people without a party could also run.

c2140427.oQueMuda: Defines how voters can revoke terms through a citizen initiative.
c2140427.porQueImporta: Today an elected politician only loses office early through removal, impeachment or resignation. Under the PEC, voters could revoke mandates through a citizen initiative.

c2145346.titulo: Allows independent candidates and civic lists
c2145346.oQueMuda: Candidates without a party could run with voter support and join civic lists.
c2145346.porQueImporta: Today one can only run for office as a member of a party. Under the PEC, candidates without a party could run with voter support and join civic lists.

c2162013.titulo: Allows candidates without a party with support from 1% of voters
c2162013.oQueMuda: Anyone backed by 1% of voters could run without a party.
c2162013.porQueImporta: Today one can only run for office as a member of a party. Under the PEC, those with support from 1% of voters could run without a party.

c2226594.oQueMuda: The government would be led by a prime minister with the support of Congress.
c2226594.porQueImporta: Today the elected president is both head of state and of government; in 1993 voters chose this system in a referendum. Under the PEC, a prime minister backed by Congress would head the government.

s8670175.titulo: Adds sport to the social rights
s8670175.oQueMuda: Adds sport to the Constitution's list of social rights (article 6). On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8670175.quemAfeta: The whole population, athletes and governments.
s8670175.porQueImporta: The Constitution already says the State must encourage sport; the change also puts it on the list of social rights.

c2153455.oQueMuda: Creates security bodies for juvenile detention centers.
c2153455.quemAfeta: Juvenile detention staff and detained teenagers.
c2153455.porQueImporta: Today staff at juvenile detention units are not part of the public security bodies. Under the PEC, juvenile security corps would be created.

c2436619.titulo: Adds integration with Portuguese-speaking countries to foreign policy
c2436619.oQueMuda: States that Brazil will seek economic, political, social and cultural integration with Portuguese-speaking countries, to form a lusophone community. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2436619.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution says Brazil will seek integration with the peoples of Latin America. Under the PEC, there would be a similar rule for Portuguese-speaking countries.

s8655096.titulo: Creates a special fiscal regime for environmental disasters
s8655096.oQueMuda: Governments could relax fiscal and procurement rules to deal with regional or local disasters.
s8655096.quemAfeta: Residents of affected areas and governments.
s8655096.porQueImporta: Today fiscal and procurement rules can only be relaxed in disasters recognized case by case by Congress. Under the PEC, there would be a permanent special regime for regional and local disasters.

s8394295.titulo: Creates a seniority bonus outside the pay cap for judges, prosecutors and other legal careers
s8394295.oQueMuda:
Bonus: judges and prosecutors would get 5% more salary for every 5 years of legal work, up to 35%, outside the public pay cap.
Who else: the text approved by the Senate Justice Committee extends it to audit court members, public defenders, government lawyers and police chiefs, and lets each body grant it to other servants barred from other paid work.
Counting time: time in other legal careers and in private law practice before taking office counts.
Retirement: the bonus would be included in pensions, with no contribution required.
s8394295.quemAfeta: Judges, prosecutors, public defenders, government lawyers, police chiefs, audit court members and federal and state budgets.
s8394295.porQueImporta: Since the Supreme Court decision of June 30, 2026, judges and prosecutors already receive 5% of salary for every 5 years, up to 35%. Under the PEC, the bonus would be in the Constitution, outside the cap, and extended to other careers.
s8394295.nota: The Independent Fiscal Institution, the Senate's technical body, estimated the cost at R$ 5.2 billion a year for the original text and up to R$ 42 billion a year with the extension to other careers. The Senate Budget Consultancy estimated R$ 81.6 billion from 2024 to 2026.

c2329063.titulo: Bans cutting the armed forces' budget
c2329063.oQueMuda: Removes limits and bans freezes on armed forces funding.
c2329063.quemAfeta: The armed forces and the federal budget.
c2329063.porQueImporta: Today the armed forces' budget follows general spending rules and can be frozen. Under the PEC, it would be outside the limits and protected from freezes.

s8060121.titulo: Adds the right to clean air to the fundamental rights
s8060121.oQueMuda: States that everyone has the right to air quality, including in shared indoor spaces, public or private. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8060121.quemAfeta: The whole population, companies and governments.
s8060121.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution guarantees an ecologically balanced environment, without mentioning air. Under the PEC, air quality would be an express fundamental right, including in shared indoor spaces.

s8646008.titulo: Changes small business taxation under the tax reform
s8646008.oQueMuda: Fixes rules of the new tax system for micro and small businesses and individual micro-entrepreneurs (MEIs).
s8646008.quemAfeta: Micro and small businesses and individual micro-entrepreneurs.
s8646008.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, rules of the new tax system for micro and small businesses and micro-entrepreneurs would change, such as how they generate IBS and CBS credits for buyers.

s8644146.titulo: Sends part of tourism sales tax back to the sector
s8644146.oQueMuda: States would set aside a share of ICMS from tourism services to promote tourism.
s8644146.quemAfeta: The tourism sector and state governments.
s8644146.porQueImporta: Today states' ICMS has no share reserved for tourism. Under the PEC, a percentage of ICMS on tourism services would have to go to promoting the sector.

s8639865.titulo: Adds culture to the social rights
s8639865.oQueMuda: Adds culture to the Constitution's list of social rights (article 6). On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8639865.quemAfeta: The whole population, artists and governments.
s8639865.porQueImporta: The Constitution already tells the State to guarantee cultural rights; the change also puts culture on the list of social rights.

c2017887.titulo: Lets Congress halt acts of the judiciary
c2017887.oQueMuda: Congress could annul rules issued by the judiciary.
c2017887.porQueImporta: Today Congress can suspend executive acts that exceed its regulatory power, but not judicial acts. Under the PEC, it could also annul normative acts by courts.

c2207351.titulo: Lets Congress halt acts of the judiciary
c2207351.oQueMuda: Congress could annul judiciary rules it considers excessive.
c2207351.porQueImporta: Today Congress can suspend executive acts that exceed its regulatory power, but not judicial acts. Under the PEC, it could also annul court normative acts it considers excessive.

s8386303.titulo: Adds military court judges to the CNJ
s8386303.oQueMuda: Military court judges would get a seat on the National Council of Justice.
s8386303.quemAfeta: The military courts and the CNJ.
s8386303.porQueImporta: Today the CNJ has 15 members, with no seat for military courts. Under the PEC, military court judges would have a seat on the council.

c344176.titulo: Extends special retirement to education professionals
c344176.oQueMuda: Those in teaching or teaching support would have five years off the required age and contribution time.
c344176.porQueImporta: Today only classroom teachers retire five years earlier. Under the PEC, those in pedagogical support roles, such as coordination and counseling, would have the same right.

c400327.titulo: Counts teaching in hospitals and prisons as teaching service
c400327.oQueMuda: Teachers in hospitals, rehabilitation centers and prisons would have special retirement.
c400327.porQueImporta: Today basic education teachers retire five years earlier, but teaching in hospitals and prisons does not always count. Under the PEC, this work would count as teaching.

c415712.titulo: Ends the minimum retirement age for teachers
c415712.oQueMuda: Public school teachers could retire based only on contribution time, with no minimum age.
c415712.porQueImporta: Today public school teachers need a minimum age (57 for women and 60 for men, at federal level) to retire. Under the PEC, contribution time alone would suffice.

c489706.titulo: Counts time in former daycare centers toward retirement
c489706.oQueMuda: Early childhood teachers could count time worked in daycare centers before they joined school systems.
c489706.porQueImporta: Before joining school systems, many daycare centers were part of social assistance, and that time does not count as teaching. Under the PEC, early childhood teachers could count it toward special retirement.

c2117201.titulo: Adds municipal guards to public safety
c2117201.oQueMuda: Municipal guards would become part of the public safety bodies, with retirement rights.
c2117201.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution allows municipal guards to protect city property and services, outside the list of public security bodies. Under the PEC, they would join that list, with their own retirement rules.

c349704.titulo: Gives severance fund (FGTS) and unemployment insurance to political appointees
c349704.oQueMuda: Civil servants in freely appointed posts would be entitled to notice, the FGTS severance fund and unemployment insurance.
c349704.porQueImporta: Today political appointees can be dismissed at any time, without notice, severance fund or unemployment insurance. Under the PEC, they would have these rights.

s7826575.oQueMuda: Fathers and mothers could alternate and share the days of maternity leave.
s7826575.porQueImporta: Today maternity leave belongs to the mother, and paternity leave lasts 5 days. Under the PEC, father and mother could split the maternity leave days between them.

s7830951.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for Brazil to leave treaties
s7830951.oQueMuda: Brazil could only withdraw from an international treaty with Congress's prior approval.
s7830951.porQueImporta: Today the president can withdraw Brazil from an international treaty without consulting Congress. Under the PEC, it would require prior approval by lawmakers.

s7856184.titulo: Replaces maternity leave with 180-day parental leave
s7856184.oQueMuda: Creates a 180-day leave that fathers and mothers, including adoptive parents, could share.
s7856184.porQueImporta: Today maternity leave is 120 days and paternity leave 5 days. Under the PEC, there would be 180 days of parental leave that both parents, including adoptive ones, could share.

c2024222.titulo: Broadens the definition of family in the Constitution
c2024222.oQueMuda: A family would be any group of two or more people joined by blood, affection, marriage or civil union.
c2024222.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution mentions families formed by marriage, stable union or one parent with children, and in 2011 the Supreme Court recognized same-sex unions. Under the PEC, a family would be any group united by blood, affection, marriage or stable union.

c2221375.titulo: Creates a fund for a possible state formed by merging with the former capital
c2221375.oQueMuda: Creates a constitutional fund for a federal unit resulting from a merger with the former capital and sets a 10-year limit for these funds.
c2221375.quemAfeta: Residents and the government of Rio de Janeiro.
c2221375.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, a constitutional fund would be created for a federative unit formed by merging with the former capital, Rio de Janeiro, and these funds would last 10 years.

c2222665.titulo: Changes the rule on council members holding two jobs
c2222665.oQueMuda: Changes the rule that lets city council members combine their term with a job in city government.
c2222665.quemAfeta: City council members who are civil servants.
c2222665.porQueImporta: Today a city councilor who is a civil servant can combine both roles if schedules are compatible. Under the PEC, this rule would change.

c2224677.titulo: Expands the state's duty in education
c2224677.oQueMuda: Adds a new state duty toward education and changes a school funding rule.
c2224677.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, the Constitution would add a new State duty in education and change a rule on education funding.

c2084719.titulo: Guarantees civil servants a yearly raise at least equal to inflation
c2084719.oQueMuda: The general annual salary review for civil servants could not be lower than inflation.
c2084719.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution provides an annual review of civil servants' salaries, but with no minimum index, and some years had no raise. Under the PEC, the annual raise could not be below inflation.

s8412320.titulo: Details the right to food with the idea of food security
s8412320.oQueMuda: States that the right to food includes regular and permanent access to enough safe and healthy food for everyone. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8412320.quemAfeta: People facing food insecurity and governments.
s8412320.porQueImporta: Food has been a social right since 2010; the change explains in the Constitution what that right means.

s7753206.titulo: Creates Supreme Court terms and selection by Congress
s7753206.oQueMuda: Some justices of the Supreme Court and higher courts would be chosen by the Chamber and the Senate, with fixed terms.
s7753206.porQueImporta: Today Supreme Court and higher-court justices are nominated by the president and serve until 75. Under the PEC, some would be chosen by the Chamber and Senate, with fixed terms.

s8560990.titulo: Creates 15-year terms for Supreme Court justices
s8560990.oQueMuda: Supreme Court justices would serve 15-year terms with a minimum age of 50, with changes to how higher courts are chosen.
s8560990.quemAfeta: Justices of the Supreme Court and higher courts.
s8560990.porQueImporta: Today Supreme Court justices can be nominated from age 35 and serve until 75. Under the PEC, they would have a minimum age of 50 and a 15-year term.

s8513893.titulo: Requires a verifiable printed ballot in elections
s8513893.oQueMuda: Voting machines would have to print a ballot the voter can check, kept for audits.
s8513893.porQueImporta: Today voting is electronic only; a 2015 law requiring printed votes was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2020. Under the PEC, machines would print a ballot that the voter checks and that is kept for audits.

s8623312.titulo: Expands legislators' immunity for their opinions
s8623312.oQueMuda: Reworks the rule so deputies and senators can't be punished for opinions and votes anywhere.
s8623312.porQueImporta: Today lawmakers cannot be punished for opinions, words and votes linked to their mandate, and the Supreme Court has convicted deputies for statements outside that role. Under the PEC, protection would cover opinions anywhere.

s8622879.titulo: Requires a verifiable printed ballot in elections
s8622879.oQueMuda: Voters would be able to check their vote on paper, and counting would take place publicly at the polling station right after voting, with voters and party observers present. Each machine's result would be kept by the Electoral Court for 5 years for audits.
s8622879.porQueImporta: Today voting is electronic only, and each machine prints a results report at the end of voting. A 2015 law requiring printed votes was struck down unanimously by the Supreme Court in 2020 for endangering ballot secrecy.
s8622879.nota: Since electronic voting machines were adopted in 1996, no fraud in the results has been proven. The Armed Forces report on the 2022 election also found no fraud. Supporters of printed ballots say they would allow an independent audit of the electronic system.

s8617172.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility to 16 for heinous crimes
s8617172.oQueMuda: 16 and 17-year-olds who commit heinous crimes would be tried as adults.
s8617172.porQueImporta: Today people under 18 are subject to the Child and Adolescent Statute, with at most 3 years of detention. Under the PEC, 16- and 17-year-olds who commit heinous crimes would be tried and imprisoned as adults.

s8620564.titulo: Lets Congress halt acts of the judiciary and councils
s8620564.oQueMuda: Congress could annul acts of courts and councils that exceed their powers.
s8620564.quemAfeta: Congress, the courts, the CNJ and the CNMP.
s8620564.porQueImporta: Today Congress can suspend executive acts, but not those of courts or of the councils overseeing judges and prosecutors (CNJ and CNMP). Under the PEC, it could annul acts by these bodies.

c2196833.titulo: Tax reform: replaces five taxes with IBS and CBS
c2196833.oQueMuda:
New taxes: PIS, Cofins and IPI (federal), ICMS (state) and ISS (municipal) are replaced by CBS (federal) and IBS (states and municipalities), charged at destination without cascading, plus a Selective Tax on products harmful to health and the environment.
Lower rates: a national basic food basket at zero rate; a 60% cut for health, education, medicines and some foods; a 30% cut for regulated professions.
Cashback: part of the tax returned to low-income families.
Transition: the new taxes start in a test phase in 2026, and the old ones end by 2033.
c2196833.porQueImporta: In force since December 2023, with a transition until 2033. Today each state and municipality has its own ICMS and ISS rules, and the same product can be taxed several times along the chain.
c2196833.nota: Each exception with a lower rate raises the rate everyone else pays. After the exceptions approved by Congress in the implementing law, the Finance Ministry estimated the standard rate at about 28%, among the highest in the world for this type of tax; the law provides for a review aiming at 26.5%.

s8403380.titulo: Adjusts federal transfers to cities for inflation
s8403380.oQueMuda: Amounts in federal agreements and programs with cities would be updated for inflation.
s8403380.porQueImporta: Today amounts in federal agreements and programs with city governments are fixed, with no automatic adjustment. Under the PEC, they would be adjusted for inflation.

c459272.titulo: Aligns the Constitution with the UN disability convention
c459272.oQueMuda: Updates several articles to follow the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
c459272.porQueImporta: Since 2008 the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities has had the force of a constitutional amendment. Under the PEC, several articles would be rewritten to follow its terms.

s8609290.oQueMuda: People not affiliated with a party could run for office.
s8609290.porQueImporta: Today one can only run for office as a member of a party. Under the PEC, people without a party could also run.

s8609795.titulo: Grants amnesty for the January 8 riots and restores rights and mandates
s8609795.oQueMuda:
Amnesty: everyone involved in the January 8, 2023 events in Brasília would be pardoned for all crimes and misdemeanors.
Ineligible politicians: those declared ineligible for acts, statements and demonstrations linked to the 2022 election would regain their political rights.
Mandates: those who lost their office over these acts would return within 15 days.
s8609795.quemAfeta: People convicted or investigated over the January 8 events and politicians declared ineligible or removed over conduct linked to the 2022 election.
s8609795.porQueImporta: The Supreme Court convicted hundreds of people over the January 8, 2023 events, for crimes such as attempted coup, violent abolition of the democratic rule of law and damage to public property, and the Electoral Court declared politicians ineligible over conduct in the 2022 election. Under the PEC, these convictions and ineligibilities would be erased.

s8610921.titulo: Ends secret votes in the legislature
s8610921.oQueMuda: All votes in Congress, state assemblies and city councils would be open.
s8610921.porQueImporta: Since 2013 votes on vetoes and on removing lawmakers have been open, but others, such as approving nominated officials, are still secret. Under the PEC, all votes in legislatures would be open.

c1555270.titulo: Adds accessibility and urban mobility to the social rights
c1555270.oQueMuda: Adds 'accessibility' and 'urban mobility' to the list of social rights. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c1555270.quemAfeta: People with disabilities or reduced mobility, transport users and city governments.
c1555270.porQueImporta: The Constitution already covers accessibility for people with disabilities and, since 2015, includes transport as a social right.

c2301270.titulo: Adds accessibility and mobility to the fundamental rights
c2301270.oQueMuda: Adds to the list of fundamental rights: 'everyone is guaranteed the right to accessibility and mobility'. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2301270.quemAfeta: People with disabilities or reduced mobility, and the government.
c2301270.porQueImporta: The Constitution already covers accessibility for people with disabilities; the change turns it into a fundamental right for everyone.

c117100.titulo: Bans workplace discrimination based on sexual orientation and other grounds
c117100.oQueMuda: Bans differences in pay, role and hiring based on sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, politics or disability.
c117100.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution bans pay and hiring differences based on sex, age, color, marital status and disability. Under the PEC, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion and political views would be added.

c2195689.titulo: Gives children with disabilities priority in early education
c2195689.oQueMuda: Children with disabilities would have priority for daycare and preschool places.
c2195689.quemAfeta: Children with disabilities and their families.
c2195689.porQueImporta: Today enrollment in daycare and preschool follows each system's criteria. Under the PEC, children with disabilities would have priority for places.

c421307.titulo: Passes part of import tax to cities with customs zones
c421307.oQueMuda: 5% of the import tax would go to cities that host customs zones.
c421307.porQueImporta: Today import duty goes entirely to the federal government. Under the PEC, 5% would go to municipalities with customs ports, airports and border crossings.

s8607959.titulo: Bars reducing a legal minimum wage by agreement
s8607959.oQueMuda: Minimum salaries set by law could not be reduced by collective agreements.
s8607959.quemAfeta: Workers with a legal minimum salary and employers.
s8607959.porQueImporta: Since the 2017 labor reform, collective agreements can override the law on many points. Under the PEC, pay floors set by law could not be reduced by these agreements.

c259094.oQueMuda: Changes several parts of the tax system, in a smaller version of tax reform.
c259094.quemAfeta: Taxpayers, states and the federal government.
c259094.porQueImporta: This PEC is a part of the 2003 tax reform that was left pending in the Chamber. The broad reform of consumption taxes was only approved in 2023, through another PEC.

c536019.titulo: Charges vehicle tax (IPVA) on planes, private jets and boats
c536019.oQueMuda: The IPVA would also apply to aircraft and boats.
c536019.quemAfeta: Owners of planes, helicopters, yachts and motorboats.
c536019.porQueImporta: Until 2023 IPVA did not apply to aircraft and boats; the 2023 tax reform allowed this charge. This 2012 PEC proposed the same change.

c582954.titulo: Expands the vehicle tax (IPVA) and creates exemptions
c582954.oQueMuda: The IPVA would apply to more vehicles and be banned in some situations.
c582954.porQueImporta: Under the PEC, IPVA would apply to more types of vehicles, and charging it would be banned in some situations defined in the text.

c2081040.titulo: Sets a deadline to enact constitutional amendments
c2081040.oQueMuda: Approved amendments would have a deadline to be enacted.
c2081040.porQueImporta: Today there is no deadline for Congress's leadership to enact an approved amendment. Under the PEC, there would be one.

c2189052.titulo: Makes newly sworn-in deputies and senators lose any other office
c2189052.oQueMuda: On taking office as deputy or senator, a person would permanently lose any other elected office they held.
c2189052.quemAfeta: Officeholders who are elected to Congress.
c2189052.porQueImporta: Today someone elected deputy or senator who holds another mandate, such as city councilor, can take leave and return later. Under the PEC, they would lose the other mandate upon taking office.

c2404706.titulo: Allows using leftover COVID funds for health
c2404706.oQueMuda: Leftover federal funds sent to fight the pandemic could be used for other health actions.
c2404706.quemAfeta: States, cities and patients of the public health system (SUS).
c2404706.porQueImporta: Today leftover federal money sent to fight Covid-19 can only be used for that purpose. Under the PEC, states and municipalities could use it for other health actions.

c2406638.titulo: Creates a specific legal regime for police officers
c2406638.oQueMuda: Sets specific rules on careers, retirement and survivor pensions for police.
c2406638.porQueImporta: Today police follow career and retirement rules from the 2019 reform and each state's laws. Under the PEC, they would have their own legal regime, with career, retirement and pension rules.

c2405983.titulo: Swaps payroll contributions for a transactions tax
c2405983.oQueMuda: Contributions on payroll and revenue would be replaced by a charge on financial transactions.
c2405983.porQueImporta: Today companies pay social security contributions on payroll and revenue. Under the PEC, these would be replaced by a charge on financial transactions, like the old CPMF.

c530024.titulo: Lets foreigners vote and run in municipal elections
c530024.oQueMuda: Foreigners living in Brazil could take part in municipal elections.
c530024.porQueImporta: Today foreigners living in Brazil cannot vote or run for office, except Portuguese citizens with equal status. Under the PEC, they could take part in municipal elections.

c599448.titulo: Lets foreigners who have lived in Brazil over four years vote
c599448.oQueMuda: Foreign residents with regular status living in Brazil for more than four years could vote.
c599448.porQueImporta: Today foreigners living in Brazil cannot vote, except Portuguese citizens with equal status. Under the PEC, legal residents of more than four years could vote.

c2162990.titulo: Gives voting rights to foreigners who have lived in Brazil over five years
c2162990.oQueMuda: Foreigners legally residing in Brazil for more than five years could vote.
c2162990.porQueImporta: Today foreigners living in Brazil cannot vote, except Portuguese citizens with equal status. Under the PEC, legal residents of more than five years could vote.

c2196315.titulo: Lets military personnel return to active duty after a term
c2196315.oQueMuda: Elected military personnel could return to active service when their term ends.
c2196315.quemAfeta: Military personnel who run for office.
c2196315.porQueImporta: Today military personnel with more than 10 years of service who are elected move to the reserve and do not return to active duty. Under the PEC, they could return to active service after their term.

s8580579.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for binding Supreme Court precedents
s8580579.oQueMuda: The Supreme Court's binding precedents would be reviewed by Congress.
s8580579.porQueImporta: Today the Supreme Court alone approves binding precedents that all judges and public bodies must follow. Under the PEC, they would be reviewed by Congress.

s8582557.titulo: Requires Congress's approval to recognize Indigenous lands
s8582557.oQueMuda: Recognition of Indigenous lands would have to be approved by Congress.
s8582557.porQueImporta: Today Indigenous lands are demarcated by the federal government, by presidential decree, after studies by Funai. Under the PEC, each demarcation would need approval by Congress.

s8582970.titulo: Makes child sexual abuse a crime without bail or time limit
s8582970.oQueMuda: Child sexual abuse crimes would allow no bail and could be punished at any time.
s8582970.quemAfeta: Victims and those accused of these crimes.
s8582970.porQueImporta: Today sexual crimes against children are already heinous and non-bailable, and the time limit starts when the victim turns 18. Under the PEC, there would be no time limit.

s8583613.titulo: Requires Congress's approval to recognize Indigenous lands
s8583613.oQueMuda: Recognition of Indigenous lands would depend on approval by Congress.
s8583613.porQueImporta: Today Indigenous lands are demarcated by the federal government, by presidential decree, after studies by Funai. Under the PEC, each demarcation would depend on approval by Congress.

c553109.titulo: Requires a degree to work as a journalist
c553109.oQueMuda: Again requires a university degree to work as a journalist.
c553109.porQueImporta: Since 2009, under a Supreme Court ruling, no degree is needed to work as a journalist. Under the PEC, a journalism degree would again be required.

c1724712.titulo: Compensates owners of land declared Indigenous
c1724712.oQueMuda: Owners holding titles to areas declared Indigenous from 2013 onward could be compensated.
c1724712.porQueImporta: Today, when land is declared Indigenous, titleholders are only compensated for improvements, such as houses and crops, not for the land. Under the PEC, those with titles to areas declared from 2013 would also be compensated for the land.

s8488781.titulo: Raises science investment to 2.5% of GDP
s8488781.oQueMuda: Investment in science, technology and innovation would gradually rise to at least 2.5% of GDP.
s8488781.porQueImporta: Today Brazil invests just over 1% of GDP in research and development, counting government and companies. Under the PEC, this investment would have to gradually reach at least 2.5% of GDP.

c2288318.titulo: Allows dual citizenship without losing Brazilian nationality
c2288318.oQueMuda: Brazilians would not lose their nationality when acquiring another, unless they ask to.
c2288318.porQueImporta: Already in force (Amendment 131 of 2023): Brazilians who acquire another nationality no longer lose Brazilian nationality unless they ask to.

c621519.titulo: Gives permanent status to public workers hired without an exam
c621519.oQueMuda: People working for federal, state and city governments would be made permanent civil servants.
c621519.quemAfeta: Temporary and outsourced public sector workers.
c621519.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution requires public exams for permanent posts. Under the PEC, people already working for the federal, state and municipal governments without an exam would be made permanent.

c2224532.titulo: Allows judges to swap posts between different courts
c2224532.oQueMuda: Judges could request a transfer or swap posts with colleagues in other courts of the same branch: state, federal or labor courts.
c2224532.porQueImporta: Already in force (Amendment 130 of 2023): judges can request transfers or swap posts with colleagues in other courts of the same branch, state, federal or labor.

c407657.titulo: Creates a fund to revitalize the São Francisco River
c407657.oQueMuda: Creates a fund to restore the environment and develop the São Francisco River basin.
c407657.quemAfeta: Residents of the São Francisco basin.
c407657.porQueImporta: Today revitalizing the São Francisco River depends on federal programs with funding set each year. Under the PEC, there would be a fund with money reserved for the basin.

c483817.titulo: Makes the Cerrado and the Caatinga national heritage
c483817.oQueMuda: These two biomes would be added to the national heritage areas.
c483817.quemAfeta: Residents and producers in the Cerrado and the Caatinga.
c483817.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution lists as national heritage the Amazon, Atlantic Forest, Serra do Mar, Mato Grosso Pantanal and the coastal zone. Under the PEC, the Cerrado and Caatinga would be added, with use conditioned on preservation.

s8569449.oQueMuda: The federal government would top up the Municipal Participation Fund to keep the same share of GDP as in 2022.
s8569449.porQueImporta: Today FPM varies with income tax and IPI revenue, and falls when revenue falls. Under the PEC, the federal government would top it up to keep it at the same share of GDP as in 2022.

c398998.titulo: Ends the 'constitutional fifth' in the courts
c398998.oQueMuda: Courts would no longer reserve seats for lawyers and prosecutors.
c398998.porQueImporta: Today one fifth of seats on appeal courts and some higher courts are reserved for lawyers and prosecutors. Under the PEC, these seats would go only to career judges.

s7720809.titulo: Guarantees a full public health team for pregnant women
s7720809.oQueMuda: The public health system (SUS) would have to provide a pediatrician, gynecologist, obstetrician, nurses and psychologist during prenatal care, birth and postpartum.
s7720809.porQueImporta: Today the public health system offers prenatal care and childbirth, but the team varies by place. Under the PEC, it would have to guarantee a pediatrician, gynecologist, obstetrician, nurses and psychologist for prenatal care, birth and postpartum.

c2092664.titulo: Reserves 10% of individual amendments for public safety
c2092664.oQueMuda: 10% of legislators' individual budget amendments would go to public safety.
c2092664.porQueImporta: Today half of individual budget amendments must go to health, and the rest is free. Under the PEC, 10% would have to go to public security.

s8242831.titulo: Allows public and private companies to collect and process plasma
s8242831.oQueMuda: Today the Constitution bans all trade in organs, tissues, blood and blood products. The text approved by the Senate Justice Committee opens a single exception: human plasma could be collected, processed and sold by public and private institutions, for research and to make medicines intended preferably for SUS. The private sector would act in a complementary way, when requested by the Health Ministry. The rules would be set by law.
s8242831.quemAfeta: Blood donors, patients who depend on plasma-derived medicines, the state company Hemobrás and companies in the sector.
s8242831.porQueImporta: Today plasma donated in Brazil is processed by the state company Hemobrás, and blood donation has been voluntary and unpaid since the 1980s. Under the PEC, plasma could be traded.
s8242831.nota: The National Health Council, the Health Ministry and Hemobrás oppose it and say that trading plasma could reduce voluntary blood donations. The Brazilian Hematology Association supports the PEC and says Hemobrás meets only about 10% of the country's immunoglobulin needs.

s8442337.oQueMuda: Sets institutional rules for the prosecutors who work with the Courts of Accounts.
s8442337.quemAfeta: Audit prosecutors and Courts of Accounts.
s8442337.porQueImporta: Today the Audit Prosecutor's Office, which works in the Audit Courts, has few rules in the Constitution. Under the PEC, it would gain its own institutional rules, such as autonomy and guarantees for its members.

s8549385.titulo: Extends the right to life to the unborn
s8549385.oQueMuda: The right to life would protect the embryo from conception.
s8549385.porQueImporta: Today abortion is allowed in Brazil in cases of rape, risk to the mother's life and fetal anencephaly, rules set by the Penal Code and a Supreme Court ruling. Under the PEC, the Constitution, which ranks above those rules, would say the right to life protects the embryo from conception.

c406708.titulo: Sets aside budget money for affordable housing
c406708.oQueMuda: Federal, state and city governments would have to allocate fixed funds to social housing funds.
c406708.quemAfeta: Families without adequate housing and governments.
c406708.porQueImporta: Today affordable housing programs depend on each year's budget. Under the PEC, the federal government, states and municipalities would have to allocate fixed funds to social housing funds.

s8513795.titulo: Tax reform abolishing the ICMS and Cide
s8513795.oQueMuda: Abolishes taxes such as the ICMS and Cide and creates new state tax rules.
s8513795.porQueImporta: The 2023 reform already provides for ending ICMS by 2033, replaced by IBS. This PEC proposed abolishing ICMS and Cide with a different model of state taxes.

s8545103.titulo: Bans charging union fees to non-members
s8545103.oQueMuda: Unions could only charge any contribution to non-member workers or companies with each one's prior individual authorization.
s8545103.porQueImporta: In 2023 the Supreme Court allowed unions to charge an assistance contribution to all workers in the profession, including non-members, as long as they can opt out. Under the PEC, charging non-members would require prior individual authorization.

s8539271.titulo: Requires Supreme Court justices to face a new hearing every 8 years
s8539271.oQueMuda: The Senate would hold a public hearing of Supreme Court justices every eight years.
s8539271.quemAfeta: Supreme Court justices and the Senate.
s8539271.porQueImporta: Today Supreme Court justices are questioned by the Senate only before taking office. Under the PEC, they would face a new public hearing every eight years.

s8538765.titulo: Temporarily raises transfers to the FPM
s8538765.oQueMuda: Raises for a period the share of income tax and IPI that goes to the Municipal Participation Fund.
s8538765.porQueImporta: Today the federal government transfers 22.5% of income tax and IPI to FPM, plus extra shares in July, September and December. Under the PEC, this share would increase for a period.

s8540424.titulo: Bars judges from cases handled by relatives' law firms
s8540424.oQueMuda: Judges could not rule on cases with lawyers who are their spouses or close relatives.
s8540424.porQueImporta: In 2023 the Supreme Court struck down the Civil Procedure Code rule barring judges from cases involving law firms of relatives. Under the PEC, this bar would be in the Constitution.

s7723044.titulo: Guarantees cities the ICMS and IPVA that states fail to pass on
s7723044.oQueMuda: The federal government would withhold state funds and pay cities directly the share of ICMS and IPVA not passed on.
s7723044.porQueImporta: Today states must pass 25% of ICMS and 50% of IPVA to city governments, and there are cases of delay. Under the PEC, the federal government would withhold state money and pay cities directly what was not transferred.

s8326366.titulo: Guarantees free public transit on election day
s8326366.oQueMuda: Buses, boats and intercity transport would be free on voting days.
s8326366.porQueImporta: Since 2023, under a Supreme Court ruling, cities with public transport must offer free rides on election days. Under the PEC, free buses, boats and intercity transport would be in the Constitution.

c2223558.titulo: Exempts Brazilian-made musical instruments from taxes
c2223558.oQueMuda: Musical instruments made in Brazil would be tax-free.
c2223558.porQueImporta: Today musical instruments pay taxes like other products. Under the PEC, those made in Brazil would be tax-free.

c2225811.oQueMuda: Creates a new case in which Brazilians who naturalize through marriage keep their nationality.
c2225811.porQueImporta: This PEC was shelved; in 2023 Amendment 131 already guaranteed that Brazilians who acquire another nationality, including through marriage, do not lose Brazilian nationality.

s8520995.titulo: Changes how Congress's internal rules are amended
s8520995.oQueMuda: Sets how bills changing the internal rules of the Chamber and Senate are voted on.
s8520995.porQueImporta: Today the Chamber and Senate change their internal rules by resolution, approved only by that house. Under the PEC, there would be rules in the Constitution for these votes.

c1555497.titulo: Adds internet access and message privacy to the fundamental rights
c1555497.oQueMuda: Guarantees everyone internet access and the confidentiality of digital communications, which could only be broken by court order in criminal investigations. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c1555497.quemAfeta: Internet users, technology companies and the police.
c1555497.porQueImporta: Confidentiality of communications is already in the Constitution; the change mentions the internet explicitly.

s8513844.titulo: Guarantees free transit for low-income people with disabilities
s8513844.oQueMuda: Low-income people with disabilities would ride urban public transit for free.
s8513844.quemAfeta: People with disabilities and city governments.
s8513844.porQueImporta: Today free transport for people with disabilities depends on each city's or state's laws. Under the PEC, low-income people with disabilities would ride urban public transport free nationwide.

c1738814.oQueMuda: Guarantees extra operating time for lottery outlet permits.
c1738814.porQueImporta: Already in force: lottery outlet permits received additional operating time before a new tender.

s8488965.titulo: Changes the process for provisional measures
s8488965.oQueMuda: Changes deadlines, agenda locking and reissuing of provisional measures (executive decrees).
s8488965.porQueImporta: Today a provisional measure is valid for up to 120 days and blocks Congress's agenda after 45. Under the PEC, these deadlines, the agenda block and reissue rules would change.

s8489404.titulo: Makes the Caatinga, Cerrado and Pampa national heritage
s8489404.oQueMuda: These three biomes would be added to the national heritage areas.
s8489404.quemAfeta: Residents and producers in these biomes.
s8489404.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution lists as national heritage the Amazon, Atlantic Forest, Serra do Mar, Mato Grosso Pantanal and the coastal zone. Under the PEC, the Caatinga, Cerrado and Pampa would be added, with use conditioned on preservation.

c2118343.titulo: Limits civil servants' vacation to 30 days
c2118343.oQueMuda: All public employees would have 30 days of vacation a year, with one-third extra pay.
c2118343.quemAfeta: Civil servants, including judges and prosecutors.
c2118343.porQueImporta: Today judges, prosecutors and some other careers have 60 days of vacation a year, while other civil servants have 30. Under the PEC, all would have 30 days.

c139244.titulo: Direct election of state attorneys general
c139244.oQueMuda: The heads of state prosecutors' offices would be elected by prosecutors themselves.
c139244.porQueImporta: Today the governor chooses the head of the state prosecution service from a list of three names voted by prosecutors. Under the PEC, the prosecutors' top choice would become head, without the governor choosing.

c2152285.titulo: Creates a democracy fund financed by politicians' salaries
c2152285.oQueMuda: Politicians and appointees would pay a contribution on their salaries to a fund financing democracy.
c2152285.quemAfeta: Elected politicians and holders of appointed posts.
c2152285.porQueImporta: Today campaigns are paid mainly by the public election fund and by individual donations. Under the PEC, politicians and appointees would pay a contribution on their salaries to a democracy financing fund.

s8472168.titulo: Puts mental integrity and algorithm transparency into the Constitution
s8472168.oQueMuda: States that scientific and technological development must ensure people's mental integrity and the transparency of algorithms, as set by law. On its own, it does not create rules for companies: a law is needed.
s8472168.quemAfeta: Technology users, digital companies and lawmakers.
s8472168.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution does not address mental integrity or algorithms. Under the PEC, these topics would join the list of fundamental rights, to be regulated by law.

c1050543.titulo: Allows seizing assets from crime or corruption
c1050543.oQueMuda: Prosecutors and government attorneys could ask courts to seize assets from crime, misconduct or illicit enrichment.
c1050543.quemAfeta: People with assets of illicit origin.
c1050543.porQueImporta: Today forfeiture of crime-related assets generally depends on a criminal conviction. Under the PEC, prosecutors and government attorneys could ask courts to seize illicit assets in a separate action.

s7857865.titulo: Adds climate stability to the principles of the economy
s7857865.oQueMuda: The economic order would have to seek climate stability and the government would have to act against climate change.
s7857865.porQueImporta: Today the principles of the economic order include environmental protection but do not mention climate. Under the PEC, climate stability would be added, and governments would have a duty to act against climate change.

c427297.titulo: Guarantees night-shift pay to police and firefighters
c427297.oQueMuda: Military police, firefighters and other security agents would be entitled to night-shift pay.
c427297.porQueImporta: Today formal workers and civilian civil servants get a night-shift bonus, but military police and firefighters have no such right in the Constitution. Under the PEC, they would.

c1278930.titulo: Sets working hours for military police and firefighters
c1278930.oQueMuda: Defines daily and weekly working hours for military police and firefighters.
c1278930.porQueImporta: Today there is no working-hours limit in the Constitution for military police and firefighters. Under the PEC, there would be maximum daily and weekly hours for them.

c2092228.titulo: Places notary offices among the functions essential to justice
c2092228.oQueMuda: Notaries and registrars would get their own section in the Constitution.
c2092228.porQueImporta: Today notary offices are mentioned in the Constitution only in one article on notarial services. Under the PEC, they would get their own section among the functions essential to justice, alongside lawyers, public defenders and prosecutors.

s5073365.porQueImporta: Today sport receives money from each year's budget and part of lottery revenue. Under the PEC, there would be a dedicated national fund.

s7975882.titulo: Extends book tax exemption to digital formats
s7975882.oQueMuda: Books, newspapers and magazines, including digital ones, would be free from all taxes.
s7975882.porQueImporta: Today printed books, newspapers and magazines pay no taxes, and the Supreme Court extended this to e-books in 2017. Under the PEC, all of them, printed or digital, would be free of all taxes, including contributions.

s7986137.titulo: Adds internet access to the fundamental and social rights
s7986137.oQueMuda: States that the State must guarantee internet access to all residents, adds internet access to the social rights and tells a law to guarantee net neutrality and quality. On its own, it does not create programs or funding: a law is needed.
s7986137.quemAfeta: People without internet access, telecom companies and governments.
s7986137.porQueImporta: The Brazilian Internet Bill of Rights already treats access as essential; the change raises it to a right in the Constitution.

s7987247.titulo: Repeals the spending cap and creates spending targets
s7987247.oQueMuda: Repeals the spending cap amendment and sets spending targets in the multi-year plan, with extra spending in 2021 and 2022.
s7987247.quemAfeta: The federal government and social program recipients.
s7987247.porQueImporta: This 2020 PEC proposed ending the spending cap created in 2016. The cap was eventually replaced in 2023 by another fiscal rule.
s7987247.apelido: End of the Spending Cap PEC

s8448291.titulo: Creates an income-based contribution to repay student loans
s8448291.oQueMuda: Allows a tax so former students repay their loans according to future income.
s8448291.quemAfeta: Students who use loans such as Fies.
s8448291.porQueImporta: Today Fies student loans are repaid in fixed installments after graduation, under contract rules. Under the PEC, a tax could be created so former students repay according to income.

c323818.titulo: Splits oil and mining royalties by population and HDI
c323818.oQueMuda: Money from oil, gas and mining would be divided among states and cities by population, area and Human Development Index.
c323818.quemAfeta: States and cities, producers or not.
c323818.porQueImporta: Today most oil and mining royalties go to the states and municipalities where extraction occurs. Under the PEC, they would be split among all by population, area and HDI.

c1049154.titulo: Adds access to energy to the social rights
c1049154.oQueMuda: Adds 'access to energy' to the list of social rights. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c1049154.quemAfeta: People without electricity, low-income consumers and governments.
c1049154.porQueImporta: Today access to energy is not on the list of social rights, and programs such as the social electricity rate exist by law. Under the PEC, it would be added to that list.

c1230264.titulo: Increases the share of income tax and IPI sent to cities
c1230264.oQueMuda: Raises the percentage of these taxes going to the Municipal Participation Fund.
c1230264.porQueImporta: Today the federal government transfers 22.5% of income tax and IPI to FPM, plus extra shares in July, September and December. Under the PEC, this share would increase.

c2075915.titulo: Adds internet access to the fundamental rights
c2075915.oQueMuda: Adds to the list of fundamental rights: 'universal internet access is guaranteed to everyone'. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2075915.quemAfeta: People without internet access and governments.
c2075915.porQueImporta: The Brazilian Internet Bill of Rights already treats access as essential; the change raises it to a fundamental right.

c2088568.titulo: Adds support for women victims of violence to social assistance
c2088568.oQueMuda: Social assistance would aim to support women who are victims of violence.
c2088568.porQueImporta: Today the goals of social assistance in the Constitution include protecting families, childhood and old age. Under the PEC, support for women victims of violence would be added.

c2198865.titulo: Updates the wording to 'person with a disability'
c2198865.oQueMuda: The Constitution would use the phrase 'person with a disability' throughout.
c2198865.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution uses terms such as 'person bearing a disability'. Under the PEC, it would use 'person with a disability', without changing rights.

s7834640.titulo: Restricts appeals to the Supreme Court in criminal cases
s7834640.oQueMuda: Extraordinary appeals to the Supreme Court would no longer be allowed in criminal matters.
s7834640.quemAfeta: Criminal defendants and the Supreme Court.
s7834640.porQueImporta: Today criminal defendants can appeal to the Supreme Court when they claim a constitutional violation. Under the PEC, this appeal would no longer exist in criminal cases.

s7933328.oQueMuda: The government would have to encourage payments to those who preserve nature and create jobs in environmental activities.
s7933328.porQueImporta: Since 2021 a law has created the National Policy on Payment for Environmental Services. Under the PEC, governments would have a constitutional duty to encourage these payments.

s7959745.titulo: Requires a list of three to choose the Prosecutor General
s7959745.oQueMuda: The President would choose the Prosecutor General from a list drawn up by federal prosecutors.
s7959745.porQueImporta: Today the president freely chooses the Prosecutor General among career prosecutors, with Senate approval. Under the PEC, the choice would have to come from a list of three names voted by prosecutors.

s8323670.titulo: Gives the Supreme Court jurisdiction over crimes against democracy
s8323670.oQueMuda: Crimes against the democratic rule of law would be tried directly by the Supreme Court.
s8323670.quemAfeta: People accused of these crimes and the Supreme Court.
s8323670.porQueImporta: Today crimes against the democratic rule of law are tried by federal courts, unless defendants have special jurisdiction at the Supreme Court. Under the PEC, all such crimes would be tried directly by the Supreme Court.

s7899802.titulo: Creates a fund to fight child poverty
s7899802.oQueMuda: Creates a fund with child poverty reduction targets and rewards for governments that make progress.
s7899802.porQueImporta: Today child poverty is addressed through programs such as Bolsa Família. Under the PEC, there would be a fund with child poverty reduction targets and rewards for governments that meet them.

s7901820.titulo: Creates guarantee funds for small businesses
s7901820.oQueMuda: Creates funds to guarantee loans to micro, small and medium-sized businesses in the regions.
s7901820.porQueImporta: Today there are guarantee funds created by law, such as Pronampe's. Under the PEC, there would be regional funds in the Constitution to guarantee loans to micro, small and medium businesses.

s7905790.titulo: Exempts donations to NGOs and research institutes from tax
s7905790.oQueMuda: Donations and bequests to nonprofit organizations would not pay the inheritance and gift tax (ITCMD).
s7905790.porQueImporta: Today donations and inheritances pay ITCMD, a state tax, except for each state's exemptions. Under the PEC, those made to non-profits and research institutes would be exempt nationwide.

s7916284.titulo: Postponed the 2020 municipal elections because of the pandemic
s7916284.oQueMuda: Allowed the Superior Electoral Court to postpone the 2020 elections and set terms to unify elections from 2026.
s7916284.porQueImporta: The 2020 municipal elections were postponed to November by another PEC, which became Amendment 107. This proposal, besides the postponement, set terms to unify elections from 2026.

s7917387.titulo: Unifies elections by extending municipal terms
s7917387.oQueMuda: Mayors and council members elected in 2016 would serve 6-year terms to coincide with other elections.
s7917387.porQueImporta: Today municipal and general elections alternate every two years. Under the PEC, mayors and councilors elected in 2016 would have 6-year terms, with no election in 2020, to unify the calendar.

s7917934.titulo: Counts pandemic work time double for retirement
s7917934.oQueMuda: Public health and security workers who fought COVID-19 would have that time counted double for retirement.
s7917934.porQueImporta: Today each year worked counts once toward retirement. Under the PEC, health and security civil servants who worked during the pandemic would have that time counted double.

c104989.titulo: Lets seconded civil servants transfer permanently
c104989.oQueMuda: Civil servants on loan to another body could choose to stay where they work.
c104989.quemAfeta: Civil servants on loan to other bodies.
c104989.porQueImporta: Today seconded civil servants remain in their original post, and changing posts requires a public exam. Under the PEC, they could stay permanently in the body where they work.

s8077867.titulo: Extends pension debt installment plans to 240 months
s8077867.oQueMuda: Governments could pay debts to their employees' pension systems in up to 240 installments during the pandemic.
s8077867.quemAfeta: States, cities and their civil servants.
s8077867.porQueImporta: Today governments with debts to their civil servants' pension funds have shorter installment periods. Under the PEC, they could pay these debts in up to 240 months, or 20 years.

s8078289.titulo: Bans tax increases during the pandemic
s8078289.oQueMuda: Governments could not create or raise taxes during the emergency, except to fight it.
s8078289.porQueImporta: Today governments can create or raise taxes during disasters, following normal timing rules. Under the PEC, this would be banned during the disaster, except to fight it.

s8097900.titulo: Extends pension debt installment plans until 2021
s8097900.oQueMuda: Extends installment plans for governments' pension debts to 240 months and allows debt forgiveness.
s8097900.quemAfeta: States, cities and their civil servants.
s8097900.porQueImporta: Today governments with pension debts have shorter installment periods and cannot have debts forgiven. Under the PEC, the period would be up to 240 months and part of the debts would be forgiven.

s8099954.titulo: Creates quotas for Black candidates and by gender in the legislature
s8099954.oQueMuda: Sets minimum shares of candidates of each gender and of Black people, and reserves campaign funds and TV time for them.
s8099954.quemAfeta: Parties, women candidates and Black candidates.
s8099954.porQueImporta: Today the law requires each party to have at least 30% women candidates, and the Constitution reserves 30% of funds for women. Under the PEC, there would also be minimums for Black candidates, with reserved funds and TV time.

s8113511.titulo: Creates the Opportunities Amendment with a minimum income
s8113511.oQueMuda: Guarantees a minimum income and reserves budget money to expand early education and other opportunities.
s8113511.porQueImporta: Today income and early education programs depend on laws and each year's budget. Under the PEC, there would be a guaranteed minimum income and resources reserved in the Constitution to expand early education.

s8138727.titulo: Sends the top three candidates to the runoff
s8138727.oQueMuda: If no one wins a majority in the first round, the three top candidates would compete in the second.
s8138727.quemAfeta: Voters and candidates for president, governor and mayor.
s8138727.porQueImporta: Today, if no one gets more than half of the valid votes, the top two go to a runoff. Under the PEC, the top three would compete in the runoff.

s8154053.titulo: Changes the ICMS on fuel, gas and electricity
s8154053.oQueMuda: Changes how the ICMS is charged on petroleum products, cooking gas and electricity.
s8154053.porQueImporta: Since 2022, fuel and energy have been treated as essential goods with capped ICMS rates. Under the PEC, the way ICMS is charged on oil products, cooking gas and electricity would change.

s8154081.titulo: Bans using the science fund to pay debt
s8154081.oQueMuda: Money from the National Science and Technology Development Fund could not be used to pay down the public debt.
s8154081.porQueImporta: Today part of idle federal fund money can be used to pay public debt. Under the PEC, FNDCT money, the main science fund, could not be used this way.

s8158286.titulo: Creates a national career for public health system doctors
s8158286.oQueMuda: Creates a national career for doctors in the public health system (SUS), with set requirements and pay.
s8158286.quemAfeta: Doctors and patients of the SUS.
s8158286.porQueImporta: Today public health system doctors are hired mostly by city and state governments, each with their own rules. Under the PEC, there would be a national SUS medical career with defined requirements and salary.

s8163561.titulo: Creates Auxílio Brasil and transparency rules for amendments
s8163561.oQueMuda: Replaces Bolsa Família with Auxílio Brasil and requires transparency in carrying out legislators' amendments.
s8163561.porQueImporta: In 2021 Bolsa Família was replaced by Auxílio Brasil, by law, and was renamed Bolsa Família again in 2023. This PEC dealt with that change and with transparency in budget amendment spending.

s8166899.titulo: Makes basic income a social right
s8166899.oQueMuda: Guarantees income to vulnerable families and creates fiscal exceptions to pay for the benefit.
s8166899.porQueImporta: Today Bolsa Família exists by law and depends on each year's budget. Under the PEC, basic income would be a social right, and the benefit would have exceptions to fiscal rules so it can be paid.

s8167542.titulo: Sends part of legislators' amendments to fighting poverty
s8167542.oQueMuda: Part of individual budget amendments would have to go to anti-poverty actions.
s8167542.porQueImporta: Today half of individual budget amendments must go to health, and the rest is free. Under the PEC, a share would have to go to anti-poverty actions.

s7752094.titulo: Applies the salary cap to organizations receiving public money
s7752094.oQueMuda: Nonprofits funded with public resources, such as the 'S System' training bodies, would have to respect the salary cap.
s7752094.quemAfeta: Directors and staff of these organizations.
s7752094.porQueImporta: Today the salary cap applies to public service, but not to bodies such as the 'Sistema S', funded by mandatory contributions. Under the PEC, salaries at these bodies would also have to respect the cap.

s8436103.titulo: Expands the Federal Public Defender's budget
s8436103.oQueMuda: The Federal Public Defender's Office would get yearly increases in its spending limit for 10 years.
s8436103.quemAfeta: People who rely on public defenders, and the defenders.
s8436103.porQueImporta: In 2014 the Constitution set an eight-year deadline for public defenders in every judicial district, a goal the Federal Public Defender's Office did not meet. Under the PEC, its spending limit would rise each year for 10 years.

s8436730.oQueMuda: Medicines for human use would be tax-free.
s8436730.porQueImporta: Today medicines pay taxes, though some have reduced rates; under the tax reform, many will have a 60% reduction or exemption. Under the PEC, all human medicines would be tax-free.

s8437557.titulo: Adds a Federal District appeals judge to the CNJ
