s8437557.oQueMuda: The National Council of Justice would gain an appeals judge from the Federal District Court of Justice.
s8437557.quemAfeta: The Federal District courts and the CNJ.
s8437557.porQueImporta: Today the CNJ has one appellate judge from a state Court of Justice, chosen by the Supreme Court from all states. Under the PEC, there would be an extra seat reserved for the Federal District Court of Justice.

c2084043.titulo: Makes spending on agricultural research mandatory
c2084043.oQueMuda: The government would have to carry out budget funds for scientific research in agriculture and livestock.
c2084043.porQueImporta: Today the budget for agricultural research, such as Embrapa's, can be frozen by the government. Under the PEC, spending it would be mandatory.

s8305239.titulo: Gives special retirement to municipal guards
s8305239.oQueMuda: Municipal guards would be entitled to special retirement.
s8305239.porQueImporta: Today municipal guards follow general civil service retirement rules. Under the PEC, they would have special retirement at a lower age.

s8306962.titulo: Raises the March FPM transfer by 1%
s8306962.oQueMuda: The federal government would hand an extra 1% of its revenue to the Municipal Participation Fund every March.
s8306962.porQueImporta: Today the federal government transfers 22.5% of income tax and IPI to FPM, plus extra shares in July, September and December. Under the PEC, there would be another 1% in March.

s8319791.oQueMuda: Creates a basic income benefit with defined funding sources.
s8319791.porQueImporta: Since 2004 a law has provided for a citizen's basic income, which was never implemented. Under the PEC, there would be a basic income benefit in the Constitution, with defined funding sources.

s8320782.titulo: Bans selling state-owned companies between election and inauguration
s8320782.oQueMuda: Governments could not sell public assets or control of state companies during the transition period.
s8320782.porQueImporta: Today there is no ban on selling state companies or public assets between the election and the new government's inauguration. Under the PEC, this would be banned in that period.

s8329085.titulo: Bans political statements by Supreme Court justices
s8329085.oQueMuda: Justices of the Supreme Court and higher courts could not make political statements, or they would commit an impeachable offense.
s8329085.porQueImporta: Today judges are banned from party-political activity, but there is no impeachable offense for political statements. Under the PEC, Supreme Court and higher-court justices who made political statements could be impeached.

s8331055.titulo: Creates an integrity system and anti-corruption courts
s8331055.oQueMuda: Establishes an integrity system in the judiciary and specialized courts for crimes against public administration.
s8331055.quemAfeta: Courts and defendants in corruption cases.
s8331055.porQueImporta: Today corruption crimes are tried by ordinary or federal criminal courts. Under the PEC, there would be courts specialized in these crimes and an integrity system in the judiciary.

s8332695.titulo: Gives Congress the say on suspending legislators' social media
s8332695.oQueMuda: Only the Chamber and the Senate could suspend or remove their members' online profiles and channels.
s8332695.porQueImporta: Today courts can order lawmakers' social media profiles suspended, as happened in Supreme Court investigations. Under the PEC, only the Chamber or Senate could do so.

s8291388.oQueMuda: The federal government would have to create an ombudsman to receive complaints and fight violence against women.
s8291388.porQueImporta: Today reports of violence against women are received by Ligue 180, a federal hotline, and by police stations. Under the PEC, the federal government would have to maintain a national ombudsman's office provided for in the Constitution.

s8293254.titulo: Creates binding precedents for the Superior Court of Justice
s8293254.oQueMuda: The Superior Court of Justice could issue precedents all judges would have to follow.
s8293254.quemAfeta: Judges, lawyers and parties to cases.
s8293254.porQueImporta: Today only the Supreme Court can issue binding precedents that all judges must follow. Under the PEC, the Superior Court of Justice could too, on federal law questions.

c2351680.oQueMuda: Sets criteria and bans for sentence pardons granted by the President.
c2351680.porQueImporta: Today the president can grant pardons by decree, with bans only for heinous crimes, torture, trafficking and terrorism. Under the PEC, there would be new criteria and prohibitions.

s7741352.titulo: Raises the share of income tax and IPI sent to states to 26%
s7741352.oQueMuda: The share of income tax and IPI for the State Participation Fund would rise by 4.5 points.
s7741352.quemAfeta: State governments and the federal government.
s7741352.porQueImporta: Today the State Participation Fund receives 21.5% of income tax and IPI. Under the PEC, it would receive 26%, and the federal government would keep less.

s8402530.titulo: Adds the Federal Waterway Police to public safety
s8402530.oQueMuda: The Federal Waterway Police would become part of the public safety system.
s8402530.quemAfeta: Residents of river regions and the Federal Police.
s8402530.porQueImporta: Today policing on federal rivers is done mainly by the Federal Police and the Navy. Under the PEC, a Federal Waterway Police would join the public security bodies.

s8406896.titulo: Adds protection of security and health workers to the fundamental rights
s8406896.oQueMuda: States that protection of public security and health workers is guaranteed, as set by law. On its own, it does not say what that protection would be: a law is needed.
s8406896.quemAfeta: Police officers, firefighters, health workers and the government.
s8406896.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution has no specific right to protection for public security and health workers. Under the PEC, this right would be expressly stated, as set by law.

s8407865.titulo: Restricts appointments to state company boards
s8407865.oQueMuda: Bans appointing people with conflicts of interest to boards and management of state-owned companies.
s8407865.porQueImporta: Since 2016 the State Companies Law has banned appointing recent politicians and party leaders to run state companies. Under the PEC, rules against conflicts of interest in these appointments would be in the Constitution.

c2231670.titulo: Creates committees to reduce health lawsuits
c2231670.oQueMuda: States would have multi-agency committees to resolve health requests without going to court.
c2231670.quemAfeta: Patients, the public health system (SUS) and the judiciary.
c2231670.porQueImporta: Today patients who cannot get medicines or treatment from the public health system go to court, and there are hundreds of thousands of such cases. Under the PEC, each state would have committees to resolve these requests without a lawsuit.

s8220747.titulo: Lets all judges vote to elect court leadership
s8220747.oQueMuda: Court leadership (except the internal affairs office) would be elected by all tenured first- and second-instance judges in the region, by secret ballot, for 2-year terms.
s8220747.porQueImporta: Today court leadership is elected only by appellate judges. Under the PEC, all tenured judges, first and second instance, would vote by secret ballot, for 2-year terms.

s8221418.titulo: Allows converting hazardous work time to regular time for retirement
s8221418.oQueMuda: Social security contributors who worked in hazardous activities could convert that time into regular time.
s8221418.porQueImporta: Since the 2019 reform, people who worked exposed to health hazards cannot convert that special time into regular time to retire earlier. Under the PEC, conversion would be allowed again.

s8222502.titulo: Reserves women-only lists for court seats
s8222502.oQueMuda: One in every two nomination lists for the 'constitutional fifth' seats would be made up only of women.
s8222502.quemAfeta: Women lawyers, prosecutors and the courts.
s8222502.porQueImporta: Today the 'fifth' lists of lawyers and prosecutors for appeal courts have no gender reservation. Under the PEC, one in every two lists would include only women.

s8230006.oQueMuda: Donations of goods and services for humanitarian aid would be tax-free.
s8230006.porQueImporta: Today donations of goods and services pay taxes like ordinary sales, except for specific exemptions. Under the PEC, donations for humanitarian action would be tax-free.

s8394951.titulo: Alternates where provisional measures start between Chamber and Senate
s8394951.oQueMuda: Provisional measures would start alternately in the Chamber and the Senate, and joint committees would be abolished.
s8394951.porQueImporta: Today provisional measures go through a joint committee and start in the Chamber. Under the PEC, they would start alternately in the Chamber and Senate, without a joint committee.

c2132847.titulo: Sends work-related social security cases to the Labor Courts
c2132847.oQueMuda: Cases about work-related social security benefits, such as accidents, would go to the Labor Courts.
c2132847.quemAfeta: Injured workers and the national social security institute (INSS).
c2132847.porQueImporta: Today lawsuits against INSS over workplace accident benefits are tried by state courts. Under the PEC, they would go to the Labor Courts.

s7760703.titulo: Bans pardons for heinous and corruption crimes
s7760703.oQueMuda: The President could not pardon sentences for heinous crimes, money laundering and crimes against public administration.
s7760703.porQueImporta: Today the president cannot pardon heinous crimes, torture, trafficking and terrorism, but can pardon corruption and money laundering. Under the PEC, these would also be banned.

s8373076.titulo: Strengthens protection of final court rulings
s8373076.oQueMuda: Reaffirms that final rulings cannot be undone, including by changes in Supreme Court interpretation.
s8373076.quemAfeta: Taxpayers and parties to closed cases.
s8373076.porQueImporta: In 2023 the Supreme Court ruled that final decisions on taxes charged continuously lose effect when the court changes its view. Under the PEC, final decisions could not be undone by such changes.

c2222337.titulo: Shares pre-salt auction revenue with states and cities
c2222337.oQueMuda: The federal government would share with states and cities revenue from the pre-salt oil rights auction.
c2222337.quemAfeta: States, cities and the federal government.
c2222337.porQueImporta: In 2019 another amendment (102) already authorized sharing part of the money from the pre-salt transfer-of-rights auction with states and municipalities. This PEC dealt with the same issue.

c2351620.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for loans to other countries
c2351620.oQueMuda: Federal public banks could only lend to foreign countries with Congress's authorization.
c2351620.quemAfeta: The BNDES and other public banks.
c2351620.porQueImporta: Today federal public banks can lend to other countries without congressional approval. Under the PEC, these loans would depend on lawmakers' authorization.

s1400311.titulo: Sets deadlines to appoint officials approved by the Senate
s1400311.oQueMuda: Creates deadlines to choose and appoint officials such as agency directors, with an impeachable offense if missed.
s1400311.porQueImporta: Today there is no deadline for the president to nominate or appoint officials after Senate approval, and agency posts stay vacant for months. Under the PEC, there would be deadlines, and missing them would be an impeachable offense.

s1401169.titulo: Requires a complementary law for concession rules
s1401169.oQueMuda: Public service concessions and permits would be regulated by a complementary law.
s1401169.quemAfeta: Concession holders and public service users.
s1401169.porQueImporta: Today public service concessions are regulated by ordinary law, passed by simple majority. Under the PEC, they would require a complementary law, which needs an absolute majority to pass or change.

s3037753.titulo: Changes how the Cide fuel tax is shared with states and cities
s3037753.oQueMuda: Redistributes the revenue from the Cide fuel tax differently among states and cities.
s3037753.porQueImporta: Today 29% of the fuel levy (Cide) goes to states, which pass 25% of that to municipalities. Under the PEC, this split would change.

s7411048.titulo: Makes it easier to arrest and prosecute legislators
s7411048.oQueMuda: Allows arresting legislators after a second-instance conviction and ends Congress's power to block arrests and cases.
s7411048.porQueImporta: Today lawmakers can only be arrested when caught in the act of a non-bailable crime, and their house can vote to release them or suspend the case. Under the PEC, they could be imprisoned after an appeal-court conviction, and Congress would lose the power to block arrests and prosecutions.

s1401465.oQueMuda: Changes the system of government to parliamentarism, with a prime minister.
s1401465.porQueImporta: Today the elected president is both head of state and of government; in 1993 voters chose this system in a referendum. Under the PEC, a prime minister backed by Congress would head the government.

s1401414.titulo: Changes how attorneys general are chosen
s1401414.oQueMuda: The Prosecutor General could also come from state prosecutors' offices, and attorneys general would have to step down before seeking reappointment.
s1401414.porQueImporta: Today the Prosecutor General is chosen among federal prosecutors and can be reappointed without leaving office. Under the PEC, he or she could also come from state prosecution services, and anyone seeking reappointment would have to resign first.

s7914500.titulo: Creates a fixed term and list of three for the Federal Police chief
s7914500.oQueMuda: The Federal Police director would be chosen from a list of three, with a three-year term and Senate approval.
s7914500.quemAfeta: The Federal Police and the Presidency.
s7914500.porQueImporta: Today the Federal Police director is freely chosen by the president, with no fixed term. Under the PEC, he or she would come from a list of three names, serve a three-year term and need Senate approval.

s7989488.titulo: Requires officeholders to step down to seek reelection
s7989488.oQueMuda: The President, governors and mayors seeking reelection would have to take leave six months before.
s7989488.quemAfeta: Heads of the executive and voters.
s7989488.porQueImporta: Today the president, governors and mayors can run for re-election without leaving office. Under the PEC, they would have to step down six months before the election.

c2325720.titulo: Halves city governments' social security contributions
c2325720.oQueMuda: Cities would pay half the contribution rate on their payroll.
c2325720.porQueImporta: Today city governments pay INSS 20% of the payroll of staff without their own pension system. Under the PEC, they would pay half, and INSS would not receive the difference.

c501028.titulo: Allows using court-ordered government debts to buy a home
c501028.oQueMuda: Credits from court-ordered government debts (precatórios) could be used to buy a home.
c501028.porQueImporta: Today people owed court-ordered payments wait in the government's payment queue or sell the credit at a discount. Under the PEC, they could use it to buy a home.

s1401223.titulo: Guarantees women seats on Congress's governing boards and committees
s1401223.oQueMuda: The makeup of governing boards and committees would have to be proportional to the number of each gender.
s1401223.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution requires party proportionality in leadership boards and committees, but not gender proportionality. Under the PEC, composition would also have to reflect the number of men and women in the house.

s8392917.titulo: Changes where the President's bills start
s8392917.oQueMuda: Bills from the President and the courts could start in the Senate, not only in the Chamber.
s8392917.porQueImporta: Today bills from the president and courts always start in the Chamber. Under the PEC, they could start in the Senate.

s8133142.titulo: Requires free, science-based public health care
s8133142.oQueMuda: Public health actions and services would have to be free and based on scientific evidence.
s8133142.quemAfeta: Patients of the public health system (SUS).
s8133142.porQueImporta: Today the public health system is free by law and there is no constitutional requirement of a scientific basis for its services. Under the PEC, public health services would have to be free and evidence-based, by constitutional rule.

s8171441.titulo: Sets rules for adding new treatments to the public health system
s8171441.oQueMuda: Creates criteria for adding new medicines and procedures to the SUS, with mandatory prior review.
s8171441.porQueImporta: Since 2011 a law has required review by Conitec before the public health system adopts new medicines and procedures. Under the PEC, criteria for adoption would be in the Constitution.

s1394077.titulo: Reserves legislative seats for people with disabilities
s1394077.oQueMuda: Seats in the Chamber, state assemblies and city councils would be reserved for people with disabilities for four legislatures.
s1394077.porQueImporta: Today there are no reserved seats in legislatures for any group. Under the PEC, seats would be reserved for people with disabilities in the Chamber, state legislatures and city councils for four terms.

s1394130.titulo: Creates the Racial Equality Promotion Fund
s1394130.oQueMuda: Creates a fund for policies including Black Brazilians in housing, education and job training.
s1394130.porQueImporta: Today policies for Black Brazilians depend on each year's budget. Under the PEC, 1% of income tax and IPI would go to a Racial Equality Promotion Fund.

s1394231.titulo: Gives priority to bills on the same subject as provisional measures
s1394231.oQueMuda: Bills on the same topic as a provisional measure would be reviewed alongside it, with priority for the oldest.
s1394231.porQueImporta: Today provisional measures have priority and block the agenda, while lawmakers' bills on the same topic take a back seat. Under the PEC, they would be considered together with the measure, with priority to the older text.

s1394282.titulo: Creates national rules for public service exams
s1394282.oQueMuda: Exams would have to offer all open positions, and exams just for a waiting list or new exams with approved candidates still waiting would be banned.
s1394282.porQueImporta: Today public bodies can hold exams only for a reserve list and open new exams while approved candidates are waiting. Under the PEC, this would be banned, and all open positions would have to be offered.

s1394688.titulo: Extends special retirement rules for teachers in the transition
s1394688.oQueMuda: Basic education teachers would get five years off the requirements under the 2005 transition rule too.
s1394688.porQueImporta: Today basic education teachers have a five-year reduction under general rules, but not under one of the 2005 transition rules. Under the PEC, the reduction would also apply to that rule.

s1394843.titulo: Adjusts pensions by the most favorable inflation index
s1394843.oQueMuda: Social security benefits would be adjusted by the inflation index most favorable to retirees.
s1394843.quemAfeta: Retirees and pensioners of the national social security system.
s1394843.porQueImporta: Today INSS benefits are adjusted by the INPC, an inflation index set by law. Under the PEC, the inflation index giving retirees the largest raise would be used.

s1394997.titulo: Calls an assembly to carry out political reform
s1394997.oQueMuda: Voters would elect representatives to a review assembly devoted only to political and electoral reform.
s1394997.porQueImporta: Today changes to political and electoral rules are made by Congress itself. Under the PEC, voters would choose representatives for an assembly devoted only to political reform.

s1402212.oQueMuda: People not affiliated with parties could run in elections.
s1402212.porQueImporta: Today one can only run for office as a member of a party. Under the PEC, people without a party could also run.

s7242157.titulo: Automatically removes legislators convicted under the Clean Record Law
s7242157.oQueMuda: Deputies and senators convicted of crimes that cause ineligibility would lose their seats automatically.
s7242157.porQueImporta: Today a lawmaker convicted of a crime only loses the seat after a vote in the Chamber or Senate. Under the PEC, the loss would be automatic if the crime causes ineligibility under the Clean Record Law.

s7399577.titulo: Reserves 2% of legislators' amendments for sports
s7399577.oQueMuda: At least 2% of individual budget amendments would go to sports.
s7399577.porQueImporta: Today half of individual budget amendments must go to health, and the rest is free. Under the PEC, at least 2% would have to go to sport.

c1280152.titulo: Charges ICMS on interstate electricity sales
c1280152.oQueMuda: The ICMS would apply to electricity transactions between states.
c1280152.porQueImporta: Today electricity sold from one state to another pays no ICMS in the state of origin; the tax goes to the state where it is consumed. Under the PEC, the producing state would also charge ICMS on these sales.

c1594140.titulo: Allows reducing states' delegations in the Chamber
c1594140.oQueMuda: Ends the rule that prevents reducing the number of deputies from each state.
c1594140.porQueImporta: Today each state has between 8 and 70 federal deputies, and a rule prevents reducing a state's delegation. Under the PEC, this rule would end, and seats could be redistributed by population.

c609753.titulo: Federal aid to pay the nursing salary floor
c609753.oQueMuda:
Federal aid: the federal government gives financial support to states, municipalities, charities and private providers serving at least 60% of patients through SUS so they can pay the nursing minimum wage, with its own budget line.
Payroll limits: the extra spending on the minimum wage did not count toward payroll limits in the first year and is phased in, 10% a year.
Funding source: surpluses from federal public funds may pay the minimum wage from 2023 to 2027.
c609753.quemAfeta: Nursing professionals, municipalities, state governments, charity hospitals and hospitals serving SUS.
c609753.porQueImporta: In force since December 2022. The nursing minimum wage was created by law in 2022, but states, municipalities and hospitals said they could not afford it; the amendment set that the federal government helps pay.

c1701050.titulo: Bans creating costs for governments without naming a funding source
c1701050.oQueMuda: Laws could not impose costs on federal, state and city governments without provision in the budget.
c1701050.porQueImporta: Already in force (Amendment 128 of 2022): federal laws cannot create expenses for states and municipalities without indicating where the money will come from.

c43596.titulo: Guarantees yearly funding for the Amazon and Northeast funds
c43596.oQueMuda: A law would set mandatory yearly amounts for these regions' development funds.
c43596.quemAfeta: Companies and governments in the Amazon and Northeast.
c43596.porQueImporta: Today the Amazon and Northeast development funds receive amounts set in each year's budget. Under the PEC, a law would set mandatory annual amounts.

c2194899.titulo: Takes federal university spending out of the cap (text of the Transition PEC)
c2194899.oQueMuda: Excludes federal education institutions' spending from the spending cap; in 2022 it was the text used to vote on the Transition PEC.
c2194899.porQueImporta: In 2022 this text was used in the Chamber to vote on the Transition PEC, which allowed spending outside the cap in 2023, such as the R$600 Bolsa Família. The original proposal removed federal university spending from the cap.

c620527.oQueMuda: Federal and state governments would have to spend a minimum percentage on cultural heritage and cultural production.
c620527.porQueImporta: Today health and education have mandatory minimum spending, but culture does not. Under the PEC, the federal government, states and the Federal District would have to spend a minimum share of revenue on culture.

c2095531.titulo: Adds reciprocity to the principles of foreign policy
c2095531.oQueMuda: Adds 'reciprocity' (treating other countries as they treat Brazil) to the list of principles of international relations. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2095531.quemAfeta: The federal government, diplomacy and Brazilians abroad.
c2095531.porQueImporta: Today the foreign policy principles in the Constitution include national independence, human rights and non-intervention, but not reciprocity. Under the PEC, reciprocity would be added.

c2194813.oQueMuda: Cooking gas for household use would be tax-free.
c2194813.porQueImporta: Today cooking gas pays ICMS and other taxes. Under the PEC, gas for household use would be tax-free, and states and the federal government would stop collecting on it.

c2230007.titulo: Guarantees income for families in poverty
c2230007.oQueMuda: Social assistance would have to guarantee cash transfers to poor and extremely poor families.
c2230007.porQueImporta: Today Bolsa Família exists by law, and the Constitution has provided a family basic income since 2021. Under the PEC, social assistance would have the duty to guarantee cash transfers to poor and extremely poor families.

c2285501.titulo: Let cities pay pension debts in 240 installments
c2285501.oQueMuda: In 2021, cities could pay their social security debts in up to 240 monthly installments.
c2285501.porQueImporta: In 2021, municipalities gained the option to pay pension debts in up to 240 months. This PEC deals with that installment plan.

c2304959.titulo: Puts climate security into the Constitution
c2304959.oQueMuda: Adds 'climate security' to the fundamental rights and to the principles of the economy, and tells the government to act against climate change and its effects. It does not say which actions nor create funding.
c2304959.quemAfeta: The whole population, companies and governments.
c2304959.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution guarantees an ecologically balanced environment, without mentioning climate. Under the PEC, climate security would be added to fundamental rights and economic principles, and governments would have a duty to act against climate change.

c2336964.titulo: Federal aid to pay the nursing minimum wage
c2336964.oQueMuda: The federal government would give financial support to states, cities and charities to meet the nursing minimum salary.
c2336964.porQueImporta: This proposal was shelved; federal aid to pay the nursing salary floor entered the Constitution in 2022 through another PEC (Amendment 127).

s7728717.titulo: Adds the National Force to the public safety bodies
s7728717.oQueMuda: The National Public Safety Force would be a permanent body for cooperation among governments.
s7728717.quemAfeta: The National Force and the states.
s7728717.porQueImporta: Today the National Public Security Force exists by decree and law and acts when states request support. Under the PEC, it would be a permanent body in the Constitution.

s7732135.titulo: Separates electoral crimes from ordinary crimes in court cases
s7732135.oQueMuda: Ordinary crimes linked to electoral crimes would be tried by the regular courts.
s7732135.quemAfeta: Defendants in corruption and slush-fund cases.
s7732135.porQueImporta: Since 2019, under a Supreme Court ruling, ordinary crimes linked to electoral crimes, such as corruption tied to illegal campaign funds, are tried by Electoral Courts. Under the PEC, they would go to ordinary courts.

s7733509.titulo: Allows holding two public journalist jobs
s7733509.oQueMuda: Journalists could hold two public posts with compatible hours.
s7733509.porQueImporta: Today civil servants can only hold two public posts in listed cases, such as teachers and health professionals. Under the PEC, journalists could too.

s7738877.oQueMuda: Limits the number and duration of provisional measures, bans them on labor matters and bans unrelated add-ons.
s7738877.porQueImporta: Today there is no limit on the number of provisional measures, and Congress often adds unrelated amendments. Under the PEC, there would be limits on number and duration, measures on labor would be banned, and so would unrelated amendments.

s7741158.titulo: Requires technical selection of federal audit court ministers
s7741158.oQueMuda: Federal audit court ministers would be chosen from auditors and prosecutors with no recent elected office.
s7741158.porQueImporta: Today of the 9 Federal Audit Court ministers, 6 are chosen by Congress and 3 by the president, and many were politicians. Under the PEC, they would be chosen among audit court auditors and prosecutors, without recent elected office.

s7745408.titulo: Ends 60-day vacations and allows judges to be dismissed
s7745408.oQueMuda: Judges and prosecutors would have 30 days of vacation, would not be punished with retirement and could be dismissed.
s7745408.porQueImporta: Today judges and prosecutors have 60 days of vacation, and the maximum administrative penalty is compulsory retirement with proportional pay. Under the PEC, they would have 30 days of vacation and could lose their post as punishment.

s7748831.titulo: Allows public universities to charge for services
s7748831.oQueMuda: Universities could charge for services they provide and manage their own revenue.
s7748831.porQueImporta: Today money federal universities earn from services goes into the federal budget and can be frozen. Under the PEC, they could charge for services and manage these funds themselves.

s7752601.titulo: Moves the rural land tax to the municipalities
s7752601.oQueMuda: Cities would collect the rural land tax (ITR), now charged by the federal government.
s7752601.porQueImporta: Today the ITR rural land tax is federal, and half goes to the municipality, or all of it if the municipality handles collection. Under the PEC, the tax would become municipal.

s7753619.titulo: Caps interest rates charged by banks
s7753619.oQueMuda: Banks could not charge more than three times the Selic benchmark rate.
s7753619.porQueImporta: Today there is no limit on bank interest rates, and revolving credit card and overdraft rates are among the highest in the world. Under the PEC, no rate could exceed three times the Selic rate.

s7759040.titulo: Adjusts federal transfers to cities for inflation
s7759040.oQueMuda: Balances of federal programs with cities would be updated for inflation every year.
s7759040.porQueImporta: Today balances of federal programs with municipalities have fixed values, without automatic adjustment. Under the PEC, they would be adjusted for inflation every year.

s7759495.titulo: Requires drug testing of police and firefighters
s7759495.oQueMuda: Public safety professionals would undergo periodic drug testing.
s7759495.porQueImporta: Today professional truck and bus drivers already take drug tests, but there is no national rule for police and firefighters. Under the PEC, they would take periodic drug tests.

s7774325.oQueMuda: Products made mainly from recycled material would be tax-free.
s7774325.porQueImporta: Today recycled products pay taxes like any others. Under the PEC, products made mainly with recycled material would be tax-free.

s7775664.titulo: Bans reissuing decrees struck down by Congress
s7775664.oQueMuda: The government could not reissue, in the same year, a decree halted by Congress.
s7775664.porQueImporta: Today Congress can suspend a presidential decree, but the government can issue a similar one. Under the PEC, reissuing a suspended decree in the same year would be banned.

s7775894.titulo: Raises the share of income tax and IPI sent to cities to 30%
s7775894.oQueMuda: An extra 5.5% of these taxes would go to the Municipal Participation Fund.
s7775894.porQueImporta: Today FPM receives 22.5% of income tax and IPI, plus extra 1% shares in three months of the year. Under the PEC, it would receive 5.5 percentage points more, and the federal government would keep less.

s7786111.oQueMuda: Mayors and council members elected in 2020 would serve six years to unify elections in 2026.
s7786111.porQueImporta: Today municipal and general elections alternate every two years. Under the PEC, mayors and councilors elected in 2020 would have 6-year terms, with no election in 2024, to unify the calendar in 2026.

s7798303.titulo: Guarantees minimum public investment of 1.5% of GDP
s7798303.oQueMuda: The federal government would have to invest at least 1.5% of GDP, outside the spending cap.
s7798303.porQueImporta: Today there is no minimum for federal public investment in works and equipment. Under the PEC, the federal government would have to invest at least 1.5% of GDP a year, outside the spending limit.

s7811689.titulo: Allows endowment funds for federal universities
s7811689.oQueMuda: Universities could create funds from donations, and donors would get tax benefits.
s7811689.porQueImporta: Since 2019 a law has allowed endowment funds with donations for universities, with no tax benefit for donors. Under the PEC, these funds would have a constitutional basis and donors would get tax deductions.

s7822485.titulo: Uses regional funds for state and city infrastructure
s7822485.oQueMuda: For five years, 30% of the North, Northeast and Center-West funds would go to infrastructure works.
s7822485.quemAfeta: States and cities in these regions.
s7822485.porQueImporta: Today the North, Northeast and Center-West constitutional funds lend money to companies and producers. Under the PEC, for five years, 30% of that money would go to state and municipal infrastructure works.

s7822487.titulo: Compensates states and cities hosting rocket launch bases
s7822487.oQueMuda: Places with aerospace launch centers would receive compensation and a social fund.
s7822487.quemAfeta: Residents of Alcântara (Maranhão) and the surrounding region.
s7822487.porQueImporta: Today there is no specific compensation for states and municipalities hosting rocket launch centers, such as Alcântara in Maranhão. Under the PEC, they would receive financial compensation and a social fund.

s7828021.titulo: Protects pregnant civil servants in appointed posts
s7828021.oQueMuda: Women in appointed posts could not be dismissed from pregnancy until five months after birth.
s7828021.quemAfeta: Women civil servants in appointed posts.
s7828021.porQueImporta: Today formally employed women and tenured civil servants have job stability from pregnancy until five months after birth; for appointees, the guarantee comes from a Supreme Court ruling. Under the PEC, this protection would be in the Constitution.

s7845448.titulo: Creates a national fund for environmental emergencies
s7845448.oQueMuda: Creates a fund of the federal government and coastal states to prevent and repair environmental disasters.
s7845448.quemAfeta: Coastal residents and people in risk areas.
s7845448.porQueImporta: Today money for environmental disasters comes from each year's budget. Under the PEC, there would be a fund of the federal government and coastal states to prevent and repair such disasters.

s7971591.titulo: Adds fighting corruption to the foundations of the Republic
s7971591.oQueMuda: Adds 'preventing and fighting corruption' to the country's foundations, alongside sovereignty, citizenship and human dignity. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s7971591.quemAfeta: The whole population, public bodies and lawmakers.
s7971591.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution requires integrity in public administration, but fighting corruption is not among the foundations of the Republic, which are sovereignty, citizenship, human dignity, the value of work and political pluralism. Under the PEC, it would be added.

s8153922.titulo: Lets legislators become ambassadors without losing their seats
s8153922.oQueMuda: Deputies and senators could head embassies without losing their seats.
s8153922.porQueImporta: Today deputies and senators can only step aside without losing their seat to become ministers, secretaries or heads of temporary diplomatic missions. Under the PEC, they could head permanent embassies.

s8228548.titulo: Defines what happens to public forests
s8228548.oQueMuda: Sets deadlines and rules for allocating public forest land and bans transferring it to third parties in some cases.
s8228548.quemAfeta: Forest communities, governments and land occupants.
s8228548.porQueImporta: Today there are millions of hectares of public forests without a defined use, and the law sets no deadline. Under the PEC, there would be deadlines and rules for allocating these areas, and transfers to private parties would be banned in some cases.

s7711916.titulo: Requires open votes to elect Congress's leadership
s7711916.oQueMuda: The speakers of the Chamber and the Senate would be chosen by open vote.
s7711916.porQueImporta: Today the heads of the Chamber and Senate are elected by secret ballot. Under the PEC, the vote would be open, and voters would know whom each lawmaker voted for.

s7717123.titulo: Ends the benefit for prisoners' families
s7717123.oQueMuda: The benefit paid to prisoners' dependents would end.
s7717123.porQueImporta: Today the prisoner's family benefit is paid to dependents of low-income prisoners who contributed to INSS. Under the PEC, this benefit would cease to exist.

s7717281.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility to 16
s7717281.oQueMuda: Only people under 16 would be exempt from criminal responsibility.
s7717281.quemAfeta: Teenagers aged 16 and 17 and the justice system.
s7717281.porQueImporta: Today people under 18 are subject to the Child and Adolescent Statute, with at most 3 years of detention. Under the PEC, 16- and 17-year-olds would be tried and imprisoned as adults.

s7718602.titulo: Allows imprisonment after a second-instance conviction
s7718602.oQueMuda: Sentences would start after conviction by an appeals court, even with appeals pending.
s7718602.porQueImporta: Today, under a 2019 Supreme Court ruling, a sentence only begins after all appeals are exhausted. Under the PEC, it would begin after conviction by an appeal court.

s7724131.titulo: Counts military service in police entrance exams
s7724131.oQueMuda: Mandatory military service would count as a credential or tiebreaker in exams for police, firefighters and municipal guards.
s7724131.porQueImporta: Today police, firefighter and guard exams give no points for military service, except under each notice's rules. Under the PEC, compulsory military service would count as a credential or tiebreaker.

s7726829.titulo: Punishes trading posts for political advantage
s7726829.oQueMuda: Appointing or dismissing people to gain political advantage or influence another branch would be misconduct.
s7726829.porQueImporta: Today the Administrative Misconduct Law does not specifically cover appointing or dismissing someone for political advantage. Under the PEC, this conduct would be misconduct, with penalties such as loss of office and political rights.

s7728643.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility to 15 for serious crimes
s7728643.oQueMuda: Young people aged 15 to 17 could be tried as adults for serious crimes, based on a judge's assessment.
s7728643.porQueImporta: Today people under 18 are subject to the Child and Adolescent Statute, with at most 3 years of detention. Under the PEC, 15- to 17-year-olds could be tried as adults for serious crimes, at the judge's discretion.

s7730777.titulo: Changes how ICMS is split among cities
s7730777.oQueMuda: Lowers from 75% to 50% the share of ICMS split according to each city's economic activity.
s7730777.porQueImporta: Today 25% of ICMS goes to municipalities, and at least 65% of that share is split by each town's economic activity (75% until 2020). Under this 2019 PEC, that criterion would drop to 50%, with the rest following each state's rules.

s7731793.oQueMuda: Only parties with 5% of the vote for the Chamber or 20 deputies would be represented in Congress.
s7731793.porQueImporta: Since 2017 there has been a gradual performance threshold that by 2030 will require 3% of Chamber votes or 15 deputies for a party to get public funds and TV time. Under the PEC, only parties with 5% of votes or 20 deputies would be represented in Congress.

s7733746.oQueMuda: Merit-based promotion of judges would consider the top half of the seniority list.
s7733746.porQueImporta: Today, in merit-based promotions, judges in the first fifth of the seniority list compete. Under the PEC, the first half of the list would compete.

s7733785.titulo: Makes the Fundeb education fund permanent
s7733785.oQueMuda: The main fund financing basic education would no longer have an end date.
s7733785.porQueImporta: Already in force through another PEC (Amendment 108 of 2020): Fundeb, which pays much of teachers' salaries, became permanent, with a gradual increase in the federal share.

s7737914.titulo: Takes public investment out of the spending cap
s7737914.oQueMuda: Investment spending would not count toward the spending cap.
s7737914.quemAfeta: The federal government and public works sectors.
s7737914.porQueImporta: This 2019 PEC proposed removing public investment from the spending cap created in 2016. The cap was eventually replaced in 2023 by another fiscal rule.

s7738872.titulo: Guarantees minimum federal funding for public safety
s7738872.oQueMuda: The federal government would spend increasing amounts on the Unified Public Safety System, up to 2.5% of its revenue.
s7738872.porQueImporta: Today public security has no mandatory federal minimum spending. Under the PEC, the federal government would spend growing amounts on the Unified Public Security System, up to 2.5% of its revenue.

s7741423.titulo: Requires a list of three to choose the Prosecutor General
s7741423.oQueMuda: The Prosecutor General would be chosen from a list drawn up by members of the prosecution service.
s7741423.porQueImporta: Today the president freely chooses the Prosecutor General among career prosecutors, with Senate approval. Under the PEC, the choice would have to come from a list voted by prosecutors.

s7741529.titulo: Bans special pension plans for politicians
s7741529.oQueMuda: There could be no separate retirement systems for elected officials.
s7741529.porQueImporta: Since the 2019 reform, new lawmakers cannot join Congress's own pension plan. Under the PEC, no special retirement regime for elected officials could exist.

s7741534.oQueMuda: Repeals Amendment 95, which created the public spending cap.
s7741534.quemAfeta: The federal government and public policies.
s7741534.porQueImporta: This 2019 PEC proposed repealing the spending cap created in 2016. The cap was eventually replaced in 2023 by another fiscal rule.
s7741534.apelido: End of the Spending Cap PEC

s7746248.oQueMuda: Federal, state and city governments would create funds for infrastructure in metropolitan regions.
s7746248.porQueImporta: Today there is no constitutional fund for works in metropolitan regions, which depend on each government. Under the PEC, the federal, state and municipal governments would create infrastructure funds for these regions.

s7748924.titulo: Brings back coalitions in city council elections
s7748924.oQueMuda: Parties could form coalitions in municipal proportional elections.
s7748924.porQueImporta: Since 2020 coalitions have been banned in elections for councilors and deputies. Under the PEC, they would again be allowed in council elections.

s7748936.titulo: Makes Fundeb permanent with universal access targets
s7748936.oQueMuda: Makes Fundeb permanent and requires targets to make basic education universal and expand daycare.
s7748936.porQueImporta: Already in force through another PEC (Amendment 108 of 2020): Fundeb, which pays much of teachers' salaries, became permanent, with a gradual increase in the federal share.

s7749502.titulo: Gives the Federal District ownership of its constitutional fund
s7749502.oQueMuda: Money in the fund that pays for police, firefighters and services in the Federal District would belong to the district.
s7749502.quemAfeta: The government and residents of the Federal District.
s7749502.porQueImporta: Today the Federal District Constitutional Fund, which pays for police, firefighters, health and education, is managed by the federal government. Under the PEC, this money would belong to the Federal District.

s7752275.titulo: Bans pardons for people convicted of corruption
s7752275.oQueMuda: The President could not pardon sentences for crimes against public administration, except on humanitarian grounds.
s7752275.porQueImporta: Today the president can pardon people convicted of corruption. Under the PEC, this would be banned, except on humanitarian grounds.

s7753204.titulo: Takes pre-salt bonus transfers out of the spending cap
s7753204.oQueMuda: Transfers to states and cities from the oil signing bonus would not count toward the spending cap.
s7753204.quemAfeta: States, cities and the federal government.
s7753204.porQueImporta: In 2019, pre-salt auction money passed to states and municipalities was kept outside the spending cap. This PEC dealt with that exception.

s7756801.titulo: Takes health out of the spending cap
s7756801.oQueMuda: The health minimum would be adjusted above inflation and kept outside the spending cap.
s7756801.quemAfeta: Patients of the public health system (SUS) and the government.
s7756801.porQueImporta: Between 2017 and 2022, the spending cap limited minimum health spending to inflation adjustment; since 2023 the fiscal rule has changed. This 2019 PEC proposed raising minimum health spending above inflation and removing it from the cap.

s7783547.oQueMuda: Bans appointing relatives to positions of trust, with penalties for misconduct.
s7783547.porQueImporta: Since 2008, a binding Supreme Court precedent has banned appointing relatives to positions of trust. Under the PEC, the ban would be in the Constitution, with penalties for misconduct.

s7788352.titulo: Bans forced retirement as a punishment for judges
s7788352.oQueMuda: Judges could no longer be punished with retirement in the public interest.
s7788352.porQueImporta: Today the maximum administrative penalty for judges is compulsory retirement with pay proportional to time served. Under the PEC, this form of punishment would no longer exist.

s7788918.titulo: Bans taxes on the basic food basket
s7788918.oQueMuda: Federal, state and city governments could not tax products in the basic food basket.
s7788918.porQueImporta: The 2023 tax reform zeroed taxes on a national basic food basket defined by law. Under this 2019 PEC, no government could tax basic food basket products.

s7797419.titulo: Uses privatization money for pensions and debt
s7797419.oQueMuda: Money from selling federal property and state companies would go to social security and paying the public debt.
s7797419.porQueImporta: Today money from privatizations and federal property sales generally goes to paying public debt. Under the PEC, it would have to go to social security and debt.

s7801877.oQueMuda: Officials could give up their special court privilege and be tried in lower courts.
s7801877.porQueImporta: Today special jurisdiction is mandatory: officials who have it cannot choose to be tried at first instance. Under the PEC, they could waive this right.

s7804584.titulo: Adds conciliation and mediation to the fundamental rights
s7804584.oQueMuda: States that the State will ensure ways of settling disputes outside the courts, such as conciliation and mediation. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s7804584.quemAfeta: People in disputes, lawyers and the courts.
s7804584.porQueImporta: The Code of Civil Procedure already encourages these methods; the change puts them in the Constitution.

s7812089.titulo: Sends half of legislators' amendments to health and education
s7812089.oQueMuda: Half of individual budget amendments would go to health and education, in equal parts.
s7812089.porQueImporta: Today half of individual budget amendments must go to health, and the rest is free. Under the PEC, half would go to health and education in equal parts.

s7812302.titulo: Bans perks for former elected officials
s7812302.oQueMuda: Former presidents, governors and legislators would get no pensions, cars, security or staff paid by the state.
s7812302.porQueImporta: Today former presidents are entitled by law to government-paid security, drivers and aides. Under the PEC, no benefit arising solely from holding office, such as pensions, health plans or staff, could be given to former politicians at any level.

s7812304.titulo: Bans provisional measures on labor and pensions that cut rights
s7812304.oQueMuda: Provisional measures on labor and pensions would only be allowed to expand benefits.
s7812304.porQueImporta: Today the president can issue provisional measures on labor and pensions, including ones reducing rights. Under the PEC, measures in these areas could only expand benefits.

s7831603.titulo: Creates a fund against oil pollution
s7831603.oQueMuda: Creates a fund to fight and reduce damage from oil and fuel spills.
s7831603.porQueImporta: In 2019, an oil spill hit hundreds of beaches in the Northeast and Southeast, and the response was paid from each agency's budget. Under the PEC, there would be a dedicated fund to fight and repair oil spill damage.

s7834578.titulo: Requires a plurality of ideas on radio and TV
s7834578.oQueMuda: Broadcasters would have to follow the principle of diversity of opinion in their programming.
s7834578.porQueImporta: Today the Constitution requires radio and TV to prioritize educational, cultural and informative purposes, but does not mention plurality of opinions. Under the PEC, diversity of opinions would become a mandatory programming principle.

s7834859.titulo: Lets prosecutors receive tax data without a court order
s7834859.oQueMuda: Oversight bodies would share tax and banking data with prosecutors without a court's authorization.
s7834859.quemAfeta: People under investigation, the tax authority, the financial intelligence unit (Coaf) and prosecutors.
s7834859.porQueImporta: In 2019 the Supreme Court ruled that the tax authority and the financial intelligence unit can share data with prosecutors without a court order, under some conditions. Under the PEC, this sharing, including bank data, would be in the Constitution.

s7838773.titulo: Protects Suframa's own revenue from freezes
s7838773.oQueMuda: Fees and fines collected by the Manaus Free Trade Zone authority could not be frozen.
s7838773.quemAfeta: Suframa and companies in the Free Trade Zone.
s7838773.porQueImporta: Today fees and fines collected by Suframa go into the federal budget and can be frozen. Under the PEC, this money would be protected from freezes.

s7845422.titulo: Requires Congress's approval to clear the Amazon
s7845422.oQueMuda: Cutting vegetation in the Amazon rainforest would require prior approval from Congress.
s7845422.quemAfeta: Farmers, forest peoples and environmental agencies.
s7845422.porQueImporta: Today clearing vegetation in the Amazon requires authorization from environmental agencies, with 80% of forest properties set aside as legal reserve. Under the PEC, it would require a prior decision by Congress.

s7849073.oQueMuda: Political parties would become public-law legal entities.
s7849073.porQueImporta: Today parties are private legal entities with autonomy to organize themselves, although they receive public money. Under the PEC, they would be public legal entities.

s7852681.titulo: Changes how presidential vetoes are voted on
s7852681.oQueMuda: Vetoes would be voted on separately in the Chamber and the Senate, except those on budget laws.
s7852681.porQueImporta: Today presidential vetoes are reviewed in a joint session of Congress. Under the PEC, they would be voted separately in each house, except for budget laws.

s7853132.oQueMuda: Senators, deputies and council members would not be reimbursed for housing or relocation.
s7853132.porQueImporta: Today deputies and senators who do not use official housing receive a housing allowance. Under the PEC, no lawmaker would be reimbursed for housing or moving.

s7853575.titulo: Bans new pension tax breaks while the spending cap applies
s7853575.oQueMuda: The federal government could not create or expand pension exemptions and benefits while the fiscal regime is in force.
s7853575.quemAfeta: Sectors with exemptions and social security.
s7853575.porQueImporta: This 2019 PEC would have banned the federal government from creating or expanding social security contribution exemptions while the spending cap was in force; the cap was replaced in 2023.

s7854831.titulo: Changes the dates of executive elections
s7854831.oQueMuda: Elections for president, governor and mayor would be held in late November and early December.
s7854831.porQueImporta: Today elections are held in October, and inauguration is on January 1 (for president and governors, from 2027, on January 5 and 6). Under the PEC, executive elections would be held in late November and early December.

s7862583.titulo: Lets legislators use office allowance savings for social amendments
s7862583.oQueMuda: Legislators could send whatever they don't spend from their office allowance to social policies.
s7862583.porQueImporta: Today unspent office allowance money returns to the Chamber's or Senate's treasury. Under the PEC, lawmakers could direct it to social policies.

s7869752.titulo: Lets Brazilians abroad vote for senator and governor
s7869752.oQueMuda: Brazilians living abroad would have special districts to vote in majority-vote elections.
s7869752.porQueImporta: Today Brazilians living abroad only vote for president. Under the PEC, they would have special constituencies to also vote for senator and governor.

s7876385.titulo: Bans budget freezes at federal universities
s7876385.oQueMuda: Federal universities and institutes could not have funds frozen.
s7876385.porQueImporta: Today the budget of federal universities and institutes can be frozen by the government. Under the PEC, this would be banned.

s7969278.titulo: Defines how old Fundef court payments are used
s7969278.oQueMuda: Court-ordered payments from the old Fundef education fund would go to basic education, with part used to pay teachers.
s7969278.porQueImporta: The federal government was ordered to pay states and municipalities amounts it failed to transfer to the former Fundef. Under the PEC, this money would have to go to basic education, with part for teachers.

s8104778.titulo: Changes management of the Center-West fund
s8104778.oQueMuda: Sudeco could authorize banks to manage the Center-West financing fund.
s8104778.porQueImporta: Today the Center-West financing fund is operated by Banco do Brasil. Under the PEC, Sudeco could authorize other banks to operate it.

s8143032.titulo: Requires a woman on every executive ticket
s8143032.oQueMuda: Tickets for president and governor would have to include at least one woman.
s8143032.porQueImporta: Today tickets for president and governor can be made up only of men. Under the PEC, they would have to include at least one woman.

s8199287.titulo: Creates guarantees for police, firefighters and their families
s8199287.oQueMuda: Police and firefighters would be entitled to health care, life insurance and support for relatives.
s8199287.porQueImporta: Today benefits such as life insurance and health care for police and firefighters vary by state law. Under the PEC, they would be guaranteed in the Constitution, including support for relatives.

s8266998.titulo: Makes Ibama and ICMBio permanent institutions
s8266998.oQueMuda: The environmental agencies Ibama and ICMBio would become permanent state institutions.
s8266998.porQueImporta: Today Ibama and ICMBio are agencies created by law and can be abolished or merged by law. Under the PEC, they would be permanent institutions in the Constitution.
